**Replaced** (19 more, 144 in all; `game/src/battle/battle_calc.cpp`, `game/include/p3fes/game/battle_calc.h`; finished from the
unreviewed WIP `619c955`, names as `symbols/functions.json` gives them after IDA master update #3): the formulas
`datCalcDamage 0x303130` (10,304 B; eight arguments, `$t0..$t3` = result, kind, flags, hp_or_sp), `datCalcCheckHit 0x309490`
(4,784 B), `datCalcGetAffinity 0x306E80` (4,664 B), `datCalcGetAffinityChecked 0x30B4B0` (232 B); the helpers
`datCalcGetSkillElement 0x3082F0` (244 B), `sub_3086C0` (44 B), `sub_308860` (72 B), `sub_308A50` (48 B),
`datCalcGetSkillSlotCount 0x308BA0` (12 B), `datCalcGetSkillList 0x308BB0` (172 B), `sub_308930` (276 B),
`datCalcGetHeldWeaponType 0x308C60` (612 B), `sub_308ED0` (176 B), `sub_308F80` (76 B), `sub_308FD0` (164 B), `sub_3093A0` (236 B),
`datCalcGetWeaponParam 0x309080` (452 B), `datCalcGetArmorParam 0x309250` (336 B), `datCalcIsLowHp 0x30B5E0` (84 B). Proposed names
for the `sub_*` rows are in the header. `datCalcRand`, `datScriptCalc` (and its 51 formula functions), `datCalcGetEffectMultiplier`,
`datCalcHasSkill`, the equipment/condition readers and the K_Assert stub stay recompiled `guest::call`s.

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) `datScriptGetValue 0x30FDF0` returns `$f20` unchanged on its out-of-range path, so the callee of
`datScriptCalc` can see the caller's `$f20..$f23`: both formulas put their working multipliers there around the call (saved and
restored) and leave every constant / product in `$f0` where the compiled code does. (2) `datCalcCheckHit`'s row skills come from the
jump table `0x7B9080`, which maps rows 5 and 6 to the skill pairs 521/520 and 519/518 (not in id order); 21_battle.md calls 508..527 /
563 / 564 "hit rate up", but all of them, like the evade skills 544..546, are read on the *target* (`$a1`). (3) `datCalcDamage` with an
hp_or_sp other than 1/2 (K_Assert 1763) takes its formula from a frame slot that is never written on that path and its base / bonus from
the caller's `$s6` / `$s5`; the hand version reads the same guest bytes and registers. (4) The datScriptCalc calls of `datCalcDamage`
pass the formula index left in `$a0` by the kind comparison (1 or 2 for the damage kinds, 1 or 3 for recovery). (5) `datGetFlag(4889)`
is called and its result ignored in four places of the damage chain; the calls stay (cycles, check points).

**Cycle-model notes.** No loops: every multiplier test is its own block, so the hand versions follow the generated block costs one by
one (e.g. the evade tiers 7/6/6 then 4/4/2, a case that falls through to the join costs 1-3 cycles less than one that jumps). Both
formulas end in one shared epilogue block (17 / 18 cycles) charged on every return path. The equipment groups test the cached enemy
flag (2 cycles) for their first item and reload it (4) for the others.

**Changed in the WIP.** Renamed to the master's names (9 functions, 3 callees). `datCalcGetEffectLevel` is called directly (it is
hand-written) instead of through its shim. `sx8` became unused and went. The pair test now logs the arguments of a failing pair, gives
the party members' unit-like headers (`record + 4`, read by `datCalcGetLevel` through `sub_16CC00`) valid ids -- random ones sent the
recompiled `datCalcGetMaxHp` (`datCalcIsLowHp`) into unmapped memory -- and drops an unused constant. The WIP's 17 bodies themselves
needed no change; `datCalcCheckHit` / `datCalcDamage`, declared but not written in the WIP, are new.

## Phase 5: RenderWare sky-driver leaves -- slice render_rw (2026-10-20)

**What.** 38 functions (4,704 bytes) from `docs/ANALYSIS/queue_rendering.txt` "Full queue" (class a, no `callsB`, depth 0-2, outside
the first two slices) in `game/src/render/rw_leaves.cpp` / `game/include/p3fes/game/rw_leaves.h`: the VU0 matrix product
`sub_4C2F30`, the inverses `sub_4C32A0` / `sub_4C2860`, the normalise `sub_4C6970`, the frustum tests `sub_4C9DF0` / `sub_4A3F70`
and the morph sphere `sub_491100` (c7), the frustum sector walk `sub_49C330` (callback, c7), the render-state getter `sub_4D81B0`
(c6), the texture-cache release `sub_4F1540` (c5), the transfer-size table `sub_4DB200`, `sub_4D6B60`, `sub_4CC0A0`, the error slot
`sub_4C1C50` / `sub_4C1D10`, the list / registry / material-list / PS2All / Im3D accessors and callbacks, `sceGsGetGParam`,
`sceDmaGetChan`, `RpPDSGetPipe`, `sub_468720`. All keep their functions.json names (roles in brackets in the header, no community
names).

**Register contract.** Every register the original writes is left with the original's final value: GPRs including `$at` and the
`$t` registers, HI/LO of the two MULTs, FPRs / ACC / FCR31 (C and the D / I flags of DIV.S / SQRT.S) of the float leaves, the whole
VU0 state of the matrix product (only the xyz lanes are computed; the w lanes of vf9..vf12 are stored with the rows as VU0 held
them). Functions that call out (`sub_4F1540` release callback, `sub_49C330` sector callback, `sub_4C32A0` -> `sub_4C2860`,
`sub_4F1F80` -> memset, `RpPDSGetPipe` -> `sub_46AD20`) build the original frame with its spills (`kwln::Frame`), hold the original
s-registers across the call and set `$ra` to the original link. `sub_4C2860` routes the determinant through frame + 12 (its zero test is
a word test: only +0.0 counts as singular), `sub_468720` keeps its two name cursors in the frame (`guest::StackFrame`).

**Cycle-model notes.** `sub_4C1C50`'s two error-code paths share a tail reached by a backward `b` (a back-edge check on that path
only). `sub_4F1F80`: the call block (6) covers the return-point `b` / `li v0, 1`. `sub_4D81B0` / `sub_4DB200`: compare chains at 3
cycles per further test (2 for format 1, compared against `$t1` without a `li`), taken targets 2 (1 for the first); a miss of the
format chain ends in a `movz` (format 0 -> 2). `sub_4F1540`: every jump back into the shared tail and into the slot test is a back-edge
check, the trims' exits that jump forward are not. `sub_49C330` loop end: 3 + 2 + check + 2 + epilogue 8.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_rw.cpp`, 12 cases, 12,527 pairs): per pair every GPR (both halves), HI/LO, all FPRs, ACC,
FCR31, the whole VU0 state (FPRs and VU0 start random), the arena, the gp window `[gp-20800, gp-16800)`, the RW globals / texture-cache
/ Im3D header / PDS registry regions a function touches, the whole stack window (dead and live), cycles and check points. Callbacks are
emitted functions through the dispatch table, two of them non-leaf (`RpPDSGetPipe`, `sub_4C32A0`). Rule checks: exact matrix product,
orthonormal inverse = transpose, (3, 0, 4) normalised, MSB, the transfer-size table, alpha = max(r, g, b), the error slot keeps the first
error, the interleaved bump-map name, libdma's channel table = the ten DMAC channel bases. A planted wrong FPR in `sub_4C9DF0` was
caught. Slice **1,354,052 assertions**; `p3fes_game_tests` **151 cases / 21,591,771 assertions** on MSVC 19.44 Release
(`build/render_rw-msvc`) and clang-cl 22.1.0 Debug (`build/render_rw-clang`).

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1`, `build/render_rw-gate` MSVC Release + VU1 AOT, emitted with `--replace`: 539 replaced; ctest on
both compilers with `p3fes_recomp_emit_subset` skipped by design): dorm frame **EE0EB5DA…795D85**, M1 **E3A93615…B672**, battle
**CFAA5A61…CF606**, each **0 differing bytes / 0 runs**; `GATE: PASSED`.

**Not taken.** The resource-heap functions `sub_4C6D60` / `sub_4C6E60` / `sub_4C6F30` (an allocator; heap users are out of scope),
the depth-1 callers that allocate (`sub_4C1E70`, `sub_4CBF20`, `sub_4F3150`, `sub_4D0FD0`), the other callback walkers

## Phase 5: the game-side draw layer -- camera passes and Im2D builders (2026-10-20)

**Slice `render_game`** (`game/src/render/draw_layer.cpp`, `game/include/p3fes/game/draw_layer.h`, `tests/game/test_render_game.cpp`,
`symbols/deltas/render_game.sym`; queue `docs/ANALYSIS/queue_rendering.txt` "game-side draw layer", class `a` without `callsB`).
28 functions, 15,808 bytes of MIPS:

* camera passes (kwln draw tasks, 22_rendering.md section 1): `kwlnRootUpdate2DDrawEndTask 0x198B20`, `kwlnRootUpdate3DOn2DZClearTask` / `kwlnRootUpdate3DOn2DDrawBeginTask` /
  `kwlnRootUpdate3DOn2DDrawEndTask` (3D on 2D Zclear / Draw Begin / Draw End), `kwlnRootUpdateEtcDrawBeginTask` (etc Draw Begin), `kwlnRootUpdateDrawEndTask 0x198FD0`,
  `K_SPipe_Update3DDrwBeginTask` / `K_SPipe_Update3DDrwEndTask` (3D Draw Begin / End), `kwlnRootUpdateShadowNodeCameraTask` (Shadow Node Camera), `btlDrawMessagePass` (battle message pass, fog saved /
  off / restored around `sub_27A3B0`), `btlUpdateDraw3DTask`, `H_MoonIcon_UpdateTask` (HUD moon icon task);
* Im2D builders (section 6): `H_Cursor_UpdateDrawTask 0x100230`, `sub_422670` (the same quad with a 16-byte header), the screen fades
  `H_Fade_DrawBlue` / `H_Fade_DrawWhite` / `H_Fade_DrawColour` (one state machine and body, three colour variants), `H_MoonIcon_Draw` (the moon quad: inlined
  cosf/sinf polynomials, RwMatrixRotateOneMinusCosineSine, RwV3dTransformPoints), `frFontRasterDrawGlyph 0x3B38F0`, `sub_126710`,
  `drawIm2DIndexedTriList`, `sub_269F50`, `btlDrawTexturedQuad`, `drawGradientQuad`, and the debug print `dbgPrintDrawScreen` (40 x 53 grid), `dbgPrintDrawStrings` (string list),
  `dbgPrintDrawWindow` (window), `dbgDrawRect` (rectangle).

RenderWare stays recompiled: direct calls (`RwCameraBeginUpdate` / `EndUpdate` / `Clear`, the matrix functions) and the device
pointers `0x960090` (RwRenderStateSet) .. `0x9600A4` are called exactly where the original called them.

**Register / stack model.** These frames are live on the stack while RenderWare runs below them, so every function writes its
original prologue spills (`draw::Frame`, `sd`/`sq` and the `$f20..$f25` `swc1` spills) and reloads them in the epilogue, keeps the
s-registers and `$f20..` holding the original's values at every call, sets `$ra` to the original link value, and leaves every
caller-saved GPR/FPR it writes, HI/LO (the fades' `div`, the debug grid's `mult`) and FCR31 (the `div.s` flags, `c.eq.s` / `c.le.s`)
as the original does at every call, back-edge and return. Vertex arrays stay on the guest stack at the original offsets (their
unwritten words are whatever the previous callee left; RenderWare reads them), and the `ld`/`sd` position copies of `dbgPrintDrawWindow`
are kept per character. Float math goes through `ee/fpu.h` in the compiled operand order (ACC chains via `adda`/`madd`/`msub`).

**Cycle-model notes.** Loops test first and check before every iteration (the 4-vertex loops: 3 or 5 cycles of test, 10..51 of body
depending on how many colour bytes the body converts; the unsigned-convert idiom's `bltz` is never taken on a byte, its 5-cycle
block is charged). Exceptions kept as compiled: `frFontRasterDrawGlyph`'s 4 x 8-byte table copy and 32-byte clear are do-while loops
(check after each iteration but the last), `dbgPrintDrawStrings`'s node walk checks at the jump back, and the moon's degree wrap checks once
per 360-step pass. `drawGradientQuad` is straight-line: per vertex 32 cycles of colour conversion, then 8 (14 for the last, with the call).

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_game.cpp`, 12 cases, 5,528,895 assertions on both compilers). Stricter than
`pair_harness.h`: each pair compares the whole 32 MiB main RAM (dead stack included), all 128-bit GPRs, FPRs, ACC, FCR31, HI/LO,
cycles and check points at the end, and a trace of every check point (every callee entry and back-edge: cycles, all GPRs and FPRs).
RenderWare's device pointers and the camera's begin/end point at recompiled stand-ins (`sub_1F1C50`, a non-leaf that spills `$ra` and

## Phase 5: BF script COMM handlers, indices 0-250 (slice script_comm_a, 2026-10-20)

**What.** 56 pure handlers of `sScrCommandTable 0x7B92B0` (502 x {fn, argc}; dedupe by address, no handler of 0-250 recurs above
250) in `game/src/script/comm_a.cpp` / `comm_a.h`, each named by its IDA name (all `sub_*`) with its index and argc in the comment:
the party list `0x83A6E0` (add / clear / get / remove + compaction), the money word `0x83A6DC` (get, add clamped at 9,999,999,
subtract floored at 0; K_Assert line 1674 on a negative result), the calendar getters, the member / social-stat getters [192..205],
the persona / social-link checks and best-candidate scans [124], [186], [187], [218..220], the social context words [224], [225],
the dungeon floor record [226..232], the event config bytes [189..191], [206], the return stubs [48], [50], [145], [147], and the
field helpers [14], [121], [127], [135], [136], [138], [215]. None has a caller besides the table (no jal/data reference in the ELF).

**Fidelity model.** A `Frame` helper performs the original prologue/epilogue (`sd ra` / `sq sN` spills included), every call sets `$ra`
to the original link (`rt::jal` at the call's address) and the argument registers as 64-bit values, and `keep` puts the values the
original holds in `$sN` across calls into those registers -- so callees that spill (`sub_103C30`, the 0x16C getters) write the same
bytes, and the pair test compares the whole dead stack. Scratch registers after the last call are not reproduced (CodeFunc_Comm reads
`$v0` alone). `sub_35F210` copies its six candidate ids from `.rodata 0x69D518` into the guest frame (+80) exactly as the original
loop does (3 x 9 cycles with the back-edge check); `sub_35F360` copies four from `$gp-25232` (+88). Loops whose test block comes first
(`sub_16EA80`, `sub_16ECD0` and its inner shift loop, `sub_1C3B00`, the candidate scans) charge the test, then check, then the body.

**Skipped in 0-250** (reasons in the `comm_a.cpp` header): printf (`PUT`, `sub_35B0D0`, `SCR_RUN`, `sub_3A2B30`, `sub_35F170`,
`sub_1C37C0`, `sub_1C3820`, `sub_3604A0`); the heap / task creation (`SCR_KILL`, `sub_1C25B0`, `sub_1C2010`, `sub_1C2160`,
`sub_1C2340`, `sub_424310`, `sub_424370`, `sub_35F7A0`, `sub_1C2480`, `sub_1C3AD0`, `btlScrCmd_CALL_BATTLE`, `sub_27D730`); file
loading `sub_1C2580`; sound `sub_350200`; message windows (`scrCommand_MSG`, `sub_3A2900/2970/2660/28A0/2260/2440/2C10`,
`sub_35F5B0`, `sub_35F880`, `sub_35F680`, `sub_35F730`, `sub_35FDB0`); rendering / models / panels (`sub_1C2900`, `sub_1C2B80`,
`sub_3971A0`, `sub_3973E0`, `sub_40D410/490/540`, `sub_38D980`, `sub_3BD230`, `sub_1C2550`); and the ~110 battle-AI handlers
(0x2C7300-0x2CE090, 0x2D13C0) that dispatch through the AI tables `0x6971B0` / `0x6975E0` with `jalr` -- one template, left for a
pass with real AI action objects.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_script_comm_a.cpp`, 3 cases): 64 randomised pairs per handler (3,584) plus the documented rules (money
clamp / floor, party add / remove / slot, the floor classes, the event config bytes and wait, the constant returns, the social words)
and the table check (index -> fn / argc for 18 rows, count 502). Each pair compares v0, callee-saved GPRs, `$sp`/`$ra`, cycles, check
points, the arena, the live and the **dead** stack, low RAM and the band `[0x680000, 0x9E0000)`; the save-data block
`0x834000-0x840000` is random bytes. Two harness lessons: `clndIsDateInRange` walks month by month, so out-of-range months run for
minutes (arguments stay valid dates); `sub_174710` writes through `0x836BAC + 52 * index` for the s16 index at `0x836BA8`, so the band
is wide enough for any index and the arena is restored between the two runs. A cycle mutation in four deep paths (candidate scan,
floor slot loop, persona check, clamp) was caught. Slice: **73,553 assertions**; `p3fes_game_tests` **142 cases / 20,311,272
assertions** on MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/script_comm_a-msvc`) and on clang-cl 22.1.0 Debug (`build/script_comm_a-clang`).

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1`, `build/script_comm_a-gate`, 557 replaced): dorm `EE0EB5DA...795D85`, M1 `E3A93615...B672`,

**Replaced** (41 more, 542 in all, 20,336 bytes of MIPS; `game/src/battle/battle_rest.cpp`, `game/include/p3fes/game/battle_rest.h`;
names as `symbols/functions.json` gives them, proposed names for the `sub_*` rows in the header, no delta). The 18 functions the
battle_calc wave left in `[0x302000, 0x30B600)`: the buff-slot turn work `sub_302380` [datCalcApplyEffectMask] (2,248 B),
`sub_302C50` [ClearMaskedEffects] (236 B), `sub_302D40` [TickEffectTurns] (524 B), `sub_302F50` [FindExpiredEffect] (480 B); the
status roll `sub_305970` [datCalcRollStatus] (1,708 B) and its users `sub_306020` (1,256 B) / `sub_306510` (252 B); the skill
wrappers around datCalcDamage `sub_306610` [ApplySkill] (700 B), `sub_3068D0` [GetSkillEffectMask] (740 B), `sub_306BC0`
[SkillResults] (456 B, seven arguments); `sub_306D90` [DecodeAffinity] (232 B); the cost `sub_3083F0` (712 B) / `sub_3086F0` (368 B);
`sub_308A80` [PickMixRaidSkill] (284 B); the action rolls `sub_30A740` [RollInstantKill] (1,984 B), `sub_30AF00` / `sub_30B130`
[knock-down] (556 / 212 B), `sub_30B210` [RollFollowUp] (672 B). The queue rows still open: `datGetSkillName` / `datGetArcanaName`
(100 B each), `sub_30C220` (128 B), `sub_30C3A0` (156 B), `datCalcRestorePartyAll` (80 B) + `sub_30C490` (120 B). Their band
neighbours: `sub_30B640` [GetCounterSkill] (860 B), `sub_30B9A0` [GetHitCount] (408 B), `sub_30BC20` (44 B), `sub_30BC50` [enemy exp]
(400 B), `sub_30BDE0` [enemy drop] (736 B), `sub_30C0C0` (344 B), `sub_30C2A0` [RollEscape] (248 B); and the rest of the
datUnit/datCalc/datScript band without heap hooks: `datUnitEcAddEnemy` (284 B), `sub_2FFB00` (192 B), `sub_3005A0` (64 B),
`sub_300700` (80 B), `sub_300870` (304 B; called by datCalcDamage / GetAffinity / CheckHit), `sub_300E90` (200 B), `sub_301CA0`
[CheckEffectMask] (1,752 B, 12 callers), the datScript COMM handlers `sub_30FDC0` / `sub_3111C0` / `sub_3112E0` (40 / 40 / 36 B).

**Register discipline.** Most of these run inside the battle's action and turn state functions, so every non-leaf body keeps the
original frame (the prologue spills written to the guest stack at the original offsets, reloaded by the epilogue), the original
`$s` registers at every call, `$ra` = the original link (`jal` through the callee's generated entry point, also for the hand-written
callees of other slices) and only the argument registers the original set. The float chains (`sub_305970`, `sub_30A740`,
`sub_30BC50`, `sub_30BDE0`) run on the guest `$f0/$f1/$f20` with the recompiler's FPU primitives, so datScriptCalc's callee sees the
original `$f20` and FCR31 matches. `$v0` at the return is the original's also for the void functions (`sub_302380` leaves the last
level or flag word it computed). The pair tests compare the dead stack (8 KiB) as well; the other caller-saved GPRs are counted, not
required.

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) `sub_305970`'s element-boost table 0x7B8F70 is not in id order: element 8 -> skill 599, 9 -> 600,
10..15 -> 592..597, plus 598 for every element. (2) `sub_306020` maps weapon effects 49..66 to status skills 160..177 and 170..172 to
178..180 through a compare chain; 59/60/61 reuse the registers holding 170/171/172. (3) The status-skill rolls K_Assert (line 3077)
when the hit rate +25 is *below* 100; +25 >= 100 is a sure hit. (4) `sub_30A740` reads the **attacker's** condition (`$s4`), not the
target's. (5) `sub_308A80`'s loop bound is `slt at, i, t1` -- the slot count register, not an immediate 9 (caught by the pair test).
(6) The inlined datCalcGetSkillElement costs differ per caller (the flags0 block is 11 cycles in `sub_30A740` / `sub_30B640` but 5 in
`sub_30AF00`, which reuses the record offset; `sub_30B640`'s enemy test is 3, not 4). (7) `sub_3083F0` keeps HI/LO of its
`mult`/`div`. (8) effMiscRand's state 0x957BF0 is zero in the image and a zero state rolls 0 forever: the tests randomise it.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_battle_rest.cpp`, 7 cases, 100,350 pairs; the eight battle `.TBL` files loaded as btlTableLoad lays
them out, random items / party / flag words / RNG state / persona stock): each pair compares `$v0`, the callee-saved GPRs, all 32 FPRs,
FCR31, HI/LO, cycles, check points, the arena, the live and the dead stack and the data window `[0x7C0000, 0x9B0000)`. Slice:

## Phase 5: rendering, first slice -- the Im2D submission path (render_im2d, 2026-10-20)

**What.** The 18 functions of `docs/ANALYSIS/queue_rendering.txt` "Recommended first slice" (22_rendering.md §6, §8.1), all
`sub_*` in functions.json (verified names from `symbols/deltas/rendering.sym` in brackets in `game/include/p3fes/game/render_im2d.h`):
the device entry points `SkyIm2DRenderLine` 88 B, `SkyIm2DRenderTriangle` 96 B, `SkyIm2DRenderPrimitive`
[SkyIm2DRenderPrimitive] 116 B, `SkyIm2DRenderIndexedPrimitive` 112 B; the builders `addCopyVU1Line` 436 B,
`addCopyVU1Triangle` 544 B, `addCopyVU1PrimLineList` / `addCopyVU1PrimPolyLine` / `addCopyVU1PrimTriList` / `addCopyVU1PrimTriStrip` / `addCopyVU1PrimTriFan`
[addCopyVU1Prim{LineList,PolyLine,TriList,TriStrip,TriFan}] 652-800 B, `addCopyVU1IndPrimLineList` / `addCopyVU1IndPrimPolyLine` / `addCopyVU1IndPrimTriList` / `addCopyVU1IndPrimTriStrip` /
`addCopyVU1IndPrimTriFan` [addCopyVU1IndPrim*] 688-864 B; `open2DVU1Pkt` 420 B and `closeAndDispatchVU1Packet` 72 B.
`_rwDMAOpenVIFPkt 0x4D59D0` (D8 fromSPR, D_STAT, D_PCR, BC0F) and the rest of the DMA packet layer stay recompiled; open2DVU1Pkt
calls it directly with the original's `$v0/$v1/$a0/$a1`, `$ra` link and 48-byte frame.

**Shape.** The ten prim-array builders are one batcher (`build_packets`): per packet at most `$gp-16872` lines / `$gp-16868`
triangles (39 in both snapshots) behind one descriptor->open `jalr` (through `rt::lookup_func`, `$a0..$t1` as the original passes
them), batches of at most 16 primitives (cnt + ITOP/STCYCL, STMASK + UNPACK V4-32 header, the primitives' 64-byte `RwIm2DVertex`
records, MSCALF / MSCNT trailer), closeAndDispatch; each builder supplies a `next_prim` walk (array pointer, u16 index pointer, the
strip's `s ^= 3` winding, the fan's hub) and its block costs as data. This is where a host fast path for UI quads plugs in.

**Harness (tests/game/pair_harness.h, this slice's exclusive edit).** Opt-in hardware-observing pairs: `HwCheck` / `run_pair_hw`
compare the bus access log (`ScriptedBus`, RecordingBus-compatible), serve scripted register reads (D8_CHCR idle/busy, D_STAT polls
for the BC0F wait), compare/restore the scratchpad and caller-chosen guest ranges (RW globals, packet templates, DMA buffer), all
GPRs in 128 bits on request, HI/LO and SA, the register file at every check point and the dead stack; `gpr_in` sets `$t0..`
arguments. Documented in game/README.md "Pair tests that observe the hardware". Existing tests unchanged.

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) The packet templates at 0x965870 and 0x965880 hold the same qword in both snapshots, so the tests
randomise the templates (a swap would otherwise pass). (2) A polyline of 0 vertices is 0xFFFFFFFF lines (`addiu -1`, unsigned
compares), and a strip/fan whose `$a3` is >= 3 as a 64-bit value but 0/1 in its low word wraps the same way: never called so, not
tested. (3) The indexed fan reads index 0 even when it draws nothing. (4) open2DVU1Pkt patches PRIM = (render flags | gs_prim) & 0x7FF
into the GIF tag template itself (0x9658A4), and bit 4 of the 64-bit render flags (TME) picks 0x9659F0 over 0x9659E0.
(5) Registers: all 18 are register-faithful at every check point, call and return, and write the original prologue spills.
A first version reproduced only `$v0`, `$sp`, `$ra` and the callee-saved registers (no caller can *read* the others) and passed
every pair test, but the gate failed in 22 / 17 / 35 stack bytes (dorm / M1 / battle; frames identical): the kernel saves the whole
register file at `$sp - 0x280` on a preempting check point or a switching syscall (`KernelOptions::context_frames`, BIOS
0x80003680), so a builder's leftover `$t2` (the batch trailer quadword) reached guest memory (`--watch-write 0x1FFFA70` showed the
128-bit store of `$t2`'s value from host code). The builders' register allocation is now data (`Alloc` per builder: which register
holds the count, the trailer, the constants; per-builder header / copy finals listed from the instructions), and the harness gained
`compare_checkpoint_regs` / `compare_dead_stack`, which a one-register mutation trips at once.

**Cycle-model notes.** Two "back-edges" are forward in source terms: open2DVU1Pkt's resident-program path (`qwc - 1`, check point,
jump back into the call block) and every builder's exit through its zero-count test (clear the count, check point, test again:
2 + check + 2 + exit). Copy-loop blocks per primitive: 53/54/77/82/78 (prim) and 59/59/86/91/83 (indexed); LineList, TriList, the
indexed line/polyline, strip and fan fall through an extra 1-cycle block after the copy loop, the others do not; exits 9/10/11.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_im2d.cpp`, 8 cases, ~6,100 hardware-observing pairs; every pair compares the Outcome, all
GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, the register file at every check point, the dead stack, the bus log, the scratchpad, the RW globals
`[0x7CDDC0, 0x7CEB40)`, the templates `[0x965850, 0x965A40)` and a DMA-buffer window): closeAndDispatch 300, open2DVU1Pkt 800 (460
program calls / 340 resident, 580 runs with a fromSPR copy, 294 with the D8 busy wait), Line / Triangle 400, the five prim builders
and the five indexed builders 300 each (counts 0-120 crossing the 16-primitive batch and the 39-primitive packet, limits 0/1/5/16/17/39,
world packet states none / VIF open / VIF + cnt / GIF open, both scratchpad halves nearly full), the four entry points 1,200 (prim
0/6/7/negative/64-bit), the documented packet layout against a host model 120 (strip winding, fan hub, indexed variants, batch
headers, trailers, tail), and a 160-call UI frame (sprite / glyph quads, a glyph run, a fade, a window frame) on the battle and dorm
snapshots' RW state. Slice: **460,841 assertions** on both compilers; `p3fes_game_tests` **147 cases / 20,698,560 assertions** on
MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/render_im2d-msvc`) and clang-cl 22.1.0 Debug (`build/render_im2d-clang`). Mutations checked: a wrong
copy-loop tail cycle, the TME head choice, one register of closeAndDispatch, one constant register and one copy temporary all fail.

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build/render_im2d-gate -ClangTree build/render_im2d-clang -Jobs 3`, base `a5e75de`, 519
replaced): ctest 16 tests on both compilers, none failed (`p3fes_recomp_emit_subset` skips by design), dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85` 0 bytes, M1
`E3A93615…B672` 0 bytes, battle `CFAA5A61…F606` 0 bytes: **GATE: PASSED**.

`sub_1D8D60`); footstep / effect / virtual pad (`sub_1D9FD0`, `sub_1DA000`, `sub_1DD5E0`, `sub_1DD5F0`, `sub_1E13C0`, `sub_1E1820`)
and the NPC-placement lists (`sub_1E1840`, `sub_1E2810`, `sub_1E29E0`). Not taken: the event task itself (`K_FldEvent_UpdateFldEventTask`, io /
printf / task creation), the COMM handlers of 0x1C2000-0x1C6000 (script slices), rows with heap / io / printf / task / rw flags,
the 44-byte `jalr` destroy callbacks (RwFree through `0x96017C`), render rows.

**Registers and cycles.** Every function is register-faithful at every check point, call and return: the non-leaf ones write their
prologue spills on the guest stack, keep the original `$s0..$s2`, call through the generated entry with `$ra` = the original link,
and every scratch GPR (the walks' temporaries in their original registers, the compare chains' last constants -- `sub_1D11B0` hands
`sub_316E00` the chain's leftover `$a1`, so kind 4 -> 3 and kind 3 -> 4), `$f0`/`$f1`/`$f12`, FCR31.C and HI/LO (`div` in
`sub_1C65E0`, `divu` in `sub_1D38A0`) holds the original's value. Blocks with a `jal` are charged whole before the call; every loop
tests first (back-edge after the test block; `sub_1C0110`'s inlined 12-byte clear is the one do-while).

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_field_hi.cpp`, 12 cases, 45,154 assertions on both compilers): every pair compares the whole
register file (GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, SA, FPRs, ACC, FCR31) and the cycle count at every check point and at the return, guest
memory `[0x600000, 0xA00000)`, the arena and the stack (dead stack included), bus / syscall / trap counts. Callees left out of the
test build on purpose (`sub_1A9400`, `sub_1A91B0`, `sub_316E00`, `sub_316F70`, `sub_3174E0`, `sub_1D1640`, `sub_1A60D0`,
`sub_3B2CB0`: deep trees) stop the run through `rt::missing_function`; the hooks snapshot registers and memory at that call, so
both bodies must reach the same callee with the same state (sparse live units put the first call on varying indices). Documented
rules checked on the host: the 11 majors + 8 fields of the pad-script rule, 2.0 / 1.0 by floor kind, the Reaper `limit - frames/30`
floor at 0, the level-gap table walk, the list lookups, the kind -> model argument map. A one-register mutation (`$a3` in the
animation walks) fails 286 assertions. `p3fes_game_tests`: 203 cases / 31,438,014 assertions on MSVC 14.44 Release
(`build/field_hi-gate`) and clang-cl 19.1.5 Debug (`build/field_hi-clang`).

## Phase 5: the battle task / state machine layer -- battle_task (2026-10-20)

Slice `battle_task` (base `a504c1f`, 742 replaced -> 821): **79 functions** of `0x27C000-0x2A0000` in
`game/src/battle/battle_task.cpp` / `game/include/p3fes/game/battle_task.h` (proposed names for the `sub_*` rows in
brackets in the header; the btlAction state names come from the name column of `sBtlActionTbl 0x693410`).

**What.** The battle's entry `btlStart 0x27D1D0` (root kwln task "battle" + the three draw children, the panel task tree,
the 52-byte setup block -> btlMain INIT, or TEST / MC without one), the root task's callbacks `btlUpdateTask` (the frame's
battle drivers in their order while gBtl+12 bit 0 is set, else the teardown `sub_27CE10`) and `btlDestroyTask`; the btlMain
states of the 20-row table 0x693760 (29 bodies: NON, INIT, SCENE_SET, START, ACTION -- the result block gBtl+3036 with the
survivors, counts, the round average through the original `div`, and the outcome switch --, REVIVAL_MES, ENEMY DEAD, WIN
(the pad-skippable victory pose), CONDITION, LOSE, FADE_OUT, END update, RESULT, EXIT, TEST, MC) and `btlMainSetStateNon`;
the btlAction states (STANDBY, START HOME, CHANGE FORMATION, ANALYZE, MOVE TARGET / MOVE HOME, REINFORCE, ASSIST, EVENT,
ENDURE, PERSONA, PACKET, END init, END HOME, EXIT init, TEST, and the 15 empty `jr ra` slots), `btlActionSetStateWithDelay`;
the helpers: the packet-queue counters `sub_27E410` / `sub_27E470` / `sub_27E4D0` (queue heads gBtl+372+8q, tails +368+8q,
packet +124 next / +128 previous -- so `sub_27E4D0`'s walk along +128 visits only the heads, obs), the revival check
`sub_27D560`, the turn-order readers / reset `sub_29AD20 ... sub_29B0C0`.

**Skipped.** `btlCreate` (RwHeapMalloc through the device pointer 0x960178), `btlActionCreate` (heap), `btlActionUpdateAll`
(RwFree), `btlTableLoad*` (file loading), the draw-task bodies `btlUpdateDraw3DFrontTask` / `btlUpdateDraw2DTask` (rendering), and the big state
bodies (UNIT_CREATE / UNIT_LOAD / REVIVAL / CONDITION / END inits, WIN init, the ATTACK / SKILL / ESCAPE / COMMAND / TARGET
updates, 0.4-16 KB each) for a dedicated pass.

**Registers / cycle model.** Every function is register-faithful at each check point, call and return: `Frame` writes the
prologue spills (`sd ra`, `sq s0..s2`) and reloads them; every register the original writes ($at from the `slt`s of the
WIN / LOSE waits, $v0/$v1/$a0..$a3/$t0/$t1, $s0..$s2, HI/LO of ACTION's `div`) holds the original's value whenever a callee,
a check point or the caller can see it; the indirect calls (EVENT's +1184 callback, the state-table rows of
`btlActionSetStateWithDelay` / `btlMainSetStateNon`) run inside the original frame with $v0 = the target and $v1 = 12 * state.
Blocks are charged where they start, before their calls (the test-first loops of the packet counters and the order search
check before every iteration, $v1 / $v0 holding the `sltiu` result there).

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_battle_task.cpp`, 2 cases): every function on 400 random battle worlds (gBtl, 6 actions,
5 btlUnits with DatUnits, 0-16 packets in the four queues, both order lists, the btlMain state record, pad words; whole-register
arguments with garbage upper halves) against its `__recomp` body: the whole register file (GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, SA, FPRs,
FCR31) and the cycle count at **every check point** and at the return, or at the missing-function stop when a callee is not
emitted in the test build (snapshotted in the hooks before the unwind), and memory (the world, low RAM, `.data`/`.bss`
0x7C0000-0x840000, 0x950000-0x960000, the stack around $sp, the arena) -- 31,600 pairs, 8,669 ended at a compared stop, 64
functions also return normally (15 always reach a big callee first: btlStart -> btlCreate, the scene / sound / panel / yes-no
window callees); plus the documented rules on the host (queue counts, order slots / units / first / contains, pending
delayed states, the MOVE TARGET kind -> state map with 778 transitions, the LOSE 31-frame wait, 395 ENEMY DEAD passes).

## Phase 5: rendering, second slice -- the PS2All mesh seam (render_mesh, 2026-10-20)

**Scope.** The 21 rows of `docs/ANALYSIS/queue_rendering.txt` "Second slice (section 8.2)", all replaced, none skipped:
`game/src/render/mesh.cpp` + `game/include/p3fes/game/mesh.h`, tests `tests/game/test_render_mesh.cpp`. functions.json
names kept (`sub_*`, `RpMeshPS2AllBridgeCallBack`); roles in brackets in the header. Still recompiled behind direct calls /
the dispatch table: the DMA packet layer (`_rwDMAOpenVIFPkt`, `_rwDMAAddPURef` -> `_rwDMAClosePkt` and the reference flush),
`RxPipelineExecute 0x4F2E70`, `PS2AllNodeInstance 0x49FAA0`, `RwFrameGetLTM 0x4CB2F0`, the bounding sphere `0x4912B0`, the world
light walk `0x499C20`, the resEntry array (re)allocation `0x49E5A0` (RwMalloc/RwFree through the RW memory hooks: only on a
mesh-count change), and every callback (`jalr` through `rt::lookup_func` with the original frame and link).

**Style: register-faithful by construction.** Each body runs on a `Cpu` view of the guest context (one named variable per
GPR, 64-bit writes keep bits 64..127; LQ/MMI write 128; FPU / VU0 macro / HI-LO / DI-EI-MFC0 through the runtime's own
instruction semantics; prologue spills and epilogue reloads on the guest stack), structured control flow with the recompiled
body's block costs, and named guest offsets (`mesh::pd` = the 72-byte PipeData record PS2AllNodeBody keeps at sp+272).
Compared with render_im2d's data-plus-allocation approach this is closer to the instructions, but it is exact at every check
point, call and return without per-function register lists, and the gate passed on the first run.

**Draw data for a future VU1-bypass renderer.** `mesh::set_draw_observer` installs host callbacks (default none):
`ObjectSetup` (object matrix, light block and its quadwords, from openVU1SetupPktNew), `SkinPalette` (the palette and bone count,
from sub_46EB90 / sub_46B8E0) and `MeshDraw` per bridge (atomic, mesh, material, texture/raster, TEX0 after the cache placement,
TEX1/CLAMP/TEST shadows, the GIF tag with PRIM, transType / prim / VU1 code index, the program and whether it was uploaded, the
colour and surface quadwords, the resEntry, its DMA data address and the VIF OFFSET). A test runs the node with the observer
installed and checks the records against the documented rules; pairs stay equal with it on.

**Corrections to 22_rendering.md section 3.2.** The bridge's UNPACK targets are GIF tag -> VU1 0x3FA, material colour 0x3FB,
surface properties 0x3FC, clip vectors + flags 0x3FD..0x3FF (three qw; the doc has colour at 0x3FC). The material colour is
scaled by $f12 = 1/255 untextured or 0x3B011B50 (~1/507.6) textured, alpha always by 0x3B011B50. The untextured A+D block is two
zero quadwords + DIRECT 2 (TEST only), the textured one DIRECT 4 (TEST, TEX1, CLAMP). The resEntry `call` carries BASE 0 /
OFFSET (material pipeline +20); the use count (+28) increments every bridge and a first use (1) adds it to the reference ring.
Mesh header flags: 1 strip, 2 fan (drawn as a list), 4 line list, 8 polyline, 0x10 points (prim 4). Object identifier = mesh
header serial (+6) | geometry flags & 0x9F << 16 | morph count << 24.

**Cycle-model notes.** Backward jumps of the block layout that are not loops keep their check points (RpAtomicPS2AllPrimTypeTransTypeSetupFunc's shared tail,
the bridge's texture-state tail L_134c and its clip / A+D blocks, RpSkyTexCacheAccessRaster's eleven, sub_46EB90's inlined prim/transType and
instance test, the node's light-header paths). Dead compiled paths reproduced as such: sub_49CAB0's `bltz` halving of a
zero-extended byte, the frustum loop's `beqz` on the constant 6, sub_46B8E0's `bnez` on 4n+1 (always taken: the cnt tag block runs,
then a check point, then the header). _rpSkinMatrixUpdating's identity / 0x4000 loops run until `at == ptr` (a zero node count never happens).

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_mesh.cpp`, 14 cases, 11,223 pairs). Every pair compares all 31 GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO,
SA, every FPR, ACC, FCR31 and the whole VU0 state at the return; the register file and cycle count at every check point; the bus
log (D8 / D_STAT / D_PCR, scripted busy waits); the scratchpad; the whole stack window (dead and live); a 64 KiB world region, the
gp window, RW globals, packet templates, texture cache globals, CLUT words, skin globals and a DMA-buffer window; cycles, check
points, syscalls, traps. FPRs/ACC/VU0 start random. Worlds: random atomics / geometries / mesh headers / frames / world lights /
sector ties / skins and hierarchies / partitions / rasters with sky extensions and cache slots / materials / resEntries / node
private data, the four DMA packet states with nearly full scratchpad halves; callbacks are emitted functions (stock bridge, a
leaf, a non-leaf that spills $ra; the real sub_4A09D0 as the node's set-up callback). Per function: the five leaves 400 each;
RpAtomicPS2AllPrimTypeTransTypeSetupFunc / sub_4A0480 600 each; sub_49FF10 / sub_4A0430 800 each; sub_4A06C0 / sub_4A09D0 500 each; _rpSkinMatrixUpdating 400;
sub_46B8E0 / sub_46EB90 400 each; openVU1SetupPktNew 500; sub_4F0F30 / RpSkyTexCacheAccessRaster 800 each; the bridge 800 (591 textured, 772 program
uploads); sub_46EA80 300; PS2AllNodeBody 500 + 200 observed (1,024 mesh draws through the bridge); AtomicDefaultRenderCallBack 300 (through
RxPipelineExecute into the node); plus rule checks (filter table, prim/transType table, light block layout, identity palette,
code index and program call). Not covered by pairs (heap / heavy callees): the resEntry reallocation and PS2AllNodeInstance paths
(checked against the instructions; exercised by the gate). A one-register mutation (`$t7` written before a back-edge of
openVU1SetupPktNew) fails both the return and the check-point comparison.
Slice: **917,399 assertions** (MSVC); `p3fes_game_tests` **205 cases / 32,310,259 assertions** on MSVC 14.44 Release and

## Phase 5: the battle-AI script commands -- slice comm_ai (2026-10-20)

**What.** The 120 handlers of `sScrCommandTable 0x7B92B0` that script_comm_a left (indices 51-117, 139-144, 149-180,
235-250; band 0x2C7300-0x2CE090 plus `sub_2D13C0`, 18,900 bytes of MIPS, all `sub_*`; `sub_27D730` [166] stays out:
heap) in `game/src/script/comm_ai.cpp` / `comm_ai.h`. They are the COMM functions of the AI scripts in AICALC.TBL; the
script's user word is the acting btlAction (+48 btlUnit: +162 side, +164 id, +2604 DatUnit; +56 the command record
of `sub_2C6A00`, so +108 command kind / +110 skill; +136 the target record). An AI query is one word
`kind << 24 | (param & 0xFFFFFF)` decoded through two tables by `jalr`: the conditions `0x6971B0` (72 x {fn, name,
flag}, MYHP ... MYHOJO; e.g. MYHP `sub_2C12F0` = `100 * hp <= max_hp * param`) and the target selectors `0x6975E0`
(37 x {fn, name}, AI HPMIN LVMIN MPMAX ... HOJO); every selecting handler falls back to row 0 (AI) when its selector
returns 0. Families (X-macro tables in the header, one template each): ASK [argc 1] 57, ASK_FIXED [0] 8 (ESCAPE,
SUMMON, SENSEI, MY/FR/ENGROUP, MYHREC, MORE), TARGET_FIXED [0] 9, TARGET [1] 19, COMMAND [0] 4 (`sub_2C6A00` codes
0x8000 attack / 0x8001 / 0x8002 / 0x8007), ASK_ALLY [2] 9 and ALLY_FIXED [1] 2 (the unit with id arg0 on the acting
unit's side through `sub_2C0E30`, excluding the dead); and 12 of their own shape: `sub_2C7340` (attack / skill
(u16)arg0 / command 7 by sign), `sub_2C7540` / `sub_2C75D0` (command 9, skill 341, +118/+120 = args, target MYAI),
`sub_2D13C0` (the unit's AICALC section-15 row: `sub_2C6BA0` index, `sub_2C6E30` row, command = row +2, target query
= row +4), `sub_2C9BA0` (MYBAD on an ally, dead ones included when the bits hold 0x80000), `sub_2C9CE0` / `sub_2CE010`
(`sub_301CA0` effect mask of an ally / of the action with id arg0), `sub_2CD4E0` (APPOINT after copying the appointed
action's target record, gBtl +328), `sub_2C73E0` (item command 3, +112 item, +110 = `sub_30BC20(item)`), `sub_2CB190`
(side arg0 and id arg1), `sub_2CDF40` (MYHP of the action with id arg0, no null check), `sub_2CE090` (a normal attack
`datCalcDamage(0, me, it, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1)` would leave it at hp <= 0). No handler has another caller (no jal, no other
data word in the ELF).

**Register discipline.** Every handler writes the original prologue spills (`Frame`), sets `$ra` to the original
link for every `jal` and `jalr` (the table calls through `rt::lookup_func`, as the recompiled body), and writes
between calls exactly the GPRs the original writes with the original 64-bit values: the query halves (`$v1` = param &
0xFFFFFF, `$v0` = kind << 24, the or into `$s0`/`$s1`/`$a0`), the kind byte back out (`and` with 0xFFFFFFFFFF000000,
32-bit `srl`), the table offsets (`$v0` = 3k, `$v1` = 12k / `$v1` = 8k), the unit finder's side mask (`$v1` = side,
`$v0` = 1 << side, `$a1`, `$a2` = 0x80000), `$t0..$t3` of datCalcDamage. After the last call: `$v0` = 1 and the epilogue.
The kind-zero branches of ASK / ASK_ALLY are dead (the kinds are constants) but kept.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_comm_ai.cpp`, 4 cases). Two guest machines in lockstep (hand on one, `__recomp` on
the other), so nothing is restored between the runs; each pair compares through `run_hw` / `expect_same_hw` `$v0`,
all GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, the whole register file and the cycle count at every check point of the call tree (the
AI table functions, datCalcDamage / datScriptCalc ...), the dead stack, 14 KiB of deeper stack, the gp globals, the
party / flag records, the datScript context and RNG state, the battle world and the AI tables, the FPRs at the end,
and the whole 32 MiB of main RAM every 32 pairs and at the end of each case. Real AI action objects: the eight
battle/*.TBL files as btlTableLoad lays them out (AICALC section 15 drives `sub_2D13C0`), gBtl with 2..8 btlActions
(+8 uid, +26 active bits, +1188/+1192 links), btlUnits (+162/+164/+2604, the per-side lists gBtl +340 + 8 * side with
+2608 links, the 12 slots at gBtl +2656), DatUnits (party ids 1..10, enemy ids < 336, random HP and statuses incl. dead),
the appointed action, skills whose SKILL.TBL target bits name a side; pointer-like words aligned and inside RAM. The AI
functions are non-leaf (MYHP spills `$ra` in a 48-byte frame); a rule case checks that spill directly (0x2C7730 at
`sp - 48` under `sub_2C76B0`). Results: random battles **11,222 pairs** (conditions true 1,495 / false 5,801) plus
**298 faulting worlds** (2.6 %: the default selector AI with an empty candidate list calls `datCalcRand(0)` and loads
through the remainder -- an unmapped load, a bus error on the EE; both bodies must fault identically, counted not
compared further), 351 full-RAM compares; stub rows (every table row `jr ra; move v0, a1` / `li v0, 1` /
`move v0, zero`: the query word, the 24-bit param mask, the fallback) 1,192 pairs, 409 exact results checked; rules
(the link spill, command kinds at +108, skill / item fields, the `sub_2CB190` host model) 1,801 pairs. Slice:
**1,056,300 assertions** on MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/comm_ai-msvc`) and on clang-cl 22.1.0 Debug
(`build/comm_ai-clang`). Mutations checked: dropping the `$v1` side write before `sub_2C0E30` (caught at that
callee's entry check point, register 3) and one block cost of ASK_ALLY (+1) both fail.

**Suites and gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build\comm_ai-gate -ClangTree build\comm_ai-clang -Jobs 3 -FastGs`, base
`a504c1f`, 14,500 functions, 862 replaced): ctest 16 / 16 on MSVC 14.44 Release and on clang-cl 22.1.0 Debug;
`p3fes_game_tests` **195 cases / 32,449,160 assertions** on both; dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85`, M1 `E3A93615…B672`, battle
`CFAA5A61…F606`, all 0 differing bytes / 0 runs, gsMemory identical: **GATE: PASSED** (1,304 s). Coverage note: a
temporary first-hit probe in the 120 shims (not committed) showed that the battle route runs **none** of them (its
turns never reach an AI script's COMM calls; which path chooses them was not traced), so
the replay gates only show that nothing else moved; the evidence for these handlers is the pair tests above.
## Phase 5: rendering -- RW builders that reach the DMA packet layer (render_rw2, 2026-10-20)

**What.** 35 functions (9,164 bytes) of the RenderWare sky driver's "Full queue" (queue_rendering.txt, class a/a0 with
the callsB flag, none of the first/second slice rows), hand-written in `game/src/render/rw_builders.cpp` /
`game/include/p3fes/game/rw_builders.h`, gated with the hardware-observing pairs (`tests/game/test_render_rw2.cpp`). Hot
path first: c4 the seven PDS skin bridge wrappers `sub_472130 … sub_473380` (palette upload `sub_46B8E0` when `0x95DE38`
is set, then the bridge), c6 `RpSkyRenderStateSet` 0x4D7F60 (DIMX / ALPHA_1 / TEST_1 A+D packets), c5 the image upload
header `sub_4EF540` (BITBLTBUF / TRXREG), c1 the PTank constant attribute fills `sub_478100` / `sub_477810` / `sub_477C90`
/ `sub_485EF0` / `sub_485FF0` and the 2D lock `sub_477470`; then the per-frame DMA queue (`sub_4D4280` resource-reference
flush, `_rwDMAWaitQueue`, `_rwDMAReqFlip`), `SkyRasterShowRaster`, the camera end `sub_4D8E80` (TEXFLUSH), the raster GS
packets `sub_4E4180` / `sub_4E4420` / `sub_4E4560` / `sub_4E46C0`, the raster clear `sub_4E4800` / `sub_4E4E40`, the PDS
2D pair tail calls `sub_46FB70` / `sub_470780` / `sub_471210`, the PS2All resEntry header at 0x4A26D0 (functions.json
names it `HandleUnexpected__FP12ThrowContext…`, a stray C++ runtime symbol: kept), the VU1 record upload `sub_46C330`,
the PTank callback setters `sub_478440` / `sub_479840`, texture state `sub_4748C0` and camera block `sub_4733C0`.

**Not taken** (the other 40 callsB rows of the band): printf users `sub_46F400`, `sub_470200`, `sub_470E10` (their 12-byte
entries are taken: a tail call does not reach printf itself); syscall users through `DIntr`/`EIntr`/`SyncDCache`/
`_sceFlushCache` in their own bodies or direct callees: `sub_47A710`, `sub_4EFA00`, `sub_4EF770`, `sub_4DEFD0`,
`sub_4DE0A0`, `sub_4E53E0`, `sub_4E6D60`, `sub_4E8610`; device-pointer calls into `_rwSkySetRenderState`'s closure:
`sub_47BE10`; left for later passes by size (1-6.5 KB, MMI-heavy, most a0): the PDS bridges `matfxBridgeBumpMap`, `matfxBridgeEnvMap`,
`matfxBridgeBumpEnvMap`, `matfxBridgeDual`, `matfxBridgeUvTransform`, `matfxBridgeDualUvTransform`, `skinSplitObjectSetupCB`, the 2D bridges `sub_46FDD0`,
`RpPDS_G3_2DFont_PS2AllBridgeCallBack`, `sub_471470`, `sub_4A2790`, `_rwSkySetRenderState`, `SkyCameraBeginUpdate`,
`sub_4D8F40`, `sub_4E3640`, `sub_4F0C70`, `sub_4F1B30`, `sub_4F1780`, the PTank `sub_477150`, `sub_479170`, `sub_479590`,
`sub_485110`, `sub_485440`, `sub_478520`, `sub_479900`, `sub_47B280`, `sub_47B750`, `sub_47BF80`.

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) `sub_4E4180` puts the *FRAME_1* shadow at `$gp-17080` (picked per field from `0x9649F0` /
`0x964B60`) and ZBUF_1 at `$gp-17088`; mode 2 masks Z writes and dithers below 24 bpp, every other mode masks the colour
(a Z-only pass), and both force the render-flags shadow's bits 5..8 to 3 after saving it at `$gp-16920` (restored by
`sub_4E46C0`). (2) `sub_4E4800` passes the colour word as the 9th argument (the sprite's Z) of `sub_4E4420`. (3) The PTank
fills unroll by eight only while the count is in 9..0x7FFFFFFE (64-bit signed compares); a stream whose stride is the
element size goes through the scratchpad streamer with `count * stride` bytes, unchecked. (4) `_rwDMAReqFlip` and
`_rwDMAWaitQueue` reach `_rwDMAForceBufferSwap`, which spins until the queue drains and the busy flags clear (only the DMA
interrupts do that): the tests keep swap paths to idle worlds without an open packet. (5) `sub_4EF540`'s `$t2` only selects
between two copies of the same block (57 / 56 cycles).

**Cycle-model notes.** A block that contains a `jal` is charged in full before the call (the recompiler keeps calls inside
blocks: `SkyRasterShowRaster` charges 15 before three calls). Forward "back-edges" (an out-of-line block that jumps back
through a check point): `sub_4D8E80` (TEXFLUSH flag clear, the copy path), `RpSkyRenderStateSet` (every packet path),
`SkyRasterShowRaster` (pending clear, deferred-op flag), `sub_4748C0` (no texture), the field-parity wait of the raster
packets (`di` loop, the non-interlaced path), `sub_4E4800`'s CPU fill exit.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_rw2.cpp`, 18 cases, ~6,500 hardware-observing pairs; every pair compares the
Outcome, all GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, the register file at every check point, the dead stack, the bus log, the
scratchpad, the RW globals `[0x7CDDC0, 0x7CEB40)`, the RW absolute globals `[0x95DE00, 0x965C00)`, the DMA window and the
case's objects; functions with far-reaching recompiled callees also compare all of main RAM): pair tails 120, skin bridges
168 (an RxPS2AllPipeData fixture: the bridges and the palette upload run to completion), resEntry header 200, PU-ref flush
300 (counts split at 0xFFFF), wait queue / flip 400, raster packets 600 + 100 documented (A+D register order), render
states 800 (+ documented packets), show raster / camera end / whole clear 300, PTank setters 200 (the lock callbacks run
through `sub_4861B0`), constant UV 400, texture / camera block 200, raster clear 400 (GS and CPU paths), 2D lock 300,
constant fills 750, upload header 300, VU1 records 300, and 270 calls on the battle_ref_6150, dorm_replay_4900 and b_5800
snapshots' whole machine (render states, raster packets, camera end, raster clear). Slice: **460,719 assertions** on both
compilers. A one-register mutation (`$t4` of `sub_4E4180`) trips 102 assertions at once.
`p3fes_game_tests` **209 cases / 31,853,579 assertions** on MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/rw2-gate`) and clang-cl Debug
(`build/rw2-clang`).

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build/rw2-gate -ClangTree build/rw2-clang -Jobs 3 -FastGs`, base `a504c1f`, 777
replaced): ctest 16/16 on both compilers, dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85` 0 bytes, M1 `E3A93615…B672` 0 bytes, battle
`CFAA5A61…F606` 0 bytes, gsMemory identical in all three: **GATE: PASSED**.
## Phase 5: rendering -- the MatFX material bridges and the partitioned skin set-up (render_bridges, 2026-10-21)

**What.** The seven rows render_rw2 left for size (15,884 bytes of MIPS), hand-written in
`game/src/render/bridges.cpp` / `game/include/p3fes/game/bridges.h`, pair-tested in `tests/game/test_render_bridges.cpp`;
functions.json names kept, proposed names in `symbols/deltas/render_bridges.sym`. The bridge table `0x6B4EE4` that
`sub_46EA80` indexes with the material's MatFX effect word (extension +128) holds, by RenderWare's RpMatFXMaterialFlags
order: 0 `RpMeshPS2AllBridgeCallBack` (stock), 1 `matfxBridgeBumpMap` bump map, 2 `matfxBridgeEnvMap` environment map, 3 `matfxBridgeBumpEnvMap`
bump + environment, 4 `matfxBridgeDual` dual texture, 5 `matfxBridgeUvTransform` UV transform, 6 `matfxBridgeDualUvTransform` dual + UV transform -- the
fields each body reads confirm the order (bump frame / texture / coefficient x inverse width, environment frame /
texture / coefficient, dual texture, UV matrices). `skinSplitObjectSetupCB` is the object set-up callback of partitioned skins:
`sub_46EB90`'s body with a different palette step (skin +48 != 0: `0x95DE38` = skin + 44 and no upload, the per-mesh
wrappers `sub_472130 .. sub_473380` upload their part through `sub_46B8E0`; else the whole palette and `0x95DE38` = 0).

**Packets (new facts, from the instructions).** Every bridge is the stock bridge with an effect block before the GIF
tag and, except the UV transform, a closing packet after the resEntry call:
- UV transform: `_rwDMAOpenVIFPkt(0, 4)`, cnt 3 with STCYCL 4,4 / UNPACK V4-32 x3 -> VU1 0x3BC in the tag's VIF words,
  rows 0, 1, 3 of the UV matrix ({x, y} in the low half); a missing matrix becomes an identity RwMatrix built on the
  frame (sp+80, flags | 0x20003).
- Bump map: the bump texture (else the material's) **replaces the PipeData's texture (pd +64)** before the stock texture
  state; cnt 26, STCYCL 1,1 / UNPACK x10 -> 0x3BC: {coefficient x inverse width, 0, 1/(far-near), far}, two A+D blocks
  (ALPHA_1 = 2 | 128 << 32 and TEST_1 = the shadow & 0x70000; ALPHA_1 = 72 | 128 << 32 and TEST_1), the bump light's
  3x4 matrix (`matfxEffectMatrix(frame, out, PipeData)`: 0 = the camera's frame; cached per atomic / frame / frame counter at
  gp-17808..-17800, inverse into 0x95C460); the camera far plane / depth scale cached at gp-20924 / gp-20928 (the
  bump + environment bridge has its own pair, gp-20916 / gp-20920). Closing: DIRECT 3, ALPHA_1 / TEST_1 from the shadows.
- Two-texture effects (environment, bump + environment, dual, dual + UV): the base texture and the effect texture are
  placed (sub_4F0F30 for both, RpSkyTexCacheAccessRaster(effect, 1) then (base, 0), again for a raster whose extension
  has no cache slot at +88); the raster-alpha flag is set unless the base raster's format nibble is 6; ATE is forced on;
  both rasters narrower than 2^9 (raster +20 < 9) set the last raster to -1. The block (cnt 30 / 34 / 43 / 33) holds
  the second pass's vertex GIF tag (PRE; PRIM = 0x258 | prim | FGE from trans-type bit 0, i.e. Gouraud, textured,
  blended, **context 2**; NREG 3, REGS ST / RGBAQ / XYZF2 = 0x412) and A+D kick blocks (TEX0_1 of the base with the
  driver's FOGCOL, TEX0_2 of the effect texture with the effect's FOGCOL), the effect's matrices (environment: rows 0,
  1 and row 2 with the coefficient in w, plus the constant quadword 0x6B5150 / 0x6B5160; dual + UV: the two UV
  matrices' rows 0, 1, 3 paired in one quadword each), then DIRECT 6: GIF tag NLOOP 5 with ALPHA_2 / CLAMP_2 / TEST_2 /
  TEX1_2 / ZBUF_2 (0x43, 0x09, 0x48, 0x15, 0x4F). The effect slot's GS words: +40 ALPHA_2, +48 FOGCOL (0x01000000 =
  the driver's FOGCOL shadow gp-17056 in the dual bridges; the environment bridges use the word as given), +56 TEST_2
  bits ORed into TEST_1 & 0x70000; ZBUF_2 = the ZBUF_1 shadow. Closing: FOGCOL restored (bump + environment: ALPHA_1,
  TEST_1 and FOGCOL).

**Style and draw data.** As mesh.cpp: a Cpu view of the guest registers (one variable per GPR, the runtime's MMI / FPU /
COP0 semantics, prologue spills), structured control flow with the recompiled body's block costs; the compiler's
out-of-line blocks that jump back are inlined where they branch, keeping their check points. Each bridge reports its
mesh draw through the render_mesh observer (`mesh::MeshDraw`; `mesh::draw_observer()` added to mesh.h / mesh.cpp, two
lines, so the bridges can reach the installed observer) and the MatFX extra through `bridges::set_effect_observer`
(`EffectDraw`: effect, effect texture / raster, where the effect block and the closing packet went); `skinSplitObjectSetupCB`
reports the palette it uploads as `SkinPalette`.

**Cycle-model notes.** The layouts differ from the stock bridge in small ways that matter: `matfxBridgeBumpMap` /
`matfxBridgeBumpEnvMap` take the material's texture in an out-of-line block (a check point); the two-texture bridges'
TME-off and CLAMP-U blocks and both ABE blocks are out-of-line (check points), the CLAMP-V and AddPURef blocks are not;
`matfxBridgeDualUvTransform` reaches the identity block through one or two out-of-line blocks (each a check point, the `s1` test
skipped when `s2` is null). `skinSplitObjectSetupCB` differs from `sub_46EB90` in two block boundaries: no block of its own before
the sector-light inner loop and none after the 8-matrix palette loop (both carry a `+= 1` in `sub_46EB90`).

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_bridges.cpp`, 9 cases, 4,680 pairs; the test_render_mesh harness: every GPR in
128 bits, HI/LO, SA, FPRs, ACC, FCR31, VU0 at the return; the register file and cycles at every check point; bus log,
scratchpad, the whole stack window, the world, gp window, RW / skin globals, packet templates, texture cache, CLUT words,
the matfxEffectMatrix cache and the DMA window). Worlds: random atomic / camera / frames / geometry / mesh header, the material
with its MatFX extension (both slots, null textures / frames / matrices often), base and effect textures with rasters,
extensions and cache slots, material pipeline private data and code array, resEntries and the reference ring, GS
shadows and camera words, the four DMA packet states with nearly full scratchpad halves; skins with or without
hierarchy and partitions, 1..16 bones. Per bridge 600 pairs; skinSplitObjectSetupCB 800 (282 partitioned, 465 whole uploads, 231
of them with 9+ bones, 53 without meshes); observers 280 (240 mesh draws, 40 palettes; documented rules: the UV block's
tag and rows, the DIRECT 6 register numbers, the code index and program, the PipeData texture of the bump bridge, the
partition record). Mutations: one extra register write at the return of matfxBridgeUvTransform fails all 600 pairs; one register
written before a check point of matfxBridgeDual fails at that check point (153 assertions). Slice **405,731 assertions** on
MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/render_bridges-msvc`) and clang-cl 19.1.5 Debug (`build/render_bridges-clang`).

**Coverage on the routes** (a temporary first-hit / count probe in the seven shims, not committed, on the gate tree's
fast build): dorm (vblank 4900) `matfxBridgeUvTransform` 738, `matfxBridgeDualUvTransform` 1,230, `skinSplitObjectSetupCB` 2,214 calls; battle (vblank 6150)
`matfxBridgeEnvMap` 6,484, `matfxBridgeDual` 7,504, `matfxBridgeUvTransform` 11,653, `matfxBridgeDualUvTransform` 9,511, `skinSplitObjectSetupCB` 20,683. The two bump-map
bridges (`matfxBridgeBumpMap`, `matfxBridgeBumpEnvMap`) run on neither route: their evidence is the pair tests.

**Suites and gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Repo <worktree> -Tree build\render_bridges-gate -ClangTree
build\render_bridges-clang -Jobs 3 -FastGs`, base `24e1fe2`, 1,163 replaced): ctest 16/16 on MSVC 14.44 Release and on

`E3A93615…B672`, battle `CFAA5A61…F606`, all 0 differing bytes / 0 runs, gsMemory identical: **GATE: PASSED** (3,442 s).

`sScrCommandTable 0x7B92B0` that script_comm_a / script_comm_b / comm_b2 / comm_ai left:

* AI target pickers returning `unit +8 | 0x80000000` or -1, over the candidate filter `sub_2C3430` (action +0x38 list, u16 +0x6A
  count) and the unit counter `sub_2C0F40`: the only / a random one (`sub_2CE5C0`, `sub_2CE6C0` family of 5), the lowest HP
  (`sub_2CF450` family of 6, `sub_2D0270`), the highest level (`sub_2CEF10`, `sub_2CF1D0`, `sub_2CED60`), without a bad status
  (`sub_2CF070`, count `sub_2CF340`), the current unit if listed (`sub_2CEB20`), `sub_2CEC30`; the counts `sub_2CDB70` family of 6;

**Fidelity.** The register transfers are written with the rt:: operations of the original instructions (named idioms: `low24` =
`dsll32/dsrl32 8`, `move` = `daddu rd, rs, zero`, `la` = `lui/addiu`, `cond_row_call`, `selector_row_call`, `fixed_row_call`), in the
original order, so every GPR holds the original 64-bit value at every call, check point and return (the query words and halves, the
12k / 8k table offsets, the side masks, `$at` of `sltu` / `slti`, the six filter arguments in `$a0..$t1`, the list pointer in `$t2`);
`Frame` writes the prologue spills; the lists the originals keep in their frames (sp + 0x20 / 0x50 / 0x60 / 0x90) stay at the original
addresses because the callees fill them there. Cycle model: the loops test first, so the back-edge check comes before every body
after a successful test; `sub_2CEB20`'s walk leaves through its body (`beq`) into the same exit block as the test.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_comm_c.cpp`, 3 cases; the twin-machine harness of test_comm_ai.cpp: lockstep machines, `run_hw`
with the register file and cycle count at every check point, all GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, the dead stack, the gp globals, g_data,
the battle and field worlds, the AI tables, the FPRs, the whole 32 MiB every 32 pairs). World: the real battle/*.TBL, gBtl with 2..8
actions (mostly 5..8 so the target lists hold several candidates), the stage record gBtl +0xBBC (ids 0x1A5 / 0x1B0 / 0x1B4 / others),
the field unit records gFldUnitsPc, sField's object, sub_3C8EC0's record list, the social link table, the message manager slots.
Random worlds: 7,507 pairs (conditions true 157 / false 1,123; unit ids found 650, 98 of them from lists of several
candidates, none 1,910), 235 full-RAM compares, 45 faulting worlds (2.2 %; all in the selector rows of `sub_2CD570` /

## Phase 5: rendering -- RenderWare's particle tanks, RpPTank (render_ptank, 2026-10-21)

**What.** 44 functions (23,068 bytes) of RpPTank, hand-written in `game/src/render/ptank.cpp` /
`game/include/p3fes/game/ptank.h` and gated with `tests/game/test_render_ptank.cpp`: the ten functions `render_rw2`
deferred (the 2-D / 3-D locks `sub_477150` / `sub_479170` / `sub_479590`, the fill writers `sub_485110` /
`sub_485440`, the material bridges `sub_478520` / `sub_479900`, the object-per-matrix draws `sub_47B280` /
`sub_47B750`, the streamed format set-up `sub_47BF80`) and every class-a c1 row of queue_rendering.txt not yet
replaced (28: the 3-D sprite writers `sub_486980 … sub_4884A0` incl. the sinf/cosf-rotated four and the spilled
eight-way colour writer `sub_487BF0`, the 2-D one-vertex writers `sub_477610 / sub_477A20 / sub_477EB0 / sub_478280`,
the streamer-fast-path writers `sub_485070 / sub_485E20 / sub_486100`, the 3-D instance begin `sub_488550`, the
instance end `sub_488B80`), plus the class-a [ptank] leaves on the same per-frame path: the format set-up
`sub_4866C0`, the instance runner `sub_4861B0`, the render callbacks `sub_474160` / `sub_488B90`, the ALPHA / CLAMP
words `sub_474A80` / `sub_4749A0`. Data flow: ptank.h (the tank block layout, the instance callbacks at block
+36 .. +56, the four-vertex corner order).

**Not taken.** `sub_47BB40` (allocates through the RwMalloc pointer in its own body), `sub_47A710` / `sub_47BE10`
(render_rw2's reasons: syscall users / device-pointer closure), and the 16 class-b instance writers / streamers
(`sub_476140 … sub_476980`, `sub_47C240 … sub_485750`: D8/D9 registers in their own bodies; they stay recompiled
callees).

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) One flag word (+168) holds both the format and the attribute bits (the set-ups read it as
+80 +88). (2) The constant colour writers step by the stream's stride (not packed). (3) The 2-D writers write one
vertex per particle; the 3-D ones four, `v0 = p - r - u, v1 = p + r - u, v2 = p + r + u, v3 = p - r + u`. (4) The
lock record lives on `sub_4861B0`'s frame; without an instance-begin callback it is never cleared (the writers then
read whatever the stack held). (5) The bridges draw in GS context 2 (A+D ALPHA_2 / CLAMP_2 / TEST_2 / TEX1_2 /
ZBUF_2 from the pipeline record +184 .. +208 and the ZBUF_1 shadow). (6) `sub_4866C0` clears +52 without the 0x10
flag; `sub_47BF80` leaves it.

**Cycle-model notes.** Blocks with `jal` / `jalr` are charged in full before the call (the rotation writers' 91 .. 121
cycle blocks hold both libm calls). The eight-way loops' exits differ per body: one extra block in `sub_478280` and
`sub_487EF0`, none in `sub_4880B0`, `sub_477610`, `sub_477A20`, `sub_477EB0`, `sub_485110` / `sub_485440`,
`sub_487BF0`; likewise the four-vertex loops' exits (`sub_486100` has one, `sub_486980` none); `sub_47B280`'s clip-plane
loop has an exhausted-exit block that `sub_47B750` lacks. Forward "back-edges" (out-of-line blocks jumping back
through a check point): the lock record parts, the camera-axes paths, the first three UV / colour picks of the
set-ups, the bridges' re-instance and first-reference paths, the object draws' batch flushes. `sub_474A80`'s two `jr`
tables are C++ switches with the per-case costs (2, the default leaf 1) and the generated fallback (an out-of-table
target goes to `rt::lookup_func`).

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_ptank.cpp`; every pair compares all GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, SA, all FPRs, ACC,
FCR31, VU0, the register file and cycles at every check point, the bus log, the scratchpad, the world region, the gp
window, the whole stack window (live and dead), plus the DMA window / RW templates / texture cache / VU1 record batch
where the function reaches the packet layer). The bus is a fake DMAC: a D8 / D9 CHCR write with STR moves the
transfer at once (toSPR / fromSPR between MADR and SADR) and raises the channel's D_STAT bit, so the recompiled
streamers' waits end and their data really moves. Real call chains: `sub_4861B0` drives the hand 3-D lock and
writers; the bridges run the hand texture / colour uploads and the recompiled packet layer; the object draws run
the game's own point transform (0x4E3EC0, from the battle snapshot's device table) and RxPipelineExecute on a
one-node pipeline.
Slice: 12 cases, 11,280 pairs, **902,932 assertions** on both compilers. `p3fes_game_tests` **266 cases / 37,167,831
assertions** on MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/render_ptank-gate`) and clang-cl Debug (`build/render_ptank-clang`).

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build/render_ptank-gate -ClangTree build/render_ptank-clang -Jobs 3 -FastGs`,

## Phase 5: rendering -- the sky driver's core and the 2D bridges (render_sky, 2026-10-21)

**What.** 11 functions (15,780 bytes) that render_rw2 left for a dedicated pass, hand-written in
`game/src/render/sky.cpp` / `game/include/p3fes/game/sky.h`, gated with the hardware-observing pairs
(`tests/game/test_render_sky.cpp`): the render-state funnel `_rwSkySetRenderState` 0x4D6B90 (3,352 B; every frame,
~665 call sites through the device pointer), `SkyCameraBeginUpdate` 0x4D84C0 (2,484 B; every camera pass),
`sub_4D8F40` [SkyCameraClear] (1,312 B), `sub_4E3640` [mip-map chain on the GS] (2,036 B), the texture cache
`sub_4F0C70` [PATH3 upload] (704 B), `sub_4F1780` [placement / release / eviction hand] (936 B), `sub_4F1B30`
[deferred TEX0 / TEX1 / MIPTBP packet] (736 B), the PDS 2D bridges `sub_46FDD0` / `RpPDS_G3_2DFont_PS2AllBridgeCallBack`
0x4709E0 / `sub_471470` (1,060 B each, byte-identical bodies) and the Im3D bridge `sub_4A2790` (1,040 B; the same
skeleton with the stock code-index rule). Nothing of the prompt's list was skipped: no syscall, printf or heap in
their own bodies (`sub_4F1780` reaches DIntr/EIntr only through its recompiled callee `sub_4EFA00`).

**How.** The bodies run on `sky::Cpu` (one variable per guest register, mesh.cpp's model). They were first
transliterated mechanically from the recompiled blocks (a scratch converter: `rt::` call -> Cpu statement,
`ctx.cycles += N` -> charge, back-edge `check_events` -> backedge, `rt::jal` + delay slot + call -> `jal`), then
structured by hand (gotos -> if/else / loops, shared exits as helpers, delay slots hoisted where they do not feed
the branch, the three identical 2D bodies and the Im3D one as `bridge_2d(start)`), named and commented. The four
`jr` tables (0x7BCCC0 filter, 0x7BCC90 / 0x7BCC60 blend, 0x7BCC30 alpha test; 0x7BCF40 / 0x7BCF20 in the mip chain)
are read from guest memory as the originals do (the target stays in `$v0` / `$a1`) and dispatched on the target.

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) The funnel's compare chain (13, 30, 29, 20, 16, 15, 14, 12, 11, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, then
5 / 4 / 3 / 2 / 1 in `$a2` / `$a1` / `$v1` / `$v0` / `$s0`) leaves its constants where the handlers use them:
state 2 (address U+V) writes CLAMP_1 = `$a2` (5) for clamp, state 1 returns `$s0` (1, or 0 when the raster could not
be made resident). (2) States 2..4 refuse mirror (2) and border (4); state 13 always returns 0; blend pairs come from
the 6x6 table 0x77EF80 (a negative word = refused), src = dest = 1 adds FIX 0x80. (3) The 2D bridges force the
material alpha to 254 (always ABE) and pick code entry `camera+20 != 1` from 0x95EF84 (the camera they draw with);
they set the resEntry's use word to 1 before counting it, so their `_rwDMAAddPURef` branch never runs. (4)
`SkyCameraBeginUpdate` takes FRAME_1 from 0x9649F0 on odd frames and 0x964B60 on even ones; `sub_4F1B30` the other
way round. (5) `sub_4F1780`'s eviction hand wraps at the next-free index: the game keeps hand and end below it.

**Cycle-model notes.** The camera's frustum (corners, planes, four `sub_4C6970` calls, `sub_4EEC20`) is one
375-cycle block charged before its first call. Forward "back-edges" (out-of-line blocks jumping back through a
check point): the funnel's raster-alpha tails, Z test off, shade mode, vertex alpha, fog type 1; the camera's
first-BeginUpdate flag, FRAME_1 by parity, the owed raster packet, the XYOFFSET paths; the clear's FRAME_1 by parity
and the non-interlaced XYOFFSET; the cache's release / eviction bookkeeping; the bridges' second clip pair and
projection 3. The `di` / `sync.p` / `mfc0 Status` waits are a 7-cycle block with a check point per retry.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_sky.cpp`, 9 cases; every pair compares the Outcome, all GPRs in 128 bits,
HI/LO, the register file at every check point, the dead stack, the bus log, the scratchpad, the RW globals, the RW
absolute globals, the texture-cache words, the DMA window, the case's objects, and for the camera, cache and bridge
cases all of main RAM): funnel 1,400 (every state, refused values, whole-register states; documented A+D packets),
`sub_4F1B30` 400, camera begin 300 (camera textures resident or not, too-large rasters -> RwError, interlace),
camera clear 300, mip chain 300 (0..6 levels, PSM 0 / 1 / 0x0A / others, widths over 64), PATH3 upload 300,
placement 400 (release, keep, place, the eviction hand), the four bridges 600 (documented resEntry counts), and 480
pairs on the battle_ref_6150, dorm_replay_4900 and b_5800 snapshots' whole machine (the raster state on the cache's
own resident rasters, every other state, camera begin / clear on the kwln root camera, `sub_4F1B30`, cache
keep / release, the mip chain). Slice: **347,604 assertions** on both compilers. Mutations: ten one-instruction
changes spread over the nine distinct bodies (an FPU op of the frustum, a register of the error path, a cycle count of a
filter case, the TME bit, the clear's colour shift, the PSM 0x0A offset, the eviction store, the upload copy step,
the Im3D code index, a MIPTBP register number) fail all nine cases; the error-path and TME changes alone fail theirs.
`p3fes_game_tests` **263 cases / 36,612,503 assertions** on MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/render_sky-gate`) and clang-cl Debug
(`build/render_sky-clang`).

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build/render_sky-gate -ClangTree build/render_sky-clang -Jobs 3 -FastGs`, base `24e1fe2`, 1,167
replaced): ctest 16/16 on both compilers, dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85` 0 bytes, M1 `E3A93615…B672` 0 bytes, battle

## Phase 5: the field layer's larger functions (slice field_big, 2026-10-21)

**What.** 33 functions, 21,060 bytes, of `docs/ANALYSIS/queue_field.txt` (open class-a rows the field_lo / field_hi slices
left for size, plus the leaves they left without a route caller), in `game/src/field/field_big.cpp` /
`game/include/p3fes/game/field_big.h` (`sub_*` keep their functions.json names; proposals in brackets in the header):
the per-frame Tartarus block culling `sub_1BD950` (6,340 B: eight view wedges of 20 / 21 cells by the main camera's yaw,
written as tables of (dx, dz) cell offsets; block parts of types 10 / 11 copy their block's draw flag, enemies within
2000 of the hero get it), the floor generator's block rotation `sub_1BAB60` (1,328 B: cells from the kind table, the
2 x 2 / 1 x 2 / 3 x 3 ring moves, the door-nibble rotation) and fitting `sub_1BC630` (1,168 B: first free origin covering
the cell, doors inside 1..14 and meeting taken neighbours), the field-entry choices `sub_1B6EB0` (1,836 B: the scene
variant by time of day through the jump table 0x7B6B00 and the season), `sub_1A9850` (2,396 B: the BGM by Tartarus floor
-- floor 400, the route's Thebel, plays BGM 1 -- or by scene / season / flags) and `sub_1AA1B0` (1,844 B: ENV_*.ADX on
channel 4), the enemy pop scheduler `K_Unit_UpdateEnemyPopSchedulerTask` (1,052 B) with `sub_1D38D0` / `sub_1D3830`
and the spawner `sub_1D0720` (Thebel 51/1: encounter 466 + i with bit 16), the collision controller's
`K_FldFrame_HandleCollis` (the grid block's mesh), `sub_1AD940` / `sub_1ADD40` / `sub_1ADFF0` [position, grid cell, turn
in place], the field hits `K_FldEvent_FindFldHitAt` / `K_FldEvent_IsUnitNearFldHit`, the virtual pad's turn
`sub_1E1590` / `sub_1E13F0`, the camera's nearest point `sub_1D5140`, `sub_1C7130`, the transparent-wall fade callbacks
`sub_1C0880` / `sub_1C0960`, and the leaves `sub_19C2F0/300/310/490`, `sub_1A4770/4780/47B0`, `sub_1B01B0/01D0/0230/0250`.
Not taken: the 0x1C2000-0x1C6000 COMM handlers (script slices), `sub_1DA020` (9,936 B) / `sub_1CD9A0` (3,800 B) / the
event task (task creation, printf, sound), render rows.

**How (registers and cycles).** Every body runs on a register view of the guest context (`Cpu` in the .cpp: one proxy
per GPR with the EE's 64-bit write semantics, the FPU / HI-LO through the runtime's own instruction functions), so each
value lives in the register the original keeps it in and every check point, call and return sees the original register
file; prologue spills and the originals' stack temporaries (the block-rotation temp cells, the colour copy, the
quad-triangle pointer triples) go to the guest stack, callees are entered with `$ra` = the original link. Within one
basic block (no check point inside) the statements read in the order that explains the code; the readable structure
comes from helpers that keep the exact block costs (`scene_is` / `scene_any` for the compare chains -- 3 + 3 cycles, 2
when the minor equals the major --, `date_in`, `time_is`, `play` / `start` for the sound calls, `door_mismatch` for the
four neighbours, `draw_wedge` = one block of 8 n + 4 cycles). The shims pass the caller's registers through untouched (no
re-sign-extension of the arguments). Notes: `sub_1D5140` returns the caller's `$s1` when no point is nearer; the
default of `sub_1B6EB0`'s jump table is mirrored as an indirect jump; `sub_1D38D0` compares unsigned and leaves HI/LO
as `mult` left them; `sub_1AD940`'s inlined 12-byte memset is a do-while with its own back-edge.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_field_big.cpp`, 16 cases): the field_hi harness (the whole register file in 128 bits,
HI/LO, SA, FPRs, ACC, FCR31 and the cycle count at every check point and at the return; memory `[0x600000, 0xA00000)`,
the arena and the stack, dead stack included; bus / syscall / trap counts). Callees run for real where their trees are
small (the scene-resource lookups, the camera yaw with atan2f, the unit distance test, mdlTranslate / rotate with
sinf / cosf, the spawn-slot search); the sound driver, the collision tests, the shadow creation, the Reaper creation and
the model-matrix update are left out on purpose and compared at the call. Documented rules on the host: the player's
cell always drawn, the free-origin search, the door-nibble rotation, field 1 / 15/6 variants, floor 400 -> BGM 1,
14/1 -> ENV_050, the Reaper limit minimum, the Thebel encounter 466. Coverage counters: 41 of 46 BGM call sites,
14 of 15 ambience call sites, 119 block fits of 290 free origins, 144 spawns reaching the shadow creation, 128 field hits found. A one-register mutation (`$v1` for `$v0` in the culling's yaw test,
same float) fails 200 assertions. The slice: 16 cases / 160,603 assertions on MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/field_big-msvc`). `p3fes_game_tests`: 270 cases /
36,425,502 assertions on MSVC Release (`build/field_big-gate`) and clang-cl 19.1.5 Debug (`build/field_big-clang`).

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build/field_big-gate -ClangTree build/field_big-clang -Jobs 3 -FastGs`, base `24e1fe2`,
1,189 replaced): ctest 16/16 on both compilers, dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85` 0 bytes, M1 `E3A93615…B672` 0 bytes, battle
`CFAA5A61…F606` 0 bytes, gsMemory identical in all three: **GATE: PASSED**.
