recovery numbers from a 40-byte result record on the frame) and update `0x29CCD0` (the item 4040 used up, -> ACTION); WIN
init `0x29CE90`; CONDITION init `0x29D1F0` (the daily condition: the jump tables 0x7B7C30 / 0x7B7C10 as C++ switches on the
loaded target, per-case block costs, the `jr` fallback as in the recompiled body); END init `0x29D870` (passives 606 full /
605 +8 % HP and SP, flags 4097..4100, the party records' +16, every action to EXIT). btlAction (sBtlActionTbl 0x693410):
COMMAND `sub_28BD10` [btlActionInitStateCommand] / `sub_28BF80` [btlActionUpdateStateCommand] (the menu, its help mode on
pad bit 3 of 0x7E094C / 0x7E0956, the result -> TARGET / READY / ANALYZE / AI, a refused command's 24-frame wait), TARGET
`sub_28C310` / `sub_28C590` (candidates by the SKILL.TBL target kind, the cursor, cancel bit 5 / confirm bit 6 of
0x7E094E / 0x7E0958), `btlActionUpdateStateEscape 0x296890` (the escape roll, the runners' walk-off or turn-back),
`btlActionUpdateStateAttack 0x28EB50` (8,316 B; split into `attack_hit` / `attack_strike` / `attack_record_end` with the
704-byte frame's locals named in `atk::`) and `btlActionUpdateStateSkill 0x290BE0` (16,684 B).

**Style.** The render_mesh Cpu view, register-faithful by construction: one variable per GPR, every load / store / FPU / MMI
(`paddub`) / HI-LO (`div`, `mflo`) operation through the runtime's own instruction, the prologue spills and reloads
written out, every callee through its generated entry point with the original link. The packet idioms are helpers
(`stamp_owner`, `stamp_state_owner`, `depend` / `depend_at` / `depend_id(_at)`, `enqueue`, `clear_bit5_71`, `skill_rec`).
Control flow is structured with the recompiled body's block costs; the two 0x7B7Cxx tables are switches. SKILL keeps the
compiled block layout where it is not a plain if / else (70 labels named by their original addresses, section comments
at the main ones): a scripted pass turned forward branches into if / else and the battle idioms into the helpers, the rest
was checked by hand and by the pairs. `enter` / `backedge` call rt::check_events directly (guest::enter is noexcept, and a
test hook may stop at a check point).

**Skipped.** None of the bodies of the slice (all 16 replaced, including the UNIT_CREATE / UNIT_LOAD / REVIVAL updates
and the COMMAND / TARGET inits next to the named ones); heap allocation, file loading and sound stay in the recompiled
callees, reached through their generated entry points.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_battle_actions.cpp`, 2 cases). Every function on 600 random battle worlds (200 in Debug
builds) against its `__recomp` body: the whole register file (GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, SA, FPRs, FCR31) and the cycle count
at every check point and at the return or the stop, and memory -- the battle world, low RAM, the packet buffer, all of
.data/.bss 0x5E0000-0x9B0000, 32 KiB of stack, the arena -- with every 25th pair restoring and comparing the whole 32 MiB.
Worlds: per-side unit lists A / B, the action list, packets in four queues, the result block a hit leaves in the target
(+200..), a SKILL.TBL stand-in at *(gp-18680), pads; background words are small numbers, aligned in-world pointers or
unmapped values (no stray write lands outside the restored windows). The RW heap hook the packet allocator calls through
0x960178 is served by `sub_4B3710` (`move v0, a1`: every packet at 0x40000, aligned; UNIT_CREATE init runs without a hook);
a queue walk around a packet queued twice is broken at the cycle budget in both runs. Callee trees run for real where
small (the packet creators, panel checks, btlUnit helpers, the menu / cursor closures). Documented rules on the host: REVIVAL waits while an active packet of the actor is
queued, the command wait counts +1156 down, a whole-side skill copies the candidates.
Every function also had pairs end at a compared stop (a callee not emitted in the test build, or the same fault in both
runs on a wild world pointer): returned normally / stopped of 600 -- UNIT_LOAD update 377 / 223, REVIVAL update 414 / 186,
WIN 323 / 277, END 284 / 316, CONDITION 180 / 420, UNIT_CREATE update 377 / 223, COMMAND update 451 / 149, TARGET update
190 / 410; UNIT_CREATE init, UNIT_LOAD init, REVIVAL init, COMMAND init, TARGET init, ATTACK, SKILL and ESCAPE always reach
a deep callee first (ATTACK at the strike / record packets 0x2BACB0 / 0x2D7970, SKILL at 0x2E3560 / 0x2BB050 / 0x285F80,
ESCAPE at the sound driver 0x2DCFB0 / 0x2DD180, REVIVAL init at libc's __sinit through sprintf, UNIT_CREATE init at the
action creation). Slice: **2 cases, 131,544 assertions** (9,600 pairs, 384 whole-RAM compares; rules: 162 REVIVAL waits,
324 command waits, 187 whole-side target copies) on MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/battle_actions-msvc`) and on clang-cl
Release (`build/battle_actions-clang`). The battle replay route runs 12 of the 16 bodies (a temporary first-hit probe, not
committed: both UNIT_CREATE, both UNIT_LOAD, COMMAND init / update, TARGET init / update, SKILL, WIN, CONDITION, END); ATTACK,
ESCAPE and both REVIVAL bodies rest on the pairs only.

**A lesson for the callee lists.** The test build's emitted set is shared by every test file: emitting more callees makes
other slices' pairs run deeper. The first gate run (all 16 functions, then 481 callees) had dorm / M1 / battle at 0 bytes
but failed 3 cases of other slices -- ui2 expects printf 0x5225A8 to be a missing-function stop, and battle_task's TEST /
EXIT pairs went into trees (sub_1FDD40 ...) whose writes leave their restored windows. The list was cut back (no printf,
file loading, sound driver or kernel wrappers, no sub_1FDD40 tree) until the whole p3fes_game_tests passed.

**Suites and gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Repo <worktree> -Tree build\battle_actions-gate -ClangTree
build\battle_actions-clang -Jobs 3 -FastGs`, base `24e1fe2`, 1,172 replaced): ctest 16 / 16 on MSVC 14.44 Release and on
clang-cl Release; `p3fes_game_tests` **256 cases / 36,396,443 assertions** on both; dorm `EE0EB5DA...795D85`, M1
`E3A93615...B672`, battle `CFAA5A61...F606`, all 0 differing bytes / 0 runs, gsMemory identical: **GATE: PASSED** (991.6 s).
## battle_calc2 (Phase 5 slice): the battle data / calculation band 0x2D0000-0x31FFFF, second pass -- 97 functions

**What.** `game/src/battle/battle_calc2.cpp` (`battle_calc2.h`): the pure functions of the targeting / efficacy /
support band (btlTarget*, btlEfficacy.c, btlSupport.c: 0x2D1570-0x2DD9B0) and of the boss-rule band (btlBoss*,
btlBossElizabeth.c: 0x2DD9B0-0x2FF260), leaf-first: 81 leaves, 12 functions whose callees are all replaced already
(`datCalcChkBadStatus`, `datCalcGetLevel`, `datCalcRand`, `sub_17D800`, `datCalcGetBadStatus`, `datCalcIsDead`,
`sub_302380`, `datCalcClearEffect`, `datCalcGetEffectState`, K_Assert) and the four `nullsub`s of the band. The
datUnit / datCalc / datScript bands (0x2FF260-0x311310) were already complete but for four heap users.
Proposed names (12, ours, evidence per row): `symbols/deltas/battle_calc2.sym` (`btlTargetGetSideMask`,
`btlGetMeanLevel`, `btlCountActiveUnits`, `btlGetEncounterId`, `datCalcIsHpSkill`, the `btlSupport*` flag / queue /
timer helpers, `btlBossResetCounters`).

**Findings.** (1) The btlTarget at action +56 holds the target *actions*; its count u16 +50 is action +106, and every
"any target result ..." scan loops to the count registers (`slt` against the u16 +106 and the result count byte
+200, never a constant).
(2) The support line pickers (table 0x6978F0, called by `sub_2DAA20` as `fn(a0, a1, a2, 0)`) compare gBtl +0x148 with
the action in `$a0` (`bne v0, a0`), i.e. "this action is gBtl's current action", not with the constant 4. (3)
`sub_2E33F0` returns the compare constant for enemies 233 / 234 (the case blocks are a bare branch). (4) `sub_2D63B0`
tests SkillRecord kind == 1 (HP), like `datCalcIsHpSkill`; only 61 of the 464 SKILL.TBL records have kind 1. (5) The support
timers reset at "3 or more" (`slti 3`), so a timer already at 3 resets on the next tick. (6) `sub_2FDED0` returns the
address of `btlBossResetCounters` (a callback for its caller) and `sub_2FC410` the boss records 0x69A0E8 / 0x69A5A8.

**Not taken** (left recompiled): btlAction* / btlMain* and their state helpers (slice battle_actions), the BF COMM
handlers of the band (the comm_* slices), `datUnitCreatePc` / `datUnitCreateEc` / `datUnitDestroyGenus` /
`sub_2FF260` (RwHeapMalloc / the free hook at 0x96017C through `jalr` / kwlnTaskCreate), `btlBossSetup` (sprintf), the
float camera / VU0 code (0x2D1DE0-0x2D41C0, the boss cameras) and the model manager (0x311310-0x31FFFF, render
pipeline setters).

**Cycle-model notes.** All loops are test-first: the first test runs without a check, every later passing test is
followed by the back-edge check. The two-stage early exits (`return 1` from inside an inner loop) charge the case block
and the shared 2-cycle exit block. The id chains (`sub_2D5B50`, `sub_2E33F0`, `sub_2F9690`, `sub_2FDED0`) charge 3 per
compare block after the entry block and 2 for the fall-through jump; `sub_2FCF50` and `sub_2FD060` differ only in the
id test's miss path (a 2-cycle jump block in the first, a direct branch in the second).

**Battle route coverage** (a temporary call counter in the shims, built once into the gate tree after the gate and
removed; the battle replay to vblank 6150): 44 of the 97 run -- the support timers `btlSupportTickTimers` (763 calls, every
frame), `sub_2FD7C0` (688), `sub_2F8840` / `nullsub_20` (763), the encounter id, the target-result scans, the +160
counters, `btlCountActiveUnits`, `sub_2D3FE0`, the SKILL.TBL readers, `sub_2DC130` / `sub_2DC550`, `btlSupportRequestLine` / `btlSupportTestFlag`,
the side helpers `sub_2FDCF0` / `sub_2FDD40` and the non-boss paths of `sub_2FC410` / `sub_2F9560` / `sub_2FDED0` /
`sub_2E33F0`; the boss-only rules are covered by the pair tests.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_battle_calc2.cpp`): two machines in lockstep from one random battle world per three
pairs (gBtl, the setup block with boss / random encounter ids, 8 btlActions with target lists and results, 8 btlUnits,
8 DatUnits, 8 model records, the real SKILL / EFFECT / MODEL.TBL sections); every pair compares all GPRs in 128 bits,
HI/LO, the register file and cycles at every check point, the dead and live stack, the bus log, the scratchpad, the
world and the gp window; the whole 32 MiB every 64 pairs. 240 pairs per function (23,280), documented-rule checks
(the side mask, the support flag bit, `sub_2E33F0`'s codes, `sub_2F8EB0`'s elements, the timer reset / tick,
`sub_2FDED0`'s callback) and every skill id through `datCalcIsHpSkill` / `sub_2D4CC0` against the table bytes. Six planted
mutations (a `blez` -> `bltz` boundary in `sub_2D5FB0`, one cycle in `btlSupportTickTimers`, a table bit in `sub_2D63B0`, the s0
spill dropped from `sub_2F8EB0`'s frame, a constant loop bound in `btlTargetGetSideMask`, a scratch register swapped in
`btlSupportTestFlag`) were each caught (4 .. 1,236 failing checks) and reverted.
Slice: 3 cases, 24,233 pairs, **1,698,633 assertions** on both compilers. `p3fes_game_tests` **284 cases / 40,279,360
assertions** on MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/battle_calc2-gate`) and clang-cl (`build/battle_calc2-clang`).

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build/battle_calc2-gate -ClangTree build/battle_calc2-clang -Jobs 3 -FastGs`,
base `0010062`, 1,409 replaced): ctest 16/16 on both compilers, dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85` 0 bytes, M1 `E3A93615…B672`

## Phase 5: rendering -- RenderWare's core and the sky driver, third pass (render_core3, 2026-10-21)

**What.** 77 functions (28,324 bytes) hand-written in `game/src/render/core3.cpp` / `game/include/p3fes/game/core3.h`
and gated with `tests/game/test_render_core3.cpp`: the class-a rows of queue_rendering.txt tagged [rwcore] (30, 7,764
bytes), [rt2d] (25, 9,564), [raster] (10, 5,400), [upload] (3, 2,084), [renderstate] (1, 1,708), [im3d] (3, 900) and
[rxheap] (5, 904) that were not replaced yet and not taken by render_sky / render_world. Roles per function in
core3.h; the group overview at its top.

**Not taken.** Own-body calls through the engine's memory function pointers (0x960178 RwMalloc, 0x96017C RwFree,
0x960180 RwRealloc, 0x960188 / 0x96018C the freelists): `sub_4AB0E0`, `sub_4C1E70`, `sub_4C47E0`, `sub_4C4930`,
`sub_4CBF20`, `sub_4CC1D0`, `sub_4E4E90`, `sub_4F61C0` (the RxHeap block growth is a RwRealloc user, so the RxHeap
allocator is taken only where it bumps a game-owned block: `sub_4F3150`), and `sub_4EFA00` (also DIntr / EIntr around
the texture-cache allocator). Left for a later slice for size: the raster lock `sub_4DE0A0` (3,132 B, 26 loops, the
GS store-image path: sceGsSetDefStoreImage / sceGsExecStoreImage / sceGsSyncPath / sceDmaGetChan) and the raster
blits `sub_4E53E0` / `sub_4E6D60` / `sub_4E8610` (6,520 / 6,312 / 4,208 B, 42 / 68 / 37 loops, the texture cache,
DIntr / EIntr and the DMA packet layer). No function of the groups has hardware registers, syscalls or printf in its
own body; none has a mid-body entry.

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) The RW engine instance is 0x960070: device functions +16 (RenderStateSet 0x960090 /
Get 0x960094 = `sub_4D78B0`, Im2D 0x960098..), the 29 standard functions from 0x9600B8 (begin update 0x9600BC, end
0x9600E0, raster lock 0x9600F4 = `sub_4DE0A0`, unlock 0x9600F8 = `sub_4DECE0`, show raster 0x960108, camera clear
0x96010C, palette lock / unlock 0x960114 / 0x960118), the dirty-frame list 0x96012C, the string functions
0x960134.., the memory functions 0x960178... (2) The matrix combine ops continue after RWERROR for a bad op with a
null matrix (they update the flags word at address 12). (3) The resource heap is first fit from a hint that free moves
back and allocation moves forward; blocks > size + 64 are split. (4) `sub_4D78B0`'s blend states are valid only while
the ALPHA shadow equals the 6 x 6 table word (0x77EF80) for the two blend shadows, which index it unchecked. (5) The
swizzles move 4-row bands through 4 KiB (PSMT8) / 2 KiB (PSMT4) frame buffers, rows r / r + 2 through the HI/LO pipes
0 / 1. (6) Rt2d: the CTM stack 0x95EDF0 / depth 0x95EE70 (31 deep), the device matrix 0x95EF10 rebuilt when 0x95EF50
is clear, the tolerance 0x95EF60 when 0x95EF64 is set; the flattened path's normals are averaged pairwise.

**Cycle-model notes.** Blocks with `jal` / `jalr` are charged in full before the call. Many "back-edges" are forward
gotos to shared tails placed earlier (the RwFrame dirty link, the device-call success paths, the CTM slot creation,
`sub_4D78B0`'s five out-of-line stores before its return block, the scissor cuts, the Rt2d dirty pushes): each is an
explicit `backedge()` on that path only. `sub_4D78B0`'s two `jr` tables are switches over the loaded target with the
per-case cost and the generated fallback. The byte loads' unsigned-to-float idiom (`u2f`) charges 3 / 7 by the sign
test even though a byte never takes the 7.

**An MSVC slip.** MSVC 14.44 /O2 kept `ctx.cycles` in a host register across a call to a small, non-inlined leaf
helper that charges (the combine-op dispatch of `sub_4C33D0`: its 3 / 5 / 7 cycles were lost; the pair tests caught
it). core3.cpp's Cpu reads GPRs and updates the cycle count through volatile lvalues (a compiler barrier under
/volatile:ms), so no guest state is cached across a helper. clang-cl showed nothing.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_core3.cpp`, 19 cases): every pair compares all GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, SA, all
FPRs, ACC, FCR31, VU0, the register file and cycles at every check point, the bus log, the scratchpad, the world, the
gp window, the RW window 0x95E000..0x962000, low memory, the whole stack window, plus the case's own windows (the
deep stack of the swizzles, the execution globals 0x965A80.., the VU constant block, the DMA windows). Device /
plugin function pointers aim at callbacks of the emitted set (identity, `v0 = a1`, 1, 0, a non-leaf that spills
$ra). Real game state: the battle (6150) and dorm (4900) snapshots run the render-state getter on every state, the
Rt2d CTM / device matrix / tolerance, RwFrameGetLTM on the Rt2d camera, the VU constants, the frame-buffer binding
and allocate / free on the live resource heap, the whole RAM compared through a `PairRange`. Mutations planted
one at a time (a block charge, a dropped back-edge, a store offset, a shift, a mask, a swapped byte, a threshold, a
leftover scratch register, a skipped DMA qword, a wrong extent): all 10 caught (the DMA one after the test also
compared the half-buffer top that `sub_4D5FE0` reserves from).
Slice: 19 cases, 42,570 pairs (incl. 110 on the two snapshots); **3,461,025 assertions** on MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/render_core3-msvc`), **3,461,035** on clang-cl Release (`build/render_core3-clangr`; the rng draws
inside some argument lists run in a compiler-dependent order). `p3fes_game_tests` in the gate: **330 cases / 44,380,136 assertions** (MSVC) and 44,380,146 (clang-cl), 39 ctest entries.

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Repo <worktree> -Tree build/render_core3-gate -ClangTree build/render_core3-clangr -Jobs 3 -FastGs`, base `2f74901`, 1,546 replaced): ctest 54/54 on both compilers, dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85` 0 bytes,
M1 `E3A93615…B672` 0 bytes, battle `CFAA5A61…F606` 0 bytes, gsMemory identical in all three: **GATE: PASSED**.

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) op_res flags bit 0 / 1 are "request pending": state 0 waits for `sub_266D70() == 0`,
state 6 for `sub_266AE0() == 0`. (2) The title menu wraps 0 -> 3 on up and 3 -> 0 on down; reaching 0 (up) or 3 (down)
sets flags bit 3, which holds the menu until up / down are released on both pad words. (3) `sub_26DA90` / `sub_26DB30`
store 8 then 0 into the new item's state (both stores kept). (4) The recompiled loads / stores stop at an unaligned or
unmapped address where `guest::load` reads 0: title.cpp's accessors route such an address through the same rt op
(with `$zero`), so a wild pointer stops both bodies at the same place.

(gp-18912) init / shutdown / fill `sub_234A00` / open / close / step; `bpIfontSetDigitQuad`; brp_birth.c (gp-18880)
set-up / start / update `sub_24ADF0` (2,728 B) / draw; bai_main.c's banner (`sub_24C110`, 2,952 B; gp-18872).
**Skipped** (file I/O, brief step 7): the H_Cdvd_Request loaders `sub_2339D0` (br_base.bin), `sub_233B20`
(br_level.bin), `sub_233C00` (br_lvh.bin), `sub_24BE40` (brp_birth.bin), `sub_24BF80` (msg_combine.bmd). The queue's
22 skip-class rows (heap / printf) were not listed. None of the slice's addresses were in `game/replaced.txt` before.

**How.** The bodies run on a Cpu view (`battle_result::Cpu`, one named variable per guest register, as ptank / sky).
They were transliterated from the recompiled blocks by a scratch converter (`rt::` call -> Cpu statement, `ctx.cycles
+= N` -> charge, back-edge `check_events` -> backedge, `rt::jal` + call -> `jal`), structured automatically where the
shapes are plain (if-skips, if / else, test-first and test-last loops; the switch bodies keep their labels), then
documented. Loads and stores are the instruction's own form (`lw(rt, base, imm)`) through the runtime's `rt::lw` /
`rt::sw` .., so the recompiled body's address-error / unmapped faults, the hardware-bus routing and the BIOS window
behave identically (a value-returning `guest::load` would not fault where the recompiled body stops). The nine `jr`
tables (0x7B70E0, 0x7B7170, 0x7B7140, 0x7B71D0, 0x7B71A0, 0x7B7200, 0x7B78C0, 0x7B7890, 0x7B7860) are read from guest
memory and dispatched on the target, as the originals.

**Cycle-model notes.** Nothing unusual: entry check point + first block, a charge per block, a check point on every
backward jump (the loops, `sub_1FB3F0` / `sub_1FBD50`'s table walks, and `sub_1F0D70`'s retry jumps back to its
compare chain). A block that ends in a `jal` is charged before the call.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_battle_result.cpp`, 3 cases; every pair compares the whole register file -- GPRs in
128 bits, HI/LO, SA, FPRs, ACC, FCR31 -- and the cycle count at every check point and at the return or the
missing-function stop, the whole 32 MiB of main RAM through a PairRange, the scratchpad, and the BIOS window): 6,230
random-world pairs (70 worlds x 89 functions; 65 functions also return normally, the other 24 always reach a big
callee that the test build does not emit first), 801 pairs on the battle_ref_6150 / b_5800 / dorm_replay_4900
snapshots (the result root is live in battle_ref_6150), and the documented rules (the root's flags, the page reset,
the result-work getter, `sub_1F1DF0`'s list, the br_res accessors, the panel open / step, `sub_1FB3F0` against a host
scan, `sub_1F9D70`'s flags against a host decode of jump table 0x7B70E0). Slice: **3 cases, 59,547 assertions** (MSVC 14.44 Release) / **59,542** (clang-cl Release; the random draws differ by compiler in argument evaluation order). The test build also emits 32 leaf
callees (g_data / item accessors, 2D helpers, `sub_3B2C60`; no printf, file, sound or kernel code): the whole
`p3fes_game_tests` stays green with them. Mutations: a cycle count (`sub_1F0C40`), a dropped FPR spill
(`sub_1FBDF0`), a behaviour constant (`sub_24C110`'s SFX frame) and a scratch register (`sub_233D70`) each fail.
Harness lessons: a stray store through a random pointer can land in the BIOS window (any address folding onto
0x1FC00000..), which no RAM range covers -- the pairs check it and leave it zero; and a body walking random data without
end is cut at 20,000 check points in both runs and compared there.

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build/battle_result-gate -ClangTree build/battle_result-clang -FastGs -Jobs 3`, base `2f74901`, 1,558 replaced): ctest 54/54 on both compilers, `p3fes_game_tests` **314 cases / 40,978,658 assertions** (MSVC) and **314 / 40,978,653** (clang-cl), dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85` 0 bytes, M1 `E3A93615…B672` 0 bytes, battle `CFAA5A61…F606` 0 bytes, gsMemory identical in all three: **GATE: PASSED**.

render_sky and render_core3 hold were left alone.

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) RW globals (0x960070): +0 camera, +4 world, +8 frame stamp, +144 the render-state setter,
+344 strcmp, +376.. the heap; the point-transform table at gp-17376 (+8 = `sub_4E3EC0`) is runtime data (zero in the ELF
image: synthetic tests set it). (2) `sub_46BAB0` / `sub_46BD00` (queue tag [skin]) are Rt2d path draws (pipelines
0x95F040 / 0x95F050). (3) The three PDS 2D set-ups are one compiled body (template 0x6B5790 / 0x6B58E0 / 0x6B5A30, mode
6 / 6 / 4); the Im3D, PDS 2D and sector set-ups share the matrix and the prim / transType sequences block for block.
(4) `ps2AllMatClusterLayout`'s second passes run over 12 entries: the 10 streams plus the two pseudo-streams it writes at +112 /
+120. (5) The resEntry: header at +24 (+8 data, +24 vertices per cluster, +28 clusters, +36 count), 24-byte stream
records from +144 (+0 / +4 counts, +8 / +12 offsets, +16 / +18 strides, +20 back-step; the second morph target at
+388..). (6) The snapshots hold freed atomics whose frames are stale (live: the frame's root is its own root).

**Cycle-model notes.** Each body follows its recompiled blocks; the big builders keep the compiler's 128-bit frame
temporaries (`sq` of registers whose upper halves are stale). Jump tables (`ps2AllMatClusterLayout` x4, `ps2AllInstanceSizes`,
`ps2AllInstanceDmaChain`, `sub_4A35C0`) are C++ switches on the loaded entry with the per-case costs and the generated fallback; one
`ps2AllMatClusterLayout` table entry is the loop's own continuation (no case cost). Loop exits are not uniform: the instancers'
per-stream cluster loops end in 2, 1 or 0 extra blocks by stream, the packed / unpacked normal loops differ by one block
before the loop, the colour fill / prelit paths differ again. Forward "back-edges" (out-of-line blocks returning
through a check point): the default-pipeline picks, the sector -> world search, the shared tails of the set-ups and
the tri-strip walk.

Im3D / sector / atomic stream layouts with every stream type; real data: the battle and dorm snapshots' 296 meshes

callbacks, `ps2AllInstanceSizes`, `ps2AllInstanceDmaChain`, `ps2AllMatClusterLayout`, the skin weights on the resEntry just built), 131 live atomics and

## Phase 5: battle -- the battle command menu, bcm_main.c (battle_cmd_menu, 2026-10-21)

**What.** All 95 listed functions of the wave-10 slice `battle_cmd_menu` (queue_bands.txt; 0x1FF890-0x208AC4,
27,308 bytes), hand-written in `game/src/battle/battle_cmd_menu.cpp` / `game/include/p3fes/game/battle_cmd_menu.h`
(roles in brackets; every function keeps its functions.json `sub_*` name): the 30,644-byte menu record at
`$gp-18952` (`sub_201730` create, `sub_201780` destroy, `sub_1FFC60` teardown) and its five lists -- skills, items,
personas, tactics / targets, analyze rows -- each with its opener (`sub_202010`, `sub_202D70`, `sub_203850`,
`sub_204480`, `sub_206740`: collect the entries, place the remembered cursor with flag 390 / `sub_16F380`, open the
panel window), font-line builder, refresher (window, cursor row in style 6, the help line through `sub_3A5540` /
`sub_2082C0`), releaser and panel filler; the availability checks that grey out SKILL / ITEM / PERSONA
(`sub_201EF0`, `sub_202C90`, `sub_203760`), the top menu's icon bits (`sub_201880`, jump table 0x7B7330), the tactics
rows (`sub_204000`, jump table 0x7B7350 by pc id; "All Members" / members with `0x684F00` tactic names / "Support"),
the analyze-row confirmation (`sub_207340`), the navigator comments (`sub_208860`, jump table 0x7B73B0;
`sub_208790`), the queries, flag setters and debug switches (+30624). Skipped: none of the 95. The slice block's six
skip-class bodies (`sub_1FF890`, `sub_1FFF40`, `sub_202830`, `sub_203630`, `sub_2057C0`, `sub_2063F0`: printf) stay
recompiled, as do the battle panel's `sub_1FF430` .. `sub_1FF7F0` (unassigned slice) that these call.

**How.** Register-faithful bodies on `bcm::Cpu` (one variable per guest register; loads and stores through the
runtime's `rt::lw` / `rt::sw` ... so alignment faults and unmapped reads behave as in the recompiled code), written
block by block from the disassembly with the ADR-0013 block costs read off a block map cross-checked against every
`ctx.cycles += N` of the generated bodies (all 95 matched). The code is -O0-like (every delay slot a nop), so the
register state at each call / check point is the obvious one; idioms are helpers (`need_work` for the 86 "work !=
NULL" checks, `check` for the built-bit assertions, `glyphs_open/close`, `build_line`, `line_finish`,
`line_row_pos`, `drop_help` / `new_help`, `release_built_lists`, `reopen_windows`, `target_row_lines`). Jump tables
are read from guest memory and dispatched on the loaded target (unknown targets go to `rt::lookup_func`).

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) The record's +0 bits: 2 / 4 / 8 / 0x10 / 0x1000 / 0x2000 = skill / item / persona /
target / tactic / analyze lines built, 0x800000 help line, 0x80 / 0x100 / 0x400 a command greyed out, 0x20000000
suspended under a dialog; +12 = the selectable commands. (2) The navigator's "again" line needs the flag
`0x697BD8[pc id]`; ids 9 and 10 hold -1 in retail, so their "again" blocks are dead (the test gives them a flag).
(3) `sub_204760` / `sub_205000` keep a stale `$s3` / `$s4` line for a "Support" row in menu mode 2 (after the
assertion), and `sub_207E20` passes the caller's `$s1` for an unknown encounter -- reproduced. (4) `sub_208790` does
`divu` by the member count (0 possible) -- through `rt::divu`.

**Cycle-model notes.** Loop tests come last (`b test`), so `backedge()` follows the test block; the last case of
`sub_208860` falls through into the epilogue (3 cycles, not 5); the item-row blocks of `sub_203030` / `sub_203410`
cost 16 / 14 by row; `sub_201880`'s last icon case has no `b` (1 cycle).

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_battle_cmd_menu.cpp`, 5 cases): every pair compares the whole register file and
cycles at every check point and at the return / missing-function stop, all 32 MiB of RAM (PairRange) and the
scratchpad. Worlds: the b_5800 battle snapshot (the menu is open; its record's unbuilt lists sanitised, the RW raster
path emitted so glyph-cache misses run through) with the record's scalars randomised and recompiled builders run as
preludes before releasers / refreshers / panel fillers (40 pairs per function), and a synthetic world (60 per
function); documented rules (bit setters, the selected skill / item / persona, the skill-table predicate for ids
0..469, the cursor record); a navigator sweep (every id 0..12, flag set / clear, the -1 ids given flags). The emitted
callee closure covers the font layer, the RW raster / heap path, the 0x16C-0x17D readers and datCalc; the panel
windows, the help-line message tags and the sound / CD paths are compared stops. 79,868 assertions on both compilers.
Mutations (five, one at a time or together): a style constant in `sub_2024B0`, a block cost in `sub_204000`, `$v1`
not left masked in the three operation setters, the 3-cycle fall-through of `sub_208860`, the 223-item bound of
`sub_202C90` -- each fails its function.

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build/battle_cmd_menu-gate -ClangTree build/battle_cmd_menu-clang -FastGs
-Jobs 3`, base `b37e056`, 1,418 replaced): ctest 51/51 on both compilers, `p3fes_game_tests` 295 cases /
39,008,199 assertions on MSVC and clang-cl Release; dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85` 0 bytes, M1 `E3A93615…B672` 0 bytes,

**What.** `game/src/battle/battle_panel.cpp` (`battle_panel.h`): every listed function of the slice block in
`docs/ANALYSIS/queue_bands.txt` (0x1FC720-0x1FF888, 0x21C9F0-0x21EC38), none skipped: pb_main.c (the party / persona
picks `sub_1FC720`, `sub_1FC870`, `sub_1FCCC0`, `sub_1FCE20`, `sub_1FD350`), bp_root.c (the "battle panel" / "battle
panel draw" task updates `bpRoot_UpdateBattlePanelTask` / `bpRoot_UpdateBattlePanelDrawTask`, the setters / testers of the panel mode word and the command
record `sub_1FDF10`, the dialog request `sub_1FE650`, the item list `sub_1FE810`, the message triples `sub_1FEF90` /
`sub_1FF160`, 45 16-byte wrappers), bp_misc.c (the unit-list searches over gBtl +336 and the story-flag layout
`sub_1FF740`) and the 2D sprite helpers (uv rects with anchor modes `sub_21CD00` / `sub_21CEC0`, the 4-vertex strip
fillers `sub_21D3B0` / `sub_21E380`, corners / colours / z / uv, the rotated quad `sub_21E170` with atan2f / sinf / cosf,
the depth `sub_21EA00`). Not taken (the block's skip-class line, not in the list): `sub_1FC980` / `sub_1FCB30` (printf),
`bpRoot_CreateBattlePanelTasks` / `sub_1FDC00` / `sub_21C9F0` / `sub_21CC20` (heap); the replaced callers (`sub_1FC720`, the wrapper
`sub_1FDBE0`) call them recompiled.

**Findings.** (1) `sub_1FC720` reads `$v1` and `$s0` before writing them (`div v1, 3` compared with `v1`, `30 * s0 /
100` compared with `s0`); the hand version reproduces the reads. (2) The jump tables are not in label order: 0x7B7230
sends the command menu's state 3 to the K_Assert case (0 -> 1, 1 -> 2, 2 -> 3, 4 -> 5, 5 -> 6, 6 -> 7); 0x7B7250 /
0x7B7280 send cases 0, 1 and 6 to the K_Assert label, which hands `$s0..$s2` to `sub_25BE60` as they came. (3)
`sub_21CEC0` with a mode >= 8 keeps the incoming `$t0` as its u mode and the mode itself as its v mode; `sub_21E380` with
a mode >= 8 keeps `$s2..$s5` (the colour sources) and the frame's uv words as they were. (4) `sub_1FF630` inlines
`sub_1FF5B0` (count - 1, counted down to a0). (5) The command menu's work is the pointer at `$gp - 18952` itself (+0
flags, +36 state, +30360 index), not a task's +60. (6) The `bltz` half of the unsigned-to-float idiom is dead for the
`lbu` colour bytes (never negative) but is kept with its registers.

**Cycle-model notes.** Loops are test-first (`for (;;) { charge(test); if (!cond) break; backedge(); ... }`) except the
8-byte stack clears of `sub_21CD00` / `sub_21CEC0` (body-first, 7 per byte, guarded by a never-taken `beqz`). Join
blocks that end in a branch cost 2 more than the same block falling through (`sub_1FCE20`'s kind tails 10 / 12, the
uv cases 13 / 9 of `sub_21CD00` against 13 / 13 of `sub_21CEC0`). The unsigned-to-float idiom is a 5 / 7 pair of blocks;
each colour store opens a block of 4. A `jr` target outside a switch's labels goes to `rt::lookup_func` without the
epilogue (`Frame::dismiss`), as the generated body does.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_battle_panel.cpp`): one machine, the whole 32 MiB restored between the bodies through
a PairRange and compared after both, the scratchpad too; the whole register file (GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, SA, FPRs,

command menu's work, stand-in tasks for the callees' slots, a sprite set (16 records, 4 pages), entry lists, a command

compared stop), the same pairs on the battle snapshot b_5800 (1,290: the live panel task, work and gBtl; the unit

`sub_3C4650`, `sub_3C49E0`, `sub_3C4A90`, `sub_3C4F30`, `sub_3C4FC0` (the brief's heap rule). No mid-body entries,
hardware, syscalls or printf in the slice.

**Registers / memory.** Register-faithful Cpu view (as core3.cpp, with its volatile GPR / cycle accesses copied into the
header: the wave-10 MSVC lesson). New here: guest memory goes through the runtime's own load / store instructions
(rt::lw .. rt::sq with $zero as the base and the address as the offset; a load is written `reg = lw(address)` and
performed into that register by the assignment), so an access the original faults on -- unaligned, unmapped -- stops the
run the same way, and a hardware-window access would reach the bus with its check point. The first version used
guest::load / store (no alignment check): the pair tests caught a random list whose cursor pointed at an odd address --
the recompiled body stopped with an address error, the hand one went on.

**Cycle-model notes.** The band was compiled without delay-slot scheduling (every slot a nop), so the bodies follow
the instructions in order. Test-first loops charge the test block, then take the check point before each pass.
`nmCmdListStatus / nmCmdListStatus28` (same logic, different block layouts: the second's arms branch straight to its tail) and the
two inlined copies of the cursor-down body inside `sub_3C63F0` (5 vs 3 cycles on the flag store) keep their own charges.
Quirks kept: `sub_3C5490` resumes its pending / finished walks after the successor `nmListUnlink` returned, so that step is
not counted down on that frame; `sub_3C72D0` re-initialises the record before testing it, so its "already open" path is
dead; `sub_3C7070`'s linear branch reads `$f5`, which nothing in the function writes; `nmListCursorSeek(-1)` returns the tail
without moving the cursor.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_nm_message.cpp`, 11 cases): random node lists (sometimes with a wrong count, cursor or
flag word), list objects, nmSequence step lists, nmCmdList windows with their rows, the pad words, the record 0x95BE90
and the itfMesMng slot table; callbacks aimed at emitted leaves (0x3C4400, identity, `v0 = a1`, 1) and a non-leaf
(0x1F1C50) that spills $ra below its $sp, which also stands in for RwHeapMalloc. Every pair compares all GPRs in 128
bits, HI/LO, all FPRs, ACC, FCR31 at the return, the register file and cycles at every check point, the whole 32 MiB of
RAM (PairRange), the dead stack, the scratchpad and the bus log; FPRs / HI / LO and the unused argument registers start
random. A callee the test build does not emit (the itfMesMng window code behind printf, the sprite draw sub_3B2CB0)
stops both runs with a fatal event, compared at that point (pc, message, machine state). Real snapshots: battle 6150,
b_5800, dorm 4900 and M1 (the record -- handle 20 on the dorm route -- and the three live nm list objects, found by their
default callbacks). Callees added to the shared list: 0x3C4400 / 0x3C4410 / 0x3C4420, the eight heap functions, qsort
0x5225F8 and acosf with __ieee754_acosf / __ieee754_sqrtf (no printf, I/O, sound or kernel code). Mutations planted one at
a time (a block charge, a dropped back-edge, a store offset, a pad mask, a leftover scratch register, a constant, two FPU
operands swapped, the sequence walk quirk, a jal link value, a signed / unsigned compare, a missing FPR spill, a 64-bit
compare made 32-bit): all 12 caught (the leftover register only after the unused argument registers were randomised).
Slice: 11 cases, 8,194 pairs, **637,021 assertions** on MSVC 14.44 Release (`build/nm_message-msvc`) and on clang-cl
Release (`build/nm_message-clang`).

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Repo <worktree> -Tree build/nm_message-gate -ClangTree build/nm_message-clang -Jobs 3 -FastGs`, base `26b289a`, 2,028 replaced): ctest 60/60 on both compilers, `p3fes_game_tests` **372 cases / 46,586,113 assertions** (MSVC) and 46,586,118 (clang-cl), 45 ctest entries; dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85` 0 bytes,
M1 `E3A93615…B672` 0 bytes, battle `CFAA5A61…F606` 0 bytes, gsMemory identical in all three: **GATE: PASSED**.

## Phase 5 slice tartarus: the Tartarus field band of the Y map code (115 functions, 87,868 bytes)

`game/src/field/tartarus_smap.cpp` (36: the mini-map's leaves, cell offsets, layer / mark / sparkle drawers, the
seen-cells grid 0x95C110, "y_staire_disp_proc" `Y_SMap_UpdateStaireDispTask`, "y_smap mask draw " `Y_SMap_UpdateSmapMaskDrawTask`, the time-limit display
`Y_TimeLimit_UpdateTimeLimitDrawTask`), `tartarus_stratum.cpp` (13: the stratum title's drawing helpers and an Im2D wobble vertex),
`tartarus_ene.cpp` (33: "ene think proc" `Y_Stratum_UpdateEneThinkTask` with the roam / wander / chase / contact states, the path search
`sub_453ED0` / `sub_4534B0` / `sub_4514A0`, the sight checks, the Reaper's far room `sub_452010`), `tartarus_sym.cpp`
(33: the movement helpers, the step list `sub_453D90`, the enemy-dead effect `Y_Stratum_UpdateEneDeadEffectTask`, the symbol-direction marker,
the units' status bytes, the party members' mode / skill-use helpers, the Kyoto NPC slots); header
`game/include/p3fes/game/tartarus.h`, register view `game/src/field/tartarus_cpu.h`. Every listed function of the slice
block of `docs/ANALYSIS/queue_bands.txt` but one: `sub_4302B0` stays recompiled (file I/O: it loads the mini-map's
sprite / tmx files through `H_Cdvd_Request` / `H_Cdvd_ReadSync` / `H_Cdvd_Destroy` at init). `Y_StParts_UpdateStratumPartsTask` and the
field layer's own Tartarus code were left alone, as asked.

**Method.** Each body is written on a register view of the guest (`Cpu`: one proxy per GPR; loads / stores, the FPU, HI/LO
and the MMI byte add through the runtime's own `rt::` accessors, so the fast and slow memory paths and every flag are the
original's), with structured control flow, the original's frame and spills, `$ra` = the original link at every `jal`, and
the jump tables as C++ switches (`default:` = the out-of-table `jr`, as the generated body). Repeated bodies share
parameterised helpers (the cell offsets, the party / shadow marks, the frame handles, the seen-room marking). Comments
give each function's role and the work-record fields from the instructions and the callers.

**Cycle model notes.** A block containing a `jal` is charged whole before the call; loops whose test block comes first
check before every iteration (`backedge()` after the test); a two-level `goto` out of nested loops (`sub_452F70`'s stair
search) keeps a label (`found:`), because a `break` would leave only the inner loop -- the pair tests caught the first
version; nested jump tables (`sub_44B7D0`, `sub_44AF60`) keep the outer cases as `case` labels.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_tartarus.cpp`): one machine per case, the whole 32 MiB of RAM through a PairRange plus
the scratchpad compared after both bodies, the whole register file (GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, SA, FPRs, ACC, FCR31) and
the cycles at every check point and at the return or the missing-function stop. Inputs: synthetic records (stratum parts
work, stratum record, think works, tasks) with randomised fields, and the battle route's Tartarus snapshots b_6700 /
b_5800 (the live "ene think proc", "y_smap draw proc", "y_smap mask draw ", "y_staire_disp_proc", "smap_symbol_dirp"
tasks found by a scan for their update callbacks; states, sub-states, targets, flags, the grid's open sides and room
bytes and the seen grid varied). Documented-rule checks: `sub_44F120` / `sub_44F170` (`(int)((x + 400) / 800)`),
`sub_4311F0` (`800 x, 0, 800 z`), `sub_42BA30`, `sub_430220` / `sub_430270`, `sub_449C90` (the first match of the 30
title records), `sub_457410` (the first free NPC slot), the eight party-mode setters (mode 0..7). **9,484 pairs** (2,736
compared at a missing-function stop: `sprCreateHandle` (RW heap), the collision ray `sub_1ACC30`, the task creators).
Callees added to the shared `_callees` list (no printf / file / sound / kernel / `sub_1FDD40` code): the door lookup
`sub_1BF220`, the RW free list `_rwFreeListAllocReal` / `_rwFreeListFreeReal` (behind RwMatrixCreate / Destroy), the
NPC-band readers `sub_433810`, `sub_435260`, `sub_4352E0`, `sub_4353F0`, `sub_43C730`, `sub_43A230`, `sub_437E20`,
`sub_435060`, `sub_43A1A0`, `sub_43C910` (+ `sub_16C5F0`), the area map's `sub_423FE0`, `sub_4221A0`, `sub_4222D0`,
`sub_421FE0`, `sub_422C30` / `sub_422C90` / `sub_422C10`, the time-limit drawers `sub_45A490` / `sub_45ACE0`, the
sinf / cosf wrappers `sub_269C80` / `sub_269CA0`, the field-event readers `sub_1C6D70` / `sub_1C6DD0` / `sub_1C65E0` /
`sub_1C6450` / `sub_1C6200` (+ acosf 0x52E9E8 / 0x52ABD8 / 0x52C398), `K_Battle_FindTaskOfUnit`,
`K_FldEvent_IsUnitHero`, `sub_1AAAC0`; the whole `p3fes_game_tests` stayed green with them (ctest 45/45 before the last

## Phase 5: battle -- the effect packets and the command effects (battle_fx, 2026-10-21)

**What.** 118 functions (26,268 bytes; 0x2B7060-0x2C006C, docs/ANALYSIS/27_unmapped_bands.md §2) hand-written in
`game/src/battle/battle_fx.cpp` / `game/include/p3fes/game/battle_fx.h` and gated with `tests/game/test_battle_fx.cpp`:
every listed row of the `battle_fx` block of queue_bands.txt except two. The effect packets' creators and callbacks
(a `sub_27EC10` packet: payload at +144, start +104 / update +108 / end +112 / finished test +116): unit movement
0xB00..0xB04 (approach `sub_2B79E0`, keep 300.0 apart `sub_2B7C50`, attack spot `sub_2B8990`, home `sub_2B8C00`,
scatter `sub_2B8DC0`) and the formation slot `sub_2B77C0`; the unit effects 0x301 / 0x302 / 0x400; the battle events
0x306..0x30A, the HP / SP gauges 0x500 / 0x501 (`sub_2BD080`, `sub_2BD2E0`, the gauge draw `sub_2BCE10` /
`sub_2BF9B0`), 0x504..0x50D. The .BED effects: bind / release (`sub_2B90D0` / `sub_2B9220`), the instance update / draw
(`sub_2BA3A0` / `sub_2BA900`), the 13 position callbacks of table 0x696490 (`jalr`) and the solver `sub_2B96F0` (VU0
macro ops), the orientation `sub_2BA0F0` (jump table 0x7B7D00). The effect slots (gBtl +400, the units' 48-slot pools).
The affinity icon / colour. The debug command lists ("Attack" / "Skill" / "Item" / "Escape" / "Wait", records
0x696E10..) and the tasks "battle_command_calc" `btlCommand_UpdateBattleCommandCalcTask` (jump table 0x7B7D40, `jalr` to the list input) /
"battle_command_draw" `btlCommand_UpdateBattleCommandDrawTask`; the target lists `sub_2BFCB0` / `sub_2BFF60`. Roles proposed in brackets in the
header (no delta file).

**Not taken.** `sub_2BAA20` (the 0x400 packet's start: H_Cdvd_Request) and `sub_2BC420` (the 0x306 packet's start:
H_Cdvd_Destroy) -- file I/O. The block's skip-class functions (printf / heap) were left alone; no row of another slice
(btlDrawTexturedQuad `0x2BC9C0` stays with its owner).

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) A unit's effect-slot pool has 48 slots but a 32-bit in-use mask: the bit of slot i is
`1 << i` as a 32-bit shift, 0 from slot 32 on, so `sub_2BB9C0` never reports a full pool -- with slots 0..31 taken it
hands out slot 32 again and again (the rule test checks it). (2) `sub_2BD2E0` writes the HP gauge's start +2564 twice
and leaves the SP gauge's +2584. (3) The affinity colours: 0x200 (255,58,68), 0x400 (255,64,18), 0x100 the default
colour gp-25472. (4) `btlCommand_UpdateBattleCommandCalcTask` runs the debug lists only under gBtl +20 0x2000000 (flags 5132 / 5129 raised);
otherwise it reads the real command menu (`sub_1FDDF0` / `sub_1FDF10`). (5) The "battle_command_*" task records are
stale in b_5800 / battle_ref_6150 (not in the kwln lists; found by name in RAM).

**Cycle-model notes.** Transliterated from the recompiled blocks by a scratch converter that also structures forward
branches into if / else and the compiler's loops into `for (;;)` (a test-first loop checks after the test, before
every iteration), then documented; the remaining backward `goto`s keep their check points. The two jump tables are C++
switches on the loaded entry with the generated fallback. Cpu view with volatile register reads and cycles (the wave-10
MSVC lesson).

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_battle_fx.cpp`; per pair: the whole register file -- GPRs in 128 bits, HI/LO, SA,
FPRs, ACC, FCR31, the VU0 macro registers -- and the cycle count at every check point and at the return / stop, the
whole 32 MiB of RAM through a PairRange, the scratchpad, the BIOS window). Random effect worlds whose words include
function addresses of this slice, so the `jalr` callbacks run a non-leaf callee (`sub_2BD080`) that spills $ra below the
$sp it receives; in 75% of the worlds the RW heap pointer 0x960178 points at a leaf that hands out a world record, so
the packet creators run past `sub_27EC10`. Real data: the three snapshots (the stale command tasks, 11 live effect
packets with their own callbacks, units, task works). Host rules: busy counts, BED accessors, slot pool / alloc / free,
the 64-byte matrix copy, instance flags, the command words, the gauge reset, the list input, the affinity icon /
colour table, the position solver's four modes. 7,080 random pairs (110 of 118 functions also return normally), 1,080
snapshot pairs; 74,967 assertions (MSVC 14.44 Release) / 75,001 (clang-cl Release). Eleven planted mutations (a cycle,
a `jalr` link, a loop bound, a table value, a 64-bit shift for the mask's 32-bit one, a dropped check point, a frame

## Phase 5 tooling: test stand-ins for heap / printf / file I/O, and the slice standins_demo (22 functions, 2026-10-21)

**Why.** The slices skipped every function whose own body allocates or frees (H_Malloc / H_Free, the RW memory slots
0x960178..0x96018C, newlib malloc), calls printf / sprintf, or requests a file (H_Cdvd_*): those callees cannot run in
a pair (printf is not emitted on purpose, heap pointers point into real allocator state, loads need the disc). Counted
from the ELF (own-body direct calls plus lui-tracked loads of the RW slots; functions.json + function_chunks.txt +
replaced.txt): **1,474** not-yet-replaced game-code functions (< 0x4FB100, of 7,579) carried one of the classes --
heap 925, printf 455, file I/O 253, task creation 213 (overlapping) -- and **3,528** reached one through direct calls.
Per band (own / reach): 0x10-0x1D 470 / 793, battle UI and title 0x1E-0x26 146 / 290, battle task 0x27-0x29 38 / 170,
0x2A-0x2B 18 / 44, 0x2C-0x2D 7 / 46, 0x2E 2 / 65, datCalc 0x2F-0x31 37 / 105, effects 0x32-0x34 127 / 213, script /
message / font 0x35-0x3B 218 / 576, social / facility / Y 0x3C-0x45 162 / 642, RenderWare 0x46-0x4F 249 / 584. Only
16 of the 1,474 also touch a hardware register or make a syscall themselves.

**Built** (`tests/game/stand_ins.h/.cpp`, `tests/rt/emit_units.cmake` -DSTAND_INS, `tests/game/CMakeLists.txt`
`_stand_in_hooks`; game/README.md "Pair tests with stand-ins", brief section "Stand-ins"): in the test library every
stub of a not-emitted function asks the installed stand-ins before its missing_function stop, and the listed emitted
heap / sprintf entry points ask them at entry; both bodies of a pair meet the same stand-in (`jal`, `guest::call`,
`rt::lookup_func` through the slots). A stand-in logs the call (address, $ra, $a0..$t3, result, text / size), runs the
callee's entry check point, works on guest memory, sets $v0 and overwrites the scratch registers with a per-call
pattern. Parts: `GuestHeap` (arena 0x1C00000-0x1F00000, zero in all six replay snapshots checked; 16-byte first fit;
H_Malloc / H_Free, RwMalloc / RwFree / RwRealloc / RwCalloc / the free-list pair, newlib malloc / free / calloc /
realloc; snapshot helpers), `guest_format` + printf / sprintf / vsprintf stand-ins, `FakeCd` (H_Cdvd_Request / Update /
ReadSync / Destroy on the retail node layout and list, sCdvdCache registration through the hand-written
H_Cdvd_AddFile, files from extracted/), `install_recorder` for any other not-emitted callee, and `run_pair_si` (a fresh
world per run, the arena compared and restored, call logs / live heap blocks / request nodes compared). Opt-in: with
no set installed nothing changes -- all 48 earlier test files pass unchanged on both compilers. For the formatter's
reference the recompiled sprintf now runs to the end: newlib's string-output path joins `_callees` (`__sinit`, `std`,
`_mbtowc_r`, `__sprint`, `__sfvwrite` = functions.json `_getpid_r`, `memchr`, `localeconv`, `memmove`); the float path
(`_dtoa_r` and its bignum / soft-float helpers) stays out, so `%f/%e/%g` are formatted by the host and not
cross-checked. Found by that cross-check: this newlib's `long` is 64-bit (`%ld/%lx` print the whole slot), `hh` is
read as `h`, `%p` prints the 64-bit slot.

**Replaced** (22, `game/src/misc/standins_demo.cpp`; replaced.txt header `# Phase 5 slice standins_demo:`): file
loaders `sub_266A20` / `sub_266CB0` (op_res: oped/op_title.bin, op_logo.bin; dorm route), `sub_21C7F0` (bp_res:
battle/panel/bp_tutorial.bin), `sub_233B20` / `sub_2339D0` (br_res: br_level.bin; br_base.bin or AGS_ / AGS2_ by The
Answer and flag 752), `sub_24BE40` (brp_res: brp_birth.bin), `sub_107020` (camp/fade_pak.pak + H_Cdvd_ReadSync); heap
users `sub_2699A0`, `sub_266600` (gm_root.c), `sub_430150` / `sub_4310E0` (task-work frees, Tartarus), `sub_3C4430` /
`sub_3C45F0` / `sub_3C4F30` (nmlist.c), `Y_SMap_CreateStaireDispTask` (RwCalloc + kwlnTaskCreate -> H_Malloc),
`sub_234710` (RwMalloc + memcpy); printf / sprintf users `sub_2449D0`, `sub_1FA450` ("brfUpdateFriendEquip"),
`sub_1FBCA0` ("%d <= %d < %d"), `sub_21B8B0` (bse_main.c), `kwlnAdxErrorCallback`, `bpIfontDrawNumber` (sprintf into
its 336-byte frame). Register-faithful: prologue spills, `$ra` links, the slot calls with `$v0` = target and the
`jalr` link, every scratch register the original writes; memory through the runtime's own load / store.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_standins_demo.cpp`: whole RAM write-tracked, scratchpad, every GPR in 128 bits,
HI/LO, the register file and cycles at every check point, the dead stack, the stand-in logs, heap blocks, nodes):
loaders 960 pairs (131 through K_Assert paths; 18 real loads), sub_107020 40 (4 PAK reads), heap users 1,500, printf
users 1,260 (bpIfontDrawNumber half on the stand-in sprintf, half on the recompiled one) -- **3,760 pairs, 282,627
assertions**, MSVC Release; the same 282,627 on clang-cl 19.1.5 Release (both files: 9 cases / 286,076 assertions on each compiler). Self-tests (`test_stand_ins.cpp`): opt-in / unchanged stop,
formatter = recompiled sprintf on 3,000 formats and vsprintf on 200 va_lists, heap rules and the H_Malloc / RW slot
paths, a real file through request / dedup / read-sync / cache / deferred destroy. Two planted mutations (a dropped
`$at` write in sub_1FBCA0, a cycle in sub_3C4430) fail 479 and 600 assertions.

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build/sb-gate -ClangTree build/sb-clang -Jobs 3 -FastGs`, base `3de1539`,
2,343 replaced): ctest 65/65 on both compilers, `p3fes_game_tests` **401 cases / 47,175,846 assertions** (MSVC) and
**401 / 47,175,885** (clang-cl); dorm `EE0EB5DA…795D85`, M1 `E3A93615…B672`, battle `CFAA5A61…F606`, fusion
`9B5B5374…C58F`, shop `1165B3E0…A8E5`, all 0 differing bytes, gsMemory identical: **GATE: PASSED**.

**Still skip reasons**: mid-body entries; hardware registers or syscalls in the function's own body; the IOP / SIF RPC
and the sound driver; ADXF / ROFS / sceCd called directly (FakeCd serves the H_Cdvd API only -- recorders can stand
in for the rest); callees that are themselves hand-written (always run) or emitted but not in `_stand_in_hooks`.

## Phase 5 slice big_draws: the title screen's three draws and the date / time HUD's helpers (6 functions)

Not from queue_bands: a fixed list of large draw bodies earlier slices left only for their size. All six replaced in
`game/src/ui/big_draws.cpp` / `game/include/p3fes/game/big_draws.h`, none of them in main's `game/replaced.txt` before:
the title slice's leftovers `sub_267430` [opTitle_Draw] (6,628 B), `sub_26A2C0` opMenuUpdate (9,296 B), `sub_26EED0`
[opWait_Draw] (9,056 B), and the ui3 slice's HUD helpers `sub_183840` [H_DayPartsDraw_DrawMoon] (916 B), `sub_183BE0`
[H_DayPartsDraw_DrawDate] (888 B), `sub_183F60` [H_DayPartsDraw_DrawDayPart] (852 B). Nothing skipped. Started before
the p3fes_handgen workflow and finished under it (paused 2026-10-21, resumed on f68870a).

**How.** A scratch converter turned the recompiled blocks into Cpu-view statements, one per instruction (`rt::` call ->
statement, `ctx.cycles += N` -> charge, back-edge check -> backedge, `rt::jal` + call -> jal: the same mechanical
transcription p3fes_handgen does); a scratch structurer folded the plain shapes (if-skips, if / else diamonds,
else-chains to a common join, test-first and test-last loops: of the 591 labels of the generated bodies 3 were left in
the title draws, rewritten by hand), the verbatim idioms became Cpu helpers (`f2u8` the float -> unsigned conversion,
31 sites of which 17 inside `white_alpha`; `quad_pass` 19, `rotate_quad` 3, `scale_quad_about_centre` 2, `kassert` 4),
the .sdata float literals and $gp words were annotated, the sections documented. The HUD helpers were rewritten by hand
around their jump tables (0x7B6630 moon phase -> icon, 0x7B66B0 weekday -> glyph, 0x7B66D0 day part -> name; read from
guest memory, dispatched on the target). The Cpu view reads GPRs and updates virtual time through volatile accesses
(the render_core3 lesson). The readings were checked against the pseudocode reference (`tools/ours/ida/pseudo.py`:
the HUD switches and the glow counter match) and the recovered types (OpTitleWork / OpMenuWork / OpWaitWork):
`tools/ours/types/deltas/big_draws.json` names the timers, counters and fade grids (types_build: OpMenuWork 8 of 8
known fields found, OpWaitWork 6 of 6, 0 conflicts).

**Faithfulness audit** (`audit_faithful.py --only <the six> --seeds 96 --snapshots dorm_replay_4900,b_5800,climb_ref_17000
--snapshot-seeds 16`): **faithful 6, differ 0, crash 0, hang 0** (144 pairs each; the converted bodies were kept, no
regeneration needed).

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) The title draws only update sprite strips (positions, colour floats) in their works; every
animation is a ramp of a timer, a sine of a wrapping counter, or a rotation / zoom of a full-screen quad about
(320, 224). (2) opTitle_Draw advances its own fade timer (+4, to 200 / 512 while showing) before it draws; opMenuUpdate
steps eight background counters with the compiled `%` and the menu timer (+2332, to 80); opWait_Draw moves no timer.

## fx_types (Phase 5 slice): the effect system's effect-type handlers, band 0x324160-0x34C160 -- 129 functions

**What.** `game/src/fx/fx_types.cpp` (`fx_types.h`): 129 of the band's 400 table-dispatched effect-type handlers
(8,412 bytes), register-faithful on a Cpu view (one variable per guest register, volatile accesses, the runtime's own
load / store ops). Not a queue_bands.txt slice: the band map's direct-call closure cannot follow the jalr tables, so the
set was chosen by **measuring** -- a temporary per-function entry counter patched into the recompiled bodies of the band
(`recomp/generated`, never committed), built once into a gate tree, the dorm / M1 / battle routes run with it (the gate
passed with it in), then re-emitted away. Per route: M1 runs 3 functions of the band, dorm 30, battle 245 of 400. Of
the 129 taken, battle runs 96, dorm 15, M1 3; the hottest: the keyframe curve `sub_32A540` (55,687 calls on battle),
the screen shake `sub_347D60` (8,371 battle / 7,755 dorm / 5,520 M1: every frame), the track value setter `sub_3322D0`
(7,015), the screen-filter kind calls `sub_34B520` / `sub_34B580` / `sub_34B5C0` (~3,070 each), the class-12 setters
`sub_339760` (3,032) / `sub_339770`, the track update `sub_332210` (2,851). The other 33 are the class table's shared
defaults (`sub_324630` .. `sub_324670`, 65+ table slots) and slot dispatchers, and other slots / twins of the classes
that run. Proposed names (113 unique): `symbols/deltas/fx_types.sym`; record layouts: `tools/ours/types/deltas/fx_types.json`
(EffectNode first child / sibling / key, FxTrack, FxCurve, FxShakeRecord).

**Findings.** (1) The class table 0x69BE20 has 27 rows of 13 words (`52 * class`, the u16 at effect +4); slot 0 makes the
instance, slot 1 destroys it, 2 / 3 update / draw; the base dispatchers `sub_324930` .. `sub_324AF0` never ran on the
three routes. (2) The classes 9, 10, 12, 13, 16 delegate to kind rows: 0x69C5D0 / 0x69C650 of six words (stride 24:
init, param, destroy, update, draw, size) and 0x69C850 / 0x69C970 of seven (stride 28: the size word is the seventh);
class 10 has 9 kinds, 12 and 16 three. (3) The track update `sub_332210` resets as many key slots as the track's own
count word (+8, `sltu a2, a0`), not a fixed four (the first version's bug, caught by the pair tests). (4) The shake
trigger `sub_348110`: +0 is the shake's length (past it the call does nothing; 0 never ends), the weight ramps over
the fade-in / fade-out, amplitude = 10 * strength * weight and 4 * that / 10. (5) The tint copies (`sub_337E10` /
`sub_338CE0`) write an alpha of 255 as 254 and restore it. (6) The curve `sub_32A540` has three modes (linear, one key,
two keys; keys as fractions of the duration), any other mode holds the start value.

**Not taken** (left recompiled): the VU0-heavy node / particle bodies (`sub_3252A0` .. `sub_32A890`, the 2-5 KB kind
updates of 0x32AF30 .. 0x346530, `sub_3275D0`, `sub_3282E0`), the class create / clone functions of class 2 and class 13
(class 13 never ran), the DMA packet builders 0x3294D0 .. 0x329630 and their callers (`sub_348DA0`, `sub_349D30`,
`sub_34A1D0`, ...: the rendering queue), `sub_324160` / `sub_324510` (their first callee is the RW mesh / raster
creation; a pair could only run to it).

**Cycle-model notes.** The kind calls form the row offset as `((k << 1) + k) << 3` or `((k << 3) - k) << 2` with $v0 /
$v1 as the original; the first block of every forwarder includes the call and the epilogue (no branch: one charge).
Test-first loops (`sub_3261C0`, `sub_326200`, `sub_326240`, `sub_332210`, `sub_347D60`) charge the test block, then
check before every pass.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_fx_types.cpp`): a "pointer soup" world (64 KiB of pointers back into it, small
integers, floats, noise) plus the records each function reads by shape (effect records with a class and an instance,
filter instances, kind objects, tracks, node children, curves, shake records, the gp-relative shake state); the ELF's
class table and kind rows with slots re-aimed at callbacks (leaves and a non-leaf that spills $ra below its $sp);
RwMalloc / RwFree aimed at callbacks so the class creators run. Every pair compares all GPRs (128 bits), HI/LO, FPRs,
ACC, FCR31, the VU0 register file, the register file and cycles at every check point, the whole 32 MiB, the dead stack,
the scratchpad and the bus log; documented-rule checks (block getters, slot dispatch, child lookups, key-slot reset,
masks, update+draw counter, tint, curve modes, shake hold); the shake update / screen size on the three replay
snapshots. Six planted mutations were each caught and reverted: one cycle in the tint copy (88 failing checks), the
kind-row offset formed in a stale register (617), the s0 spill dropped from the shared prologue (6,932), a `blez` ->
`bltz` boundary in the kind draw (344), the curve's second key read from +28 (853), the shake amplitude factor 4.0 ->
5.0 (842). Slice: 12 cases, 12,643 pairs, **1,000,788 assertions** (MSVC 14.44 Release, `build/fx_types-gate`).
**Audit** (`audit_faithful.py --only <the 129> --seeds 96 --snapshots dorm_replay_4900,b_5800,climb_ref_17000
--snapshot-seeds 16`): **129 faithful, 0 differ** (313 s).

**Gate** (`tools/ours/gate/gate.ps1 -Tree build\fx_types-gate -Slice -FastGs -Jobs 3`, base 9f3a796, 2,599 replaced):
ctest 59/59, `p3fes_game_tests` 431 cases / 48,519,381 assertions; dorm `EE0EB5DA...`, m1 `E3A93615...`, battle

the key condition `sub_360ED0`, the unit / key lists, the scene loaders (`sub_38F0F0`, `sub_38F440`, `sub_38F8C0`,
`sub_38FA10`, `sub_38FFB0`), the camera slots (`sub_38CA80` / `sub_38CC10` / `sub_38D560`), the allocator (`sub_386AE0` /
`sub_386B70` with the per-class counters). **Skipped**: nothing of the list; the editor menus (127 functions, debug only,
no route reaches them) and the 0x385B20-0x38DAD0 / 0x38DAD0-0x3902B8 functions that neither run nor serve the player
(save / load of edited events, path editing, resource backups) are left for later.

**Readability** (on the p3fes_handgen bodies; nothing that runs changed): every function has its role, arguments and
result written above it; `game/include/p3fes/game/events.h` documents EvtWork (2448 B, 58 named fields and the flag
bits), EvtUnit (156 B), EvtKey (84 B), the PM key rows and the gp-relative globals 0x7CE5BC..0x7CE5F4; 942 loads / stores
use the named offsets (`lw(a3, a0, unit::kKeyHead)`) where the base register holds that record for the whole function, 38
gp accesses use the global names, the switch cases of the key-defaults switch (`sub_361350`, by unit type) and of the load
states (`sub_36DB20`) and the sections of the play step are labelled. The layouts were checked against a live event: two
snapshots made for this slice during the dorm event (`--reference-mode`, extracted/_ours/events_dorm_2100 / 2300: event
E401_002, frames 0..60, current 30, 38 units in type-rank order, frame-sorted keys, flags 0x28 = play mode + waiting
for a message). Types delta `tools/ours/types/deltas/events.json` (types_build: EvtWork 56 of 58 fields found, EvtUnit
16 of 19, EvtKey 8 of 13, 0 conflicts; the project total 14 -> 13 conflicts).

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) Units are kept sorted by the rank byte of their type (0x69D590: the type itself, except 47 /
49 -> 5 and 50 -> 6), keys by frame (insertion before the first greater frame). (2) A key fires when its unit type has no
conditions (`sub_36F500`: the editor table row lists menu 18; cached in the row's byte +10) or its condition holds:
type 1 = event counter (g_scrGlobals + 800) equals the value, type 2 = flag bit in bank 0 / 1024 / 4096 (bank >= 3 never),
an invalid type prints an assert, clears the condition and fires. (3) The timeline advances one frame per process step
unless something holds it (pause, message, effect channel, fade, sub task, comu message: `sub_36D030` holds or releases
every actor when that changes); a jump key takes effect at the next advance; in play mode the last frame ends the event
(flag 0x40000 -> `sub_36E260`, which waits for the fades). (4) Events 80-1 and 80-5 can be skipped from frame 31 on.
(5) The state appliers receive the current key and the next one; camera units interpolate between them with the
progress (frame - cur) / (next - cur).

**What.** `game/src/model/models.cpp` (`models.h`): 148 of the band's 168 functions (26,480 bytes of `mdlManager.c` /
`mdlFile.c`): the model instance record (MdlModel, 1,072 bytes, one list per model kind at 0x9571F0 -- in the replay
snapshots kind 1 the party, 2 enemies, 3 / 4 battle and map objects, 5 NPCs, 7 / 10 the party's weapons as children),
create (`sub_316690`) / find / clone / destroy, creation from a file, memory or an archive through the H_Cdvd layer and
the load state machine `sub_31B220`, the clump set-up `sub_316970` (the big-skeleton PDS pipelines, skin types, MatFX,
the "step_" UV materials, per-material model colours), the four animation slots (animation sets, the end callback
`sub_313090`, set-time / speed / frame queries, the bone-scale key hook `sub_312D40` / `sub_312C70`, the look-at
setters), attachments on helper frames, helper matrices (`sub_318D10`), effect lists and after effects bound to
helpers, the NPC / party-member file names and the packed kinds' archive names, the sound record, the keyframe curves.

load, set-up, slot and attachment paths are now readable C++ with named record layouts.

**How.** p3fes_handgen bodies (faithful by construction), made readable by an annotation pass that is checked rather than
hand-edited: every function's role above it (wrapped prose), proposed names in brackets, block roles, named offsets
(`models.h`: MdlModel, MdlAnimSlot, MdlAnimSet, MdlLoad, MdlFxNode) put in through per-function typed views of the base
registers, the callee roles on every `jal`, the gp constants' values. A checker strips comments, folds the named offsets
back to numbers and compares the result with the generator's output line by line: **identical code** (8,175 lines), so no
statement, charge or check point moved. Pseudocode reference used as a reading hint only. Names:
`symbols/deltas/models.sym` (146 unique); layouts fed back in `tools/ours/types/deltas/models.json` (types_build: MdlModel
35 known fields, 30 found, **0 conflicting** -- the earlier +0xD8 width conflict is gone: the flags are a u16).

read: `sub_316E00` finds it, `sub_316F70` copies it once ready), 0x4000 synchronous load (H_Cdvd_ReadSync), 0x4 / 0x8000
attached child. (2) The animation sets' 80-byte entries are {root matrix, animation, flags}; slot 0's entry matrix becomes
the model's root offset (`sub_3182D0`), and `sub_3176C0` places the clump at root offset x placement. A placeholder
animation (the address 0x9571D0) marks entries that exist but play nothing. (3) The slot record +48 is the effect binding
`sub_311480` updates ({count, setter argument, per-animation effect lists +20, running / wanted lists +24 / +28,

substitutions by flag (0xB00..0xB03), and the 190 NPCs of the list 0x69AF00 wear "a" (summer) from 57 to 178 days after
April 5 (June 1 - September 30) and "b" otherwise; NPC numbers 60000..60399 stand for the hero / party slots 0-2 (`sub_31B680`).
(5) The packed kinds 1 / 2 load "model/pack/<name>.pac" (or "<name>a.pac" with the outfit flag of 0x69BA18 or in The
Answer). (6) The three sound-bank slots (0x957220) are least-recently used by a stamp counter.

## Phase 5 slice read_script: the regenerated script VM and comm_b bodies made readable (113 functions, no new ones)

A readability pass, not new functions: the faithfulness audit had regenerated 113 functions of four script files with
p3fes_handgen (register-level `hg_cpu` statements with the old comments above them). They are readable again without
changing what runs. `game/replaced.txt` is unchanged.

| file | functions made readable | what changed |
|---|---:|---|
| `game/src/script/script_ops.cpp` | 38 | the PUSH / POP opcodes, CALL, END, MINUS, NOT, IF, scrOperation and the ADD..LE wrappers, scrSet*ReturnVal / scrSetPC / scrGetLabelAddr / scrGet{Int,Float,Str}Para |
| `game/src/script/script_vm.cpp` | 4 | PROC, JUMP, GOTO, ApplyRelocTable |
| `game/src/script/script_vm2.cpp` | 25 | scrTraceCode, scrScriptProcess, scrForceTraceCode, scrStartScript2, sub_35BD20, scrFindPrcdIdxByName, scrSetUserData, the COMM functions 7..46 and the dds3 accessors |
| `game/src/script/comm_b.cpp` | 46 | the COMM handlers 255..494 |

- **Roles**: every function has a role comment. A COMM handler's comment gives its `sScrCommandTable 0x7B92B0` index in
  decimal and hex (read from the ELF, the same as comm_b.h's), its arguments, what it does and what it returns. Each
  role also lists the block costs. Proposed names are in brackets and match the earlier slices' proposals:
  [dds3ProcessExists], [scrCommand_SQRT], [scrCommand_SCR_KILL_SYNC] and so on. No new `.sym` delta.
- **Named offsets and typed views**:
  - `scr::ofs` (script_vm.h) gives the ScrTask fields, the instruction / label layout and the script `$gp` globals
    as instruction immediates. They are `static_assert`ed against the `ScrTask` struct and the `scr::k*` constants.
  - `bf::` (script_vm2.cpp) gives the BF header and its 16-byte section descriptors, asserted against `scr2::kBf*`.
  - `cb::` (comm_b.cpp) gives the $gp globals asserted against comm_b.h's values, plus EventWork::field, the field
    descriptor's id / flags / +8, btlAction (id, flags2, unit, move kind / arg, next), btlUnit (side, dat),
    DatUnit (flags, base id), gBtl (actions, setup, script words), KwlnTask::work and the g_data words.
    Field names come from types_query.py / types.json and the proposed headers (script_event.h, unit.h,
    battle_state.h, task.h), each confirmed from the body's own instructions.
  - Registers are named (`Gpr& task = s0`, `Gpr &image = s5, &procs = s4, ...`), and the scr::Tag / scr::Op constants
    replace the bare immediates.
  - The accessor calls are labelled (`// arg 2 (int)`, `// the COMM result`, `// K_Assert(file, line): a no-op in
    retail`).
- **Structure**: 50 of the 51 `goto` statements are gone. The one left is scrGetStrPara's out-of-table tag jumping into the
  jump table's shared abort case.
  - goto-skips over a block that ends in `return` / `break` became `if (!c) { ... }`.
  - A block two paths jump to is written out on both paths. Examples: the PopInt tag-0 / tag-4 raw read, and the
    float OR / AND true / false blocks.
  - In CodeFunc_IF the original's inlined PopInt / PopFloat are local lambdas called where the generated body
    jumped to them. In scrOperation the float path, the int path, the float push 0x35DF6C and the epilogue are
    lambdas, and the top-level tag tests decide between `float_path()` and `int_path()`.
  - Elsewhere the epilogue copies became one `epilogue()` lambda (scrStartScript2, scrFindPrcdIdxByName), and loop
    exits became `break`s (scrTraceCode, scrFindPrcdIdxByName, sub_1C3FE0).
  - Every path runs exactly the generated statements, charges and check points in the generated order.
- **Statement check** (scratch tool, not committed): it extracts every guest statement of each old (HEAD) and new
  body, with aliases and constants resolved. 108 of the 113 functions keep the same statements in the same order.
  sub_1C3FE0, scrTraceCode, scrScriptProcess and scrFindPrcdIdxByName keep the same multiset in a moved text order.
  CodeFunc_End / CodeFunc_Not / CodeFunc_IF / scrOperation / scrStartScript2 keep every old statement, plus the copies
  of the shared blocks they now write on each path, or minus the merged epilogue copies. All of these were checked by
  hand.
- **Types delta** `tools/ours/types/deltas/read_script.json` names fields of ScrTask, BfHeader, EventWork, FieldParams
  and btlAction. `types_build.py` (outputs to scratch) shows the same totals with and without it: 1,454 known
  fields, 1,085 found, 13 conflicting. The delta adds no conflicts.

(sin / cos and the 1 - cos path with its three combine ops), create / destroy, the module and its tolerances, the
matrix stream reader), free lists (11), the resource arena (10: init, open / close, allocate with eviction, free, the

(14), textures / dictionaries (19 incl. the texture / dictionary stream reader and writer), rasters (8), the heap users
the earlier render slices skipped (17: geometry unlock, the build-mesh append, tri-list / tri-strip generation, the

(own-body EE / GS register access: the 16 `lui 0x1000/0x1200` rows of queue_rendering.txt class b, sce* library, cop0)
were not considered. None of the 150 touches hardware registers, makes a syscall or talks to the IOP in its own body:
`sub_4DE0A0` reaches the GS store-image path only through its callees (sceGsSetDefStoreImage / sceDmaGetChan /
sceGsExecStoreImage / SyncDCache), the blits the DMA packet layer through theirs (DIntr / EIntr are callees). No RW
skin / anim / HAnim function was taken (models slice).

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) RwFrame: +144 the objects' link list (each object's sync callback at object + 16,
called with the object), +152 child, +156 next, +160 root; the dirty list 0x96012C links roots at +8; private flags
bits 0..1 on a root = in the dirty list / LTMs to sync, bits 2..3 on a frame = its LTM / objects to sync. Clone
recurse points the source's root word at its clone (the map the clump clone's second pass reads) and builds child
lists in reverse order. (2) Matrix flags: bit 0 normal, bit 1 orthogonal, bit 17 identity; the module's tolerances at
+12 / +16 / +20 (normal / orthogonal / identity). (3) Free-list entries: (block + bitmap + alignment + 7) &
-alignment + size x index, bitmap MSB first; for-all-used snapshots each bitmap first (RwMalloc) so the callback may
free. (4) The resource arena keeps two list heads (+16 / +24) and two pointers that swap every frame (+36 this
frame's, +32 the older); allocation evicts the older list's tail first, then this frame's (counted at +8). Every
resEntry of the snapshots carries the PS2All release `sub_49CC30` as its destroy notification, which waits for the
DMA references to drop. (5) Chunk headers: version = ((id >> 14) & 0x3FF00) + 0x30000 | (id >> 16) & 0x3F, build =
id & 0xFFFF; a pre-3.1 id (high half 0) -> version id << 8; accepted 0x35000..0x37002, written 0x37002 build 0x37.
(6) `sub_4C17F0` / `sub_4C1820` and `sub_4C1850` / `sub_4C1910` are byte-identical pairs.

**Types delta.** `tools/ours/types/deltas/render_rw4.json`: RwFrame, RwMatrix, RwFreeList, RwStream, RwResEntry,
RwTexture, RwRaster (anchored on their accessors). `types_build.py` takes it (the regenerated headers are not
committed); one width conflict is listed: RwTexture +0x50, which `sub_4BD4E0` writes as a byte (the filter-mode byte of
the filter / addressing word) -- a union, not a header error.

entries with their destroy notifications cleared, see rule 4), registries with their live objects, memory streams over

## Phase 5 slice read_text: the text and UI bodies made readable again (2026-10-22)

A readability pass, no new functions (game/replaced.txt unchanged): the register-level bodies the faithfulness audit
regenerated in `game/src/msg/msg2.cpp` (68), `game/src/ui/font.cpp` (41) and `game/src/ui/ui2.cpp` (45) = 154 keep every
statement, charge, check point and call of p3fes_handgen's output in the same order on every path, and now say what they
do. `datSetFlag` (the lead's readable version) is unchanged.

- **`game/include/p3fes/game/text_view.h`** (new, header only, namespace `tview`): `la(r, va)` the adjacent
  `lui`/`addiu` pair, `hi()` / `lo()` / `gp_off()` / `gw_off()` the address a `lui` pair, a `$gp` offset or a
  gGlobalWork offset forms, `k_assert(a0, a1, pc, file, line)` the four statements of a K_Assert call; the record
  offsets, each from the instructions that use it and checked against msg2.h / bmd_msg.h / font.h / ui2.h and the type
  recovery: the manager slot and the message handle with its speaker / text / selection / window sub-records
  (`mes_slot::`, `mes_handle::`, `speaker_rec::`, `text_rec::`, `select_rec::`, `window_rec::`), the BMD image and
  dialogue records (`bmd_img::`, `dialogue_rec::`), line and glyph nodes (`line_node::`, `glyph_node::`), the itfPnl
  panels, their animation record and per-type work buffers (`pnl::`, `pnl_anim::`, `pnl_buf::`), the font styles and
  .FNT header (`fnt_style::`, `fnt_hdr::`), text codes (`text_code::`), the Huffman blocks and GS list (`gsl_blocks::`,
  `gsl_entry::`), the ring buffers (`ring::`), the raster-slot cache (`raster_mgr::`, `raster_slot::`), the tag scan
  (`tag_scan::`, `tag_window::`, `tag_flags::`), the social stats (`social::`) and event/itemtbl.bin (`itemtbl::`).
- **Mechanical, value-preserving rewrites** (scripted, then checked statement for statement against main's bodies by a
  normaliser that evaluates every named constant and helper and compares each function's statement sequence and its
  multiset of branch conditions): 30 K_Assert calls, 40 `lui`/`addiu` pairs, 34 `lui` + load/store pairs, 62 `$gp`
  offsets; then every load / store offset named by its record field.
- **Structure**: no goto left in the three files (52 before). A goto became an if / else / break with a host `bool`
  where paths merge (`moved`, `in_range`, `holiday`, `inside`, `found`, `picked`, `hit`, `end_code` ...), a duplicated
  epilogue one epilogue, the generator's `for (;;) { test; if (a) { check; ...; continue; } break; }` row walks
  `for (;;) { test; if (!a) break; check; ...; if (!b) break; ...; next; }` (the same blocks in the same order). Every
  function comment gives its role and, for a `sub_` name, a proposed name in brackets; every block comment its role.
- **Types delta** `tools/ours/types/deltas/read_text.json`: ItfMesTextRecord +8 / +17..+24 (dialogue record, tag flags,
  style, colour set, mode, alpha, last line index, line), FrFontLineNode +18 line step / +32 style glyph, ItfPnlAnimWork
  +4 scale. types_build: 1217 -> 1218 documented fields found, conflicts unchanged (12).

**How an event is started, stepped and ended** (written out in `events2.h` for the scene editor and the server): the field
root creates the PM reader and then the viewer (`mtEvtMain_CreateZikkiPlayModeEventViewerTask`: EvtWork, the kwln task);
its first update sets play mode and installs the process steps; `sub_36DB20` loads (state 3 = `sub_3942F0`, state 11 =
`sub_3912F0`: units and keys, frame header -> kFrameCount +12 / kStartFrame +16 / kEndFrame +20, kFrame = start,
kPrevFrame = -1); `sub_36E690` steps one frame per call: flag dispatch first (kFlagEnd 0x40000 -> `sub_36E260`, kFlagReload
0x80 -> `sub_36DB20`, 0x10000 -> `sub_36E2F0`, kFlagOverlay 0x20000 -> `sub_36E140` waiting for the custom-event task),
the keys of a new frame applied (`sub_366AC0`), the frame advanced unless kStopped holds it, jumps taken at the next
advance; the end: the last frame sets kFlagEnd, `sub_36E260` waits for the fades and returns -1, the task's destroy
callback `sub_36F260` frees everything; the field root then reads `sub_36F480` (free movement) and `sub_36F4C0` (entrance).
