## anim (Phase 5 slice): animation and skinning -- RtAnim, RpHAnim, RpSkin, RpUVAnim, the keyframe schemes -- 151 functions

**What.** `game/src/model/anim.cpp` (`anim.h`): 151 functions, 46,288 bytes, all p3fes_handgen bodies (0 refused):
- RtAnim 0x4B65A0-0x4B75D0 (20): the plugin (id 0x1B7) and the interpolation-scheme registry (0x95FBE0, 16 x 48-byte
  `RtAnimInterpolatorInfo`, count 0x7CE8A0), animations (create / read / stream read, write, size / node count),
  interpolators (create / set animation / add, sub and set time / blend / copy / sub-interpolators / loop callback).
- RpUVAnim + RtDict 0x4B76B0-0x4B97F0 (44): the material UV animation of the models' UV materials: the two UV schemes
  (0x1C0 linear, 0x1C1 parametric) and their callbacks, the 48-byte material extension (two UV matrices + eight
  interpolator slots), its streams, the animation dictionaries, `RpUVAnimMaterialApplyInterpolators`.
- RpHAnim 0x464760-0x466EF0 (25): the standard keyframe scheme (id 1), the plugin (id 0x11E) with its 8-byte frame
  extension and streams, hierarchy create / sub-hierarchies / attach, `RpHAnimHierarchyUpdateMatrices` and the
  no-matrix-array variant.
- RpSkin 0x489020-0x48AC10 (41): the plugin (id 0x116), the 4-byte atomic (hierarchy) and geometry (`RpSkin*`)
  extensions, the skin streams (generic and native), split data, skin types and the PDS skin pipelines (0x11002, MatFX
  0x11013 / 0x11014), and `skinPrepareWeights` -- the bone indices packed into the weights' low bits for the VU1 skin
  programs. (`sub_48A3E0` was already on main.)
- The compressed keyframe scheme 0x4F7300-0x4F8E10 (10): id 2; every live character animation in the snapshots uses
  it (24-byte keyframes: time, 4 + 3 16-bit floats; 24 bytes of custom data = translation offset[3], scale[3]).
- The game's own keyframe scheme 0x35A290-0x35ABA0 (9): id 0x44A07195, 52-byte keyframes with quaternion,
  translation, scale and a scalar.
- Two model-manager leftovers: `sub_311730` (the look-at hierarchy update, 5.4 KB) and `sub_317730` [mdlModelUpdate].

**The animation state a networked character needs** (documented in `anim.h`): per animation slot of the MdlModel
(+236, 156 bytes each): the animation index (+4), time (+12), speed (+8), loop flag (+0 bit 0) and, while blending, the
previous index / time (+16 / +20), the blend length in frames (+24, a u16 not named before) and the progress (+28, 0..1;
>= 1 = no blend). Everything else is derived: `RtAnimInterpolatorSetCurrentTime` rebuilds the interpolated frames
from the animation at that time, `RpHAnimHierarchyUpdateMatrices` the node matrices (hierarchy +8, 64 bytes x nodes),
`_rpSkinMatrixUpdating` the skin palette from those -- so a remote character is posed by setting index / time / blend
on its slot and running the normal update. Node matrices are the fallback payload (94 / 91 / 102 nodes for the three
party models of b_5800). The look-at (slot +76..) and the material animation (MdlModel +868) are separate small states.

**How.** p3fes_handgen bodies made readable by a checked annotation pass (scratch tool, not committed): each function's
role and proposed name above it; named offsets put in through typed views of the base registers (entry types per
function, callee-saved copies, pointer fields loaded from typed records; 403 offsets in 70 functions, `anim::` records
in `anim.h`, models.h's `mdl::` slot names); the callee's role on every call and the global's role on the address
comments. A checker strips comments, folds the constants back to numbers and compares with the generator's output:
identical code (14,759 lines). Then one structure edit: the 15 blocks the generator parks after a function's last
return and reaches by a single goto are written out at that goto (gotos 104 -> 89; the same statements, charges and
check points on every path; checked by the audit and the pair tests). Pseudocode reference used as a reading hint
only. Names: `symbols/deltas/anim.sym` (151 rows; RenderWare names only where the body matches the public RW 3.x
API). Types: `tools/ours/types/deltas/anim.json` -- RtAnimInterpolator 19 known / 19 found, RtAnimInterpolatorInfo
12 / 12, RpHAnimHierarchy 9 / 8, RtAnimAnimation 6 / 5, RpSkin 15 / 8, 0 conflicts; totals 1,433 -> 1,484 found, 13
conflicts unchanged (base c67ffac).

**Findings.** (1) Every character animation runs on the compressed scheme (id 2): the decode is sign | ((e << 12) +
112 << 23) | (m << 12) for a 4-bit exponent and 11-bit mantissa, and the interpolated translation is the lerp of the
decoded keyframes x scale + offset from the animation's custom data -- checked on 17,331 frames. (2) The slot's blend
is a progress, not a weight: +28 grows by 1 / (+24 blend frames) per update while `RtAnimInterpolatorBlend` mixes the
two blend interpolators (+36 / +40) into the hierarchy's; at >= 1 the hierarchy's interpolator takes the incoming
animation (read from the recompiled `sub_313490`). (3) With `mdlAnimEndCB` attached, a wrap can freeze a non-looping
slot at the end or re-time a looping one (models.cpp); the RtAnim wrap rule (time - n x duration) holds with the
callback detached. (4) 0x96012C is the RW engine's dirty-frame list head (it points at itself when empty). (5)
`name__C9type_info` (0x48A3D0) is a FLIRT mismatch: it is the skin's bone-count getter.

**Not taken.** None of the chosen bands was refused (no mid-body entries, hardware registers, syscalls, IOP or VU0
macro code). Trimmed after the merge with main, per the brief: `test_field3_units` / `test_field3_event` (new on main)
stand in `sub_313490` [mdlAnimSlotUpdate], `sub_3138E0` [mdlAnimSlotSetAnim], `sub_314850` / `sub_314D30` (material
animation start / update), `sub_4663D0` [RpHAnimHierarchyDestroy], `sub_4B6980` [RtAnimAnimationDestroy],
`sub_4B6EB0` [RtAnimInterpolatorDestroy] and `sub_4B78B0` [RtDictDestroy] with recorders, and a replaced callee cannot
be stood in (their pairs failed: a missing strncmp inside the hand `sub_314850`, no recorded `sub_3138E0` calls); the
eight stay recompiled (all eight were faithful in the audit before the trim). Left for later: `sub_4B7630` /
`sub_4B7690` (dictionary-schema set-up shared with the movie player), the plugin band 0x45EC00-0x464540 (another
plugin, error id 0x122, and shadow code), `sub_3151D0` (a draw). Callee added for the tests:
`RpMatFXMaterialSetUVTransformMatrices` 0x4699B0 (a leaf) in `_callees`.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_anim.cpp`, 7 cases / 367,687 assertions on MSVC): the generic sweep (9,664 pairs);
RtAnim on the 26 live interpolators of b_5800 / dorm_replay_4900 / climb_ref_17000 (554 pairs; the frame rule on 17,331

## Phase 5 slice savedata: the save system -- the save format, its packer / unpackers / verifier, the memory-card screens, the name entry (123 functions, 2026-10-22)

Every multiplayer player will carry a save of their own, so this slice rewrites and documents the code that packs and
unpacks the game state, and the screens around it. 123 functions in `game/src/data/savedata.cpp` /
`game/include/p3fes/game/savedata.h`, generated by p3fes_handgen (0 refused) and made readable: a role comment for
every function (proposed names in brackets, ADR-0009), the save blocks named at every store of the packer and at
every compare of the unpackers' dispatch chain, named labels, card-process work offsets named at 202 loads / stores,
23 single-use tail blocks moved to their goto, and the two 158-way compare chains (sub_179360: nesting 51 deep, which
MSVC refuses with C1061; sub_17A430: 159) flattened to one level by a structure-only transform (every path keeps its
statements, charges and check points in order).

**The save format** (savedata.h has the full table; checked byte for byte against the save the game itself wrote on
`extracted/_ours/cards/tartarus.ps2`): the card file `BASLUS-21621Save<N>` (`...SaveG<N>` in The Answer, Persona 3's
`BASLUS-21569Save<N>` for a carry-over load) is the packed buffer, 36,182 bytes, little-endian and unaligned:
- `+0` u32 version 3; `+4` a 52-byte header for the slot list (u16 day, u16 time slot, s32 play time in 1/30 s =
  counter 47, u8 level from the exp table, u8 clear mark from flags 0x1311 / 0x1319, u8 *0x83AA98, the two 18-byte
  names, the field major / minor, a u16 byte sum of header bytes 0..49 -- never checked on load; header byte 11 is
  stale stack);
- `+56` 158 blocks `{s32 id, u32 size, data}`: ids 1..36 (no 32) = the whole gGlobalWork range 0x836200..0x83AA9C in 35
  pieces (the equipment stock and item counts through their pointers +0x594 / +0x598; names, the hero's unit, social
  links, date / time slot / time skip, the persona stock, the compendium 256 x 52, the flags 704, the counters 512,
  money, party, the return field / floor, the tables of blocks 27..31, The Answer's day index); `0x100 (k + 1) +
  piece` = the ten party records 0x834010 + 868 k (k 0..9) in twelve pieces each (`kRecordPieces`); 0x1000 the
  20-entry equipment table 0x833E80; 0x1001 the item count table 0x833C20; 0x2000 the checksum (one u8: the byte sum of
  everything from +56 up to that block);
- then `s32 -1`.
The loader copies a block only when both its id and size match (unknown ids are skipped), then rebuilds the hero's
display names; the verifier needs >= 4,096 bytes and checks the sum for version >= 3; a carry-over load copies only
blocks 2 / 16 / 17 / 24 into four buffers. Before packing, the packer re-reads the return field (the field work
*0x7CD540) and floor (K_FldDungeon_GetCurrentFloor) into blocks 21..23.

**Functions:** the save (sub_177DB0 [datSavePack], sub_179030 [datSaveUnpack], sub_1791D0 [datSaveVerify], sub_179360
[datSaveUnpackBlock], sub_17A430 [datSaveUnpackCarryOverBlock]); the 30 g_data.c functions 0x17C2F0-0x17D7C0 (the
compendium get / store / compare / register / completion percent, the tables of save blocks 27..31, two tail
wrappers); datPersona.c sub_173C60 [datPersonaGetEquipStatBonus], sub_174C10 [datPersonaRemoveSlot], sub_175820
[datPersonaGive], sub_175CE0 [datPersonaCalcLevelUp] (sub_176210 was the calendar slice's); the H_Memcard request
setters (save / load / list / area check requests, the overwrite / format confirmations, the cancel word) and the
500-word list init; the memory-card screens 0x41BE50-0x42176C (40: "mcProc" with its check / free-space / save / load
steps and the slot-list state machine, "mcProcDraw", the row and element draws that show the save headers, the
"mcWNDProc" / "mcWNDProcDraw" message windows; sub_41BF80 was already main's); the name entry 0x45A3B0-0x45EBF8 (36:
"M_NameEntry", "M_Name_KeyProc", the input / cursor / confirm steps, the animation tracks, the draws, and the
field-event helpers on the task in 0x7CE6F8 that share the band).

**Skipped:** the libmc2 sequencers `H_Memcard_Init` 0x18F100 (sceDbcInit / sceMc2Init / sceMc2CreateSocket),
`H_Memcard_Check` 0x18F190 (sceMc2CheckAsync), `H_Memcard_UpdateSeqMode` 0x18F2C0, `sub_190590`, `sub_190720`,
`sub_190CD0`, `H_Memcard_UpdateChkAreaSeq` 0x191260, `sub_191660`: direct sceMc2* card calls in their own bodies (the
card driver stays recompiled). `sub_17B860` left alone (test_battle_panel). Nothing taken from the calendar slice's

climb_ref_17000 --snapshot-seeds 16 --jobs 3`): **faithful 123, differ 0, crash 0, hang 0** (375 s), on the readable

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) RwCamera: +104 / +108 the view window, +112 / +116 its reciprocals, +120 / +124 the view
offset, +128 / +132 near / far, +136 fog, +140 / +144 the device z scale / shift: the clip range (1 / near .. 1 / far
in perspective, near .. far in parallel) maps onto the device range 0x960088 .. 0x96008C narrowed by 1e-4 of itself at
both ends; the frustum planes at +148 (6 x 20 bytes: normal, distance = normal . a corner, three closest-corner bytes
= 1 for a non-negative normal component, else 0), the frustum's bounding box at +268 (maximum, then minimum), the 8
corners at +292. (2) The camera's world extension holds the visible-sector array (grown by 50), its count, the world
and the camera's own begin / end / sync callbacks, which the world wrappers call. The walk enters a plane's left side
when the frustum box's minimum on the plane's axis is below the left bound, its right side when the maximum is above
the right bound (the camera position's side first, the other order for a parallel camera), and keeps a sector unless a
frustum plane has the sector box's closest corner outside. (3) Object-to-sector ties are 24-byte records in two lists
(the sector's at +0, the object's at +12; +8 the object, +20 the sector); atomics tie through their world bounding
sphere's box, local lights (type bit 7) through their frame position +- radius; global lights (type < 0x80) sit in the
world's list at +60, local ones at +52. (4) BSP nodes: +0 the axis offset (< 0: a sector), +4 the plane, +8 / +12 the
children, +16 / +20 the children's bounds; a sector's +72 box is its cell (sub_499D30), its +96 box the vertex box
the older collision reader takes. (5) A collision block: flags (bit 0 a triangle map), the box (maximum first; the
stream holds the minimum first), u16 triangles / splits, the 16-aligned split array and the 2-aligned map in the same
allocation. (6) Header corrections (types delta): RwCamera +136 is the fog plane and +140 / +144 the z scale / shift
(the seed said +136 z shift, +140 / +144 view offset; the offset is at +120 / +124); RpMorphTarget +20 is the vertex
array, +24 the normals (only with geometry flag 0x10; the seed said +20 normals).

**Types delta.** `tools/ours/types/deltas/render_rw5.json`: RwCamera, RpLight, RpMaterial, RpClump, RpAtomic, RpWorld,
RpWorldSector, RpMorphTarget, RwImage, RpCollTree. `types_build.py` takes it (the regenerated headers are not
committed): found / known RwCamera 13 / 23 (was 8 / 11), RpAtomic 15 / 20 (14 / 17), RpWorld 7 / 12 (3 / 6),
RpWorldSector 4 / 11 (1 / 3), new records RpLight 7 / 13, RwImage 7 / 7, RpCollTree 5 / 7, RpMorphTarget 4 / 4, RpClump
1 / 4; 0 conflicts.

**What.** 162 functions of the battle bands 0x27BBA0-0x311310 (game/src/battle/battle3.cpp, roles and layouts in

the next emission overwrote it) on the battle route to vblank 6150 (307 functions hit) and the full climb to vblank
39820 (786 hit); of those, the leaf-first closure over the callees (pseudocode facts, then every `gen::` callee of the
generated bodies re-checked against main's replaced.txt) left 213, minus the battle UI part 0x271230-0x27BBA0
(battle_ui3), the model manager band, the functions other tests stand in with recorders (0x282D40, 0x2879F0,
0x288110, 0x2D3D70, 0x2DD9B0, 0x2FF260 / 0x2FF340 / 0x2FF3E0 / 0x2FF760, test_battle_core2) and their two callers
(sub_2826D0, sub_2831C0), sub_2E4430 (its callee sub_2C1CE0 was battle_ui3's, unmerged then), the two sound-driver
callers sub_2E2920 / sub_2E2A60, and two colour-fade updates (sub_29F150 / sub_29F760, VU0 float only) to stay near
160. Groups:
- the unit packets (kinds 271 / 272 / 274 / 277 / 278 / 279 / 280 / 281 / 282: creators, hold / release callbacks on
  the unit's busy count +160, the updates: look at a point / a unit, stop looking, the VU0 tint fade, show / hide the
  model parts, aura off, move) and the motion helpers (row from the table 0x693290 or the boss remap, frames, blend);
- the fade / effect handles and objects, the camera hooks, the result pop-up and skill-name banners, the
  "battle_command_calc" destroy;
- the all-out attack: the check `sub_28A200` [btlCheckAllOutAttack] (hero able, every living enemy knocked down, the
  joining members into gBtl +2952 / +2968) and the state ROUNDUP_MES `sub_298060`; the action states CHANGE FORMATION
  (init), PERSONA (init), DEAD (update); the one-more check `sub_28A3E0`; the effect-request flush `sub_28A780`;
- the rolls: advantage `sub_2D50C0`, escape `sub_2D4ED0`, ailment skip `sub_2DC070` and recovery `sub_2DC180` (the
  datScriptCalc formulas 8..14, skills 610 / 611), the shadow variant `sub_2D5570`; the action cost `sub_2D8110`;
- the battle grid (`sub_2D2280`: cell = round((int)(x + 1750) / 25); corners, placement, re-placement);
- the support (navigator) line pickers of the table 0x6978F0 (rows 15, 22, 27) and the party voice lines;
- the boss rules: index map, motion remap (encounters 0x1A0..0x1B4), event scheduler (417..436), work words;
- the enemy AI: the unit finder `sub_2C0E30` [btlAIFindUnit] and counter `sub_2C0F40`, eleven conditions of the table
  0x6971B0 (MYHP MYMP FRLV_O FRCNT ENCNT SENSEI MYHANSYA MYWEAK TURN ENOVERLV MYHOJO, the table's own strings), the
  fallback target selector AI (row 0 of 0x6975E0, `sub_2C3770`: weighted towards the lowest HP ratio with the weights
  0x696FA0 = {100} {60 40} {60 30 10} {40 30 20 10}), the support auto-target `sub_2C0AC0`, the best-skill pick
  `sub_2C48A0`, the command decoder `sub_2C6A00`, the AICALC section-15 row evaluation `sub_2C6BA0` and its weighted
  entry pick `sub_2C6E30`, the AI target-record accessors.

**How.** p3fes_handgen bodies (0 refused). The readability pass: a register-type propagation over each body (typed loads
from gBtl / btlAction / btlUnit / DatUnit / packet / AI target record, copies, call returns, the if / else / loop
nesting) named 808 load / store offsets and 178 `$gp` slots with constants of the same value (`b3::gbtl::`, `act::`,
`unit::`, `dat::`, `pkt::`, `airec::` in the header -- a constant replaces only the number it equals, so a mistyped
register can at worst mislabel); every function has its role and, for `sub_` names, a proposed name in brackets;
75 gotos became structure (280 -> 205: the AI finder, ENOVERLV, the all-out check, the one-more check, the three motion
helpers, the support auto-target, the AI row evaluation, the best-skill pick) with host `bool`s where paths merge and
one `epilogue` lambda per function, each path keeping its statements, charges and check points in order. The rest are
the jump-table / compare ladders of the voice and boss tables and shared exits. Types: tools/ours/types/deltas/battle3.json
(gBtl, btlAction, btlUnit, the new BtlAiTargetRecord): whole program 1,769 known / 1,293 found / 13 conflicts ->
1,803 / 1,322 / 12; gBtl 77 / 63 -> 89 / 72, btlUnit 43 / 40 -> 56 / 53, btlAction 44 / 38 / 1 conflict -> 49 / 42 / 0
(the header's "u32 command word +112" is a u16 item id: `sub_2D8110` reads it with lhu), BtlAiTargetRecord 4 / 3.
**Skipped**: none of the 162; out of the list (see above) for tests that stand them in, an unmerged callee, the sound
driver below `sub_10A2E0` / `sub_10A720`.

**Findings.** (1) gBtl +2970 is not a round counter: 0 means "no escape" and the opening support line; the escape roll
adds AICALC section 6 [+2970 - 1] and [9 + +2972 - 1] (named kEscRowA / kEscRowB). (2) The AI command code 0x8005 writes
nothing (its case falls out of the decoder). (3) `sub_2C48A0`'s kind argument filters on SkillRecord +8 (0 = only
all-target skills, 1 = only single-target), not magic / physical. (4) `sub_2C6BA0` answers for set 0 before set 1,
combinations c0&c1&c2, c0&c1, c0&c2, c1&c2, c0, c1, c2, always; 8 = no answer.

**The battle state a co-op server would own** (header comment, in full there): gBtl (flags +12, advantage +26, outcome +28,
the btlMain state +692 / +696 / +700, the hero's action +328, the action list +332, the side lists +336..+364, the turn
order +584..+688, the all-out list +2952 / +2968, the escape counters +2970 / +2972, the boss work +2884..+2900, the
setup block +2984 / +3004 / +3012); per btlAction the uid, the state machine +12..+28, turns +32, one-more +40, the
unit +48, targets +56 / +106, the command +108 / +110 / +112, the AI target record +136..+194, the ailment turn
counters +1122 u8[24]; per btlUnit side / id / uid / flags / DatUnit; the DatUnits (party ones in gGlobalWork). The packet
queues are presentation but gate the turn flow (waits on "no packet of this owner left"): a server runs them or turns
each wait into a "clients done" barrier. The random source is datCalcRand 0x2FFBC0 -> effMiscRand(0) 0x357FD0 (a 4-word
shift register behind *(u32*)0x957BF0, the +-3 re-roll at 0x7CE510); the AI target picks, row picks and every roll of
this slice draw from it, and so do presentation paths (the random idle frame `sub_282BC0`, four camera shots, ~40
effect functions): a server that owns the stream must give presentation its own generator and then no longer
reproduces the original sequence -- a determinism decision for the multiplayer ADR.

  prelight gradient and the VU0 band builder `sub_333970` (side vectors from the camera, `vrsqrt`).

  draw; streak grids and textured two-frame quads), the class-10 / class-16 instance allocators, the streamer kinds 1 /
  2 of class 16 (rows 0x69C970).

  flare class 9 (13 elements of the styles at 0x69C9E0 along the light-centre axis), the shake object class 21, the

**How chosen.** A temporary per-function entry counter (count + the last call's $a0..$a2 and cycles) patched into the
recompiled bodies of the band in the gate tree (never committed; the next emission removed it), the battle, fusion and
dorm routes run on it: 115 of the 209 candidates run (battle 103, fusion 63, dorm 7; the hottest: the filter quad
builders `sub_348340` / `sub_348760`, 27,747 calls on battle; the kind-7 filter cells 2,812; the ribbon push
`sub_333970` 662). 112 of them are here, with 42 that complete the classes they belong to (class 13's slots, the class
2 / 15 / 4 / 5 / 7 / 9 siblings, the EPL constructors). Not taken (left recompiled): the unreached big bodies --
class 13's kinds (`sub_334310` .. `sub_3377F0`, lightning strands), class 12 kind 2 (`sub_338530` .. `sub_338AC0`),
class 10 kinds 3 / 7 / 9 (`sub_33B0D0` .. `sub_33BBE0`, `sub_33E700` .. `sub_33F2E0`, `sub_3402C0` .. `sub_341BA0` with
its debug printf), class 16 kind 3 (`sub_344AA0` .. `sub_345970`), particle-system type 11's update `sub_331650`, the
filter updates `sub_349FD0` / `sub_34A370` / `sub_34A650` / `sub_34AE30`, `sub_349620` / `sub_349090` / `sub_348950`;
`sub_34DC00` / `sub_34EAE0` stay with the rendering queue. No function of the band touches hardware registers, makes a
syscall or reaches the IOP / sound driver: nothing was skipped for a skip reason.

**Left out: `sub_343B60` [k16Streamer2Create]** (run on fusion). With it, `test_fx_types.cpp`'s kind-object case
failed one pair (`sub_345DB0 k16 create`, seed 3385080813): its random world gives the effect a negative block-A
pointer (0xFFFFCCF0), `sub_343B60` (now reached instead of a missing-function stop) raises the segment count at
params +140 to 3 there, and that address lies outside the RAM range the pair restores, so the recompiled run reads the
hand run's store (a check-point trace of both runs showed the first difference at that load; the same pair with the
class-16 kind slots in reference mode still failed, and `sub_343B60` / `sub_342890` / `sub_342480` / `sub_342550` /
`sub_345CF0` each matched their recompiled bodies on 1,500 random worlds). Per the brief the slice was trimmed rather
than the other test edited; with it out, fx_types / fx_epl / fx_layers / fx2 pass.

**Method.** The readability pass is reproducible: a spec (a role comment and a header brief per function, block
comments, the records with a (register -> record) map per function) applied by a script to the pristine generated
file; a constant replaces an offset only when its value is the instruction's offset. A check script confirms that,
comments dropped and constants replaced by their values, the five files equal the generator's output statement for
statement: **154 functions, 17,836 statements, 0 differ**. Constants named in the comments were read from the ELF
(0x7CAE4C = 1/255: the VU0 colour scale; 0x7CADA0 = 0.01: the filter curves are in percent; 0x7CAE50 / 0x7CAE90 =
2 pi, 0x7CAE58 = pi).

**Findings.** (1) fx_types' "track" (0x69C510) is a particle system: its type rows are {update, scale, state size,
parameter size}; the class-2 / 15 instances and the EPL kinds 3 / 4 own one. (2) Class 13's and class 12's kind tables
are six words {init, create, destroy, update, draw, size}, class 10's and 16's seven {init, create, destroy, clone,
update, draw, size}; class 13's kind destroy receives the instance, not the kind object. (3) Every class-10 kind's
draw, and class 12's kinds 1 / 3, are byte-identical bodies. (4) The kind-7 filter cell pulse goes through the
compiler's soft-double calls (fptodp / fabs / dpsub / dpmul / dptofp).

reference builds') at the vblanks where the band's effects are alive, with the instance each update / draw was last

## Phase 5 slice libc: the C runtime -- newlib leaves, libm, libgcc's 64-bit division and soft-float doubles (107 functions)

**What** (game/src/libc/{libc_string,libc_stdlib,libm,libgcc_div,libgcc_float}.cpp, game/include/p3fes/game/libc.h,
tests/game/test_libc.cpp, tools/ours/types/deltas/libc.json, symbols/deltas/libc.sym): the first library slice. All
107 bodies are p3fes_handgen's (0 refused), split by family into five files, then made readable by a scripted,
checked pass: a role comment per function (its C-standard contract plus what the instructions add: the MMI quadword
loops of mem* / str*, the has-zero-byte word test, the 16-bit-half schoolbook division with the bit-length table
0x7C0388, the fp-bit record layout), block roles in the string / division / mprec / trig bodies, and named offsets in
`libc.h` (`reent::` errno / setlocale category and name / Bigint free lists / strtok position, `bigint::`, `file::`
for the FILE record `std` initialises, `parts::` for the unpacked soft-float number). A normaliser (comments stripped,
every named constant evaluated) proves all 107 bodies token-equal to the generated ones.
- newlib 0x51E0E0-0x5287D8 (45): abs, atoi, bzero, quorem, `sub_51F690` [__errno], `std` [FILE init], _setlocale_r,
  setlocale, localeconv, _mbtowc_r, memchr, memcmp, memcpy, memmove, memset, _Bfree, _hi0bits, _lo0bits, __mcmp, _ulp,
  _b2d, _ratio, _mprec_log10, copysign, scalbn, copysignf, scalbnf, eofread, strcasecmp, strcat, strchr, strcmp,
  strcpy, strlen, strncat, strncpy, strrchr, strstr, strtok, _strtol_r, strtol, _strtoul_r, strtoul, exponent, __sccl.
- libm 0x528AE0-0x52EA60 (31): __ieee754_acos / log / log10 / sqrt, __ieee754_acosf / asinf / powf / rem_pio2f /
  sqrtf, __kernel_cos / sin / rem_pio2, __kernel_cosf / sinf / tanf / rem_pio2f, floor, atanf, cosf, fabsf, floorf,
  sinf, tanf, acos, log10, acosf, asinf, atan2f, logf, powf, sqrtf (atan2f and logf are two-chunk functions: a stub at
  the entry, the body at 0x52B380 / 0x52B548).
- libgcc 0x52EA78-0x5318F8 (31): __muldi3, __divdi3, __moddi3, __udivdi3, __umoddi3, __udivmoddi4 and its copies
  __udivmoddi4_0 / _2, __floatdidf, __floatdisf, __fixunsdfdi, __fixdfdi, __pack_f, __unpack_f, __make_fp, __pack_d,
  __unpack_d, _fpadd_parts, dpadd, dpsub, dpmul, _fpmul_parts, dpdiv, _fpdiv_parts, __fpcmp_parts_d, dpcmp, litodp,
  dptoli, __make_dp, dptofp, dptoul.

Findings from the bodies (all checked by the tests): the soft-float library never rounds (add / mul / div truncate,
`__pack_d` drops the 8 guard bits; every result is the host's correctly rounded double or the next one toward zero),
flushes denormals to zero, and returns the NaN record 0x7C0488 for Inf - Inf, 0 * Inf, 0 / 0; `__unpack_f` treats
exponent 0xFF as an ordinary exponent (the EE has no single Inf / NaN) and `__pack_f` saturates only past it;
`long` is 64-bit (strtol's cut-off goes through __udivdi3 / __umoddi3); scalbnf takes the integer in $a0;
`_hi0bits` ends on a 64-bit `bgez` (callers pass sign-extended words); 0x531998 onwards (the 20-byte "atan2l / cosl /
coshl / expl / hypotf" stubs and everything after) is other libraries (they call 0x5649A8... in the CRI band), as are
the "numbered copies" (sinl_9, atan2l_10, __env_lock_N, sceLibgcc32GetErxEntries_N) in 0x56D000-0x57FFFF.

**Kept recompiled, with the reason** (every other named function of 0x51E0E0-0x531998):
- heap or kernel in the body or below it: malloc / cfree / realloc / calloc (stood in by the heap tests), _malloc_r,
  _realloc_r, malloc_extend_top, _calloc_r, _free_r, _malloc_trim_r, __malloc_lock / __malloc_unlock (QueryIntrContext
  / DIntr / EIntr), _sbrk_r, _read_r, _write_r, _close_r, _kill_r, `_execve_r` (lseek), `_fork_r` (malloc + isatty);
  _Balloc (-> _calloc_r) and its users _multadd, _s2b, _i2b, _multiply, _pow5mult, _lshift, __mdiff, _d2b, _dtoa_r,
  _strtod_r, strtod, strtodf;
- stdio (fflush, the FILE callbacks through jalr, the file syscalls): `_getpid_r` (the buffered-write routine),
  _fwalk, fflush, lflush, _sprintf_r (-> vfprintf), __srefill, ungetc, __submore, __sprint, __sbprintf, vfprintf, cvt, vfscanf, __svfscanf,
  _vfscanf_r, __svfscanf_r, sscanf, _sscanf_r, __swsetup, __sread, __swrite, __sseek, __sclose, fread, exit, __sinit,
  __sfp, __sfmoreglue, _cleanup(_r);
- stood in by another slice's test (a replaced callee cannot be stood in): printf / sprintf / vsprintf (stand_ins.h),
  isinf / isnan (test_field3_units), fabs (test_field3_kosaka, test_field3_camera), cos / sin (test_events2), fptodp
  (test_events), strncmp (test_models); and what calls them: pow, __ieee754_pow (fabs), __ieee754_rem_pio2 (fabs; only
  cos / sin use it), __fixunssfdi (fptodp);
- mid-body entries: _printf_r, _vsprintf_r (jump into vfprintf at loc_5262B0);
- qsort: 24 comparator calls through jalr; needs a guest comparator to pair -- left for the next library slice.

**Tests** (test_libc.cpp, 10 cases): the generic sweep (32 random worlds per function, 3,424 pairs, 658 stopped
identically) and meaningful sections, each with hand / recompiled pairs plus bulk documented-rule checks on the
recompiled body: `<string.h>` on random buffers / strings at every alignment and the word loops' edge lengths against
the host (396 pairs); strtok / setlocale / localeconv / __errno / mbtowc state in the _reent over call sequences (27);
strtol / strtoul / atoi against strtoll / strtoull with end pointer and errno = ERANGE (800 conversions, 108 pairs);
the 64-bit helpers against host u64 / s64 incl. powers of two and the extreme values (23,896 results, 480 pairs);

comparisons and integer conversions exact; specials (4,000 operand pairs, 518 pairs); pack / unpack record layout and

logf 1 ulp; atanf, atan2f, powf 2 ulps; sqrtf, floorf, fabsf, scalbnf, copysignf exact; acos, log10, log 1 ulp;

**What.** 163 functions (45,172 bytes) of the RW band in `game/src/render/render_rw6.cpp` /
`game/include/p3fes/game/render_rw6.h`, started from `p3fes_handgen` (0 refused) and made readable the way render_rw4 /
render_rw5 were: each function's role (proposed names in brackets, `symbols/deltas/render_rw6.sym`, 155 rows), the role
of the main blocks (the collision walks labelled phase by phase: the BSP stack, the plane / split interval tests, the
sector's collision block, the tree's root entry, the inside / outside bits, the leaf triangles through the triangle map,
the triangle test, the collision triangle and the callback), the record offsets named (`rw6::` beside `rw4::` / `rw5::`:
isect / colltri / tri / wsect / geo / interp / collsplit / pnode / allmatpriv / allmatinit / rtfs / rtfile / path2d /
seg2d / devreq) and the RW globals labelled. The readable file is produced from the generated one by a scratch tool that
only adds comments and replaces literal load / store offsets by those names for the base registers a per-function spec
names, and checks that the code token stream with the names resolved equals the generated body's (121,075 tokens,
equal). No structural rewrites (the 285 `goto`s p3fes_handgen leaves are shared blocks of the walks' explicit stacks).
Groups:
* **Collision** (12, 24,752 bytes -- the size render_rw5 left them for): the three world walks behind
  `RpCollisionWorldForAllIntersections` -- line `sub_45F930`, sphere `sub_460EC0`, box `sub_4606B0` --, the geometry
  tests behind `RpAtomicForAllIntersections` -- the atomic's sphere into its space `sub_463F20`, line / sphere through
  the geometry's collision tree `sub_461EA0` / `sub_462BB0` or every triangle `sub_461900` / `sub_461D00`, line /
  sphere on the vertices blended between two morph targets `sub_463490` / `sub_463B20` --, and the triangle tests
  `sub_4BAE00` (sphere / triangle, with the contact normal and distance) and `sub_4BB5D0` (box / triangle, separating
  axes).
* **Rt2d** (87): the CTM stack's open / close, `Rt2dCTMTranslate` / `Rt2dCTMScale`, the path pieces (`Rt2dPathEmpty`,
  `Rt2dPathLineto`, `Rt2dPathCurveto`, the bounds, the even-odd point-inside test), the polygon helpers of the fill
  triangulation (create, split, destroy, the corner side, the point-in-triangle classification), the brush / shape /
  scene / object / maestro list and queue helpers, the toolkit's free lists and 2-D pipelines (`rt2dPS2PipeOpen`).
* **RtFS** (22): the manager's file-system list (register, lookup by name, the name check, the device lookup, the
  device-prefix skip), a file system's init, the generic ('host:') file system (creation, file records, operations),
  the fread / fwrite / fseek / feof adaptors, the end-of-file test, the completion of a file operation.
* **sList and the error module** (11): get-new-entries (growth by n + a quarter), destroy, to-array, the end, the
  count drop, the data getter, `RwErrorGet`, the error / module open / close counters.
* **PS2AllMat and the PS2 pipelines** (22): `RxPipelineNodeCreateInitData` / `RxPipelineNodeGetInitData`, the
  tri-list / tri-strip / point batch set-ups, the node's callbacks / VU1 code array / VIF offset, the PS2 pipeline-id
  plugin of geometries, atomics and world sectors (constructor, stream-always and rights callbacks, registration), the
  default material / sector / atomic pipelines from `RpPDSGetPipe`.
* **Engine** (9): `_rwDeviceSystemRequest` with the single-sub-system standard answers, `RwEngineGetVideoModeInfo`,
  `RwEngineGetCurrentVideoMode`, `RwEngineSetVideoMode`, `RwEngineGetVersion`, `RwEngineRegisterPlugin`,

**Not taken / skipped.** (1) `sub_464020` (`RpCollisionWorldForAllIntersections`, the dispatch by intersection type)
and `sub_464120` (`RpAtomicForAllIntersections`): `test_field3_collision`, `test_field3_event` and `test_render_game2`
stand them in, and a replaced function cannot be stood in; every test they dispatch to is in this slice. (2) The known
stand-in conflicts of render_rw5's section and every RW-band address another slice's test file names (stand-ins,
recorders), with their callers. (3) The 0x4C0000 / 0x4D0000 hardware bands (DMA / VIF / GS register users) were not
considered; the PDS pipe constructors (0x46A0F0-0x46A970) and the 0x490000 clump / atomic leftovers were left for a
later pass to keep the slice at its size (no technical reason); `sub_4A5540`'s neighbours 0x4A5470-0x4AA540 (Rt2d's
object / font layer) likewise. None of the 163 touches hardware registers, makes a syscall or talks to the IOP in its
own body: the device requests reach the PS2 driver only through the device's system function, the RtFS adaptors the
CD / host layers only through a file system's operations.

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) The collision callbacks: world walks (a0 = the intersection, a1 = the sector, a2 = the
collision triangle, $f12 = the distance, a3 = the data), geometry walks (a0 = the intersection, a1 = the triangle, $f12,
a2 = the data); 0 stops the walk. Distances: the line's t in [0, 1]; the sphere's plane distance / radius; the box 0.
(2) Lines take front faces only (det = e1 . (d x e2) > 1e-8; edges within 1e-5 of det). (3) A collision tree's split
is two 8-byte child entries {u8 type (bits 2..3 the axis offset), u8 count (0xFF = a split), u16 index, f32 bound}; a
block without splits is one leaf of all its triangles; the triangle map (when present) gives each leaf's triangles.
(4) The sphere and box walks carry six inside / outside bits per child (which faces of the child's box the query's
inner box crosses): a subtree inside the sphere's inscribed box or inside the query box is reported whole, untested
(so a sphere walk's result equals the all-triangles test's). (5) The snapshots' worlds hold no triangles (their
sectors are empty, no collision block): the field and dungeon collision is the atomics' geometry collision trees (73
geometries in dorm_replay_4900, 114 in climb_ref_17000, 6 in b_5800). (6) RtFS: the generic file system's 92-byte record
(operations at +20..+76, name at +80, the 112-byte file records at +88); a file's state 4 (after a seek) makes the
completion callback receive the position. (7) Rt2d path segments: 24 bytes {type, x, y, unit normal (dy, -dx) / length,
the running length}; the previous point's normal becomes the mitre (n0 + n1) / (n0 . (n0 + n1)) once the sub-path has
two points.

**Types delta.** `tools/ours/types/deltas/render_rw6.json`: RpIntersection, RpInterpolator, RxPipelineNode, RwSList,
RtFileSystem, RtFile, Rt2dPath (anchored on their accessors). `types_build.py` takes it (the regenerated headers are not
committed): found / known RpIntersection 3 / 3, RpInterpolator 4 / 6, RxPipelineNode 3 / 3, RwSList 4 / 4 (instances in
all six snapshots), RtFileSystem 6 / 13 (3 instances in each snapshot), RtFile 8 / 10, Rt2dPath 4 / 4; 0 conflicts.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_rw6.cpp`, 12 cases, 270,592 assertions, 331 s on MSVC Release). Every pair
compares the whole register file and cycles at every check point, all 32 MiB (dead stack included), the scratchpad, the
bus log, the stand-ins' call logs and heaps, and the collision callback's calls (triangle index, distance). Collision, on

(mostly against a face's normal, through a surface point) and spheres through the tree walks and the all-triangles
tests -- the tree walk reports exactly the all-triangles test's triangles, and both what the host's double-precision
test finds (front-face line / triangle, closest-point sphere distance; a triangle within 1e-3 of a boundary may go either
way): 113 line and 5,846 sphere reports, every clear hit found, no clear miss reported; a tenth of the queries stop at
the first callback (at most one call); the atomic sphere test on 32 live atomics (96 pairs, host check in world space
through the LTM: 3,031 reports); the world line / sphere / box walks on 48 worlds built around those geometries (one

geometry walks report and the host's separating-axis box test finds (1,059 box reports, distance 0); the morph-target
tests on geometries given a second, displaced morph target (64 pairs; the blended vertices of the host; start = end
equals the one-target test); the sphere / triangle and box / triangle tests on 600 random triangles each against the
host (the contact normal unit and parallel to the face, the distance the centre's signed plane distance). Documented

**What.** `game/src/ui/font2.cpp` (`font2.h`): 114 p3fes_handgen bodies made readable -- a role comment above every function
(and in the header; proposed names in brackets, 101 rows in `symbols/deltas/font2.sym`), the globals as named constants
`font2::fnt / rw / pad / dbg / bust / fade / snd / spr / fx` and the record offsets as typed views `line / glyph / cache /

literal it replaces: 287 globals, 23 named symbols, 352 field offsets), block comments in the glyph-cache path, two bodies
restructured without their `goto`s (`frFontCacheGlyph`'s hit / miss join, `sub_3AE420`'s two range asserts); the other 112
are token-identical to the generated bodies once comments are dropped and the constants are replaced by their values (a
second script checks this, and that the 114 shims are unchanged). The header documents the glyph pipeline: text -> glyph
nodes -> the glyph cache (hit: one more reference to the slot's cache record; miss: Huffman-decode, take a raster slot,
swizzle into its raster, register a GS-list entry) -> frFontDraw -> the chain release and the slot ageing that make a glyph

**Corrections to earlier docs.** font.h calls the line node's +0xC the glyph count: `frFontBuildGlyphList` adds every
advance there (the width, 1/16 px) and counts glyphs in +0x18; its +0x20 is the last glyph (the types header called it
a style record) and the glyph node's +0x24 the previous glyph (`frFontBuildGlyphList` stores the old tail there; the kerning
is taken off it). The types delta `tools/ours/types/deltas/font2.json` records these (FrFontLineNode, FrFontGlyphNode,
FrFontGlyphCache, FontRasterSlot, FontRasterSlotManager, FrFontStyle, FmGslEntry: 0 conflicts after the rebuild; the slot
manager 6 of 6 fields known, was 4). On a "slot without cache record" miss `frFontCacheGlyph` passes the caller's `$s3` to
`frFontRegisterGlyphRaster` (the original never sets it on that path; kept).

the list window animation exist (three identical); sub_40C150 computes a flag bit into $v1 and returns nothing.

## Phase 5 slice boot: the boot and file-setup band 0x18A3F0-0x19FF10 (141 functions, 2026-10-23)

The engine and the server need to know what the game does from power-on to the first playable frame and what a new
game starts with; this slice takes the game side of the boot. 141 functions in three files, generated by p3fes_handgen
(0 refused) and made readable: `game/src/boot/boot.cpp` (73: 0x191D10-0x1997A0), `boot_panels.cpp` (45:
0x18A3F0-0x18F0E0), `boot_scene.cpp` (23: 0x199C60-0x19FF10), headers `boot.h` / `boot_panels.h` / `boot_scene.h`. A
role comment for every function (proposed names in brackets, ADR-0009), named offsets (`boot::task / rw / node / fs`),
block roles, and every `goto` of the generated bodies turned into structured flow (0 left): the jump-table state
machines' shared "return 0" blocks became host flags after the switch (a structure-only transform: each path keeps its
statements, charges and check points in order), the two loops' found-blocks moved into the loop, the shared tails of
the cut-in's unit tables written out in their cases.

**THE BOOT SEQUENCE** (`boot.h` has it in full, with the call order): main ("jpx235") -> initAndLoop -> kwlnMain;
kwlnInitPS2Systems (IOP reboot with IOPRP310.IMG, 15 modules: SIO2MAN, SIO2D, PADMAN, DBCMAN, MC2_S1, LIBSD,
CRI_ADXI, SDRDRV, MODHSYN, MODMSIN, MODSESQ, SKSOUND, SKHSYNTH x2, SKSESQ); kwlnInitRenderer (RW, video mode 82,
640 x 448 camera); kwlnInitMain (CDVD, sound, ADX, the vsync callback, the CVM volumes data / bgm / btl, then the game
modules' inits in order -- the debug printer, the effect programs, the battle .TBLs, the fonts, the field main script,
camp/fade_pak.pak, camp/areapnl.pak and camp/ptypnl.pak read synchronously, ...); the main loop (root task +

# Phase 5 slice sce1 â€” the pure parts of the Sony runtime libraries (2026-10-23)

70 functions of the Sony libraries linked into the ELF, replaced by p3fes_handgen bodies (70 generated, 0 refused) in
`game/src/sce/{sce_graph,sce_kernel,sce_printf,sce_mc2path}.cpp`, declarations and named layouts in
`game/include/p3fes/game/sce.h`, tests in `tests/game/test_sce1.cpp`. The Sony SDK is proprietary: the work used the
binary (the handgen bodies, the pseudocode reference) and public GS / VIF / GIF register documentation only; names are
symbols/functions.json's (ADR-0009), `[proposed]` roles beside the 12 `sub_` names. A normaliser proves all 70 bodies
token-equal to the generated ones (comments dropped, the named offsets of `sce.h` folded back).

The pure set is smaller than the 120-160 the prompt aimed at: the ELF has no libvu0 / libvif code under sce names, and
most of what remains of these libraries touches hardware, makes syscalls or is an IOP driver. Stopped at the pure set.

- **libgraph** (6): `checkModelVersion` (rom0:ROMVER through sceOpen / sceRead / sceClose -- IOP file requests, stood in
  by the tests), `sceGsSetDefDispEnv` (PMODE / SMODE2 / DISPFB / DISPLAY / BGCOLOR for NTSC / PAL / 480p; the DX / DY
  corrections of `_sce_GetGsDxDyOffset` asked for every mode but NTSC / PAL), `sceGszbufaddr`, `sceGsSetDefDrawEnv` /
  `sceGsSetDefDrawEnv2` (8 A+D pairs; context 2's FBW has no +63 rounding), `sceGsSetDefStoreImage` (MSKPATH3 / FLUSHA /
  DIRECT + GIF tag + BITBLTBUF / TRXPOS / TRXREG / FINISH / TRXDIR). The builders' stores use `sce::disp::` /
  `sce::draw::` / `sce::store::` / `sce::gparam::` offsets.
- **libdma** (3): `CheckAddress` (scratchpad -> SPR flag), `memclr`, `sceDmaGetEnv` (copies the shadow at 0x965AC8).
- **libkernel** (51): the newlib glue (open / close / ioctl / lseek / isatty / fstat / getpid / kill / stat / unlink),
  `sceResetttyinit`; the tty ring (`QueueInit`, `QueuePeekWriteDone` / `ReadDone`, `sceTtyRead`), `deci2Putchar`,
  `serialPutchar`, the small printf (`_sceSnprintf`, `printfloat`, `ftoi`, `snprintf_char`, `printf_char`,
  `kprintf_char`, `_sceSnprintf_pf`, `sceVsnprintf`, `sceSnprintf` -- the sinks take the character in `$a2` and skip
  NULs); the SIF software registers and command tables (`_set_sreg`, `_change_addr`, `sceSifGetSreg` / `SetSreg`,
  `sceSifGetDataTable`, `sub_506400` / `sub_506418` / `sub_506430` [set user / system table, add handler]); the alarm
  pool (`sub_50E190` insert by key, `sub_50E218` unlink, `sub_50E5D8` allocate: id = record << 4 | odd 10-bit tag,
  `sub_50E690` free, `sub_50E7A0` status, `sub_50EB50` time left), the 147,456,000 Hz conversions (`sub_50EE38`,
  `sub_50EEE0`, `sub_50EF50`, `sub_50EFA8`), `_InitAlarm`, `AlarmHandler` (jalr to the user handler), `_fs_version` /
  `_lf_version`, `__sceKernlGetEhSemaId`, `sub_50D840` [byte copy], `nullsub_131`.
- **libmc2** (8): `instr`, `isCorrNameSize`, `isCorrFname`, `isPathCurParent`, `isWildFit`, `_strtok`, `_get_dir_nest`,
  `_make_path` (pure string code; the card / FAT code stays).
- **libdbc** (2): `_get_free_slot`, `DPRINT` (empty).

**Kept recompiled** (for the native-port phase): everything in these libraries that touches hardware in its own body or
makes a syscall or talks to the IOP --

  btl_eff.pac request and its ten battle-effect EPLs (create / release / destroy), **the exit ("hit") table** request
  `K_Fldrc_RequestFieldHitTableFile` and install `sub_1C7F20`, the party units' finish step `sub_1CE960`
  [K_FldUnit_FinishPcs], and the transparent-wall control of the field camera -- "trans wall CTL" (`sub_1C1F30`
  create, `sub_1C0D70` update: two rays from the camera to the target unit fade field objects (alpha byte) and
  Tartarus block atomics (material alpha) out and back in), its destroy, the "RMD fade CTL" / "atomic fade CTL"
  destroy callbacks;

  camera turns, the party hide / re-create steps, the dark-hour pair 0x1E7 / 0x1E8;

so every remaining function was taken rather than measuring reach; 60 of the 104 call game functions that are still
recompiled (162 distinct: mostly the battle-UI band 0x200000-0x27FFFF, the sound / BGM helpers 0x108570-0x10A4E0 and the
models band), which the bodies reach through their
`gen::` entry points as every other slice's do.

**Method.** p3fes_handgen bodies (0 refused), made readable by a reproducible spec per file (role block with the
proposed name per function, block comments at the key blocks and the state-machine cases, named offsets each
replacing exactly its literal); a check script confirms that the five files, comments dropped and names replaced by
their values, equal the generator's output: **104 functions, 19,712 statements, 0 differ**. 479 named-offset uses;
165 gotos remain (the shared blocks of the state machines).

**Findings.**
1. *The exit table.* Every field's table is a member `hMMM_NNN.bin` of its `DATA/FIELD/PACK/FMMM_NNN.PAC` (208
   tables, 867 records on this disc; no loose `field/table/` file). Record = 44 bytes: three gating flags, kind
   (face a side), prompt (confirm button + icon), area name, script procedure or 0xFFFF = door, the door's next
   major / minor / entry, door object / animation / sound, side. 157 doors (91 lead somewhere, every destination
   has a pack; 66 only animate), 24 script records carry ids the event task does not read, 164 records are flag-gated,
   678 need the confirm button. The table is the action half of the field's hits: the HBN hit resource's `id & 0x3FF`
   indexes it. 199 of 208 tables end in 4..28 pad bytes; the installer drops them (count = size / 44, divu).
2. *A dead check.* `K_Fldrc_RequestFieldHitTableFile` means to return 0 for major 0xFFFF, but compares the
   16-bit-masked major (`andi 0xFFFF`) with -1 (`li v0, -1`): never equal, so 0xFFFF asks for `h65535_NNN.bin` like any
   other major (tested on both bodies).
3. *Shuffle Time's result step machine* (`sub_1F6A60`): steps 0 and 3 re-dispatch themselves forever (the game never
   enters them); the pair test leaves them out.
4. The COMM handlers' resource-type switch takes `(id & 0xFFC00) >> 10` (types 1 / 3 / 10 use different model fields,
   +296 / +296 / +260); other types K_Assert and fall through (`jr $ra` in retail).

**Pair tests** (gate tree, MSVC 14.44 Release): **23 cases, 78,075 assertions** (the five files). Random worlds for all 104 (32-64 seeds each, every random
draw its own statement); real data: every exit table of the disc parsed on the host against the documented layout
(the counts above as checks), 16 real tables installed through `sub_1C7F20` (count, bytes, node destroyed), the request
rules incl. the dead 0xFFFF test; climb_ref_17000's dungeon task (script request / install of DUNGEONAT.BF / free),
the btl_eff.pac request and EPL teardown, the live "trans wall CTL" tasks of climb_ref_17000 and b_6700 (update, stop

## Phase 5: rendering -- RenderWare, seventh pass: RpMatFX, RpMorph, the PDS registry, PTank, RpRandom, RpSpline, RpUserData, the world's streams, Rt2d brushes and fonts (render_rw7, 170 functions, 2026-10-23)

**What.** 170 functions (46,744 bytes) of the RW band in `game/src/render/render_rw7.cpp` /
`game/include/p3fes/game/render_rw7.h`, started from `p3fes_handgen` (0 refused) and made readable the way render_rw4..6
were: each function's role (proposed names in brackets, `symbols/deltas/render_rw7.sym`, 166 rows), the role of the main
blocks, the record offsets named (`rw7::` beside `rw4::`..`rw6::`: mfx / mfxslot / mfxbump / mfxenv / mfxdual / mfxuv,
morphgeo / morphkey / morphatom, pdsreg, rrand, spline, uda / udlist, meshhdr / mesh / geoext, ptankdata, tsedge / tstri,
objsetup, font2d / brush2d, rxpipe / rxnodedef) and the RW globals labelled. As in render_rw6, a scratch tool only adds
comments and replaces literal load / store offsets by those names for the base registers a per-function spec names, and
checks that the code token stream with the names resolved equals the generated body's (125,642 tokens, equal). Groups:
* **RpMatFX** (43, plugin 0x120): open / close, the 132-byte material extension (two 64-byte effect slots, flags +128),
  its reset / destructor / stream write / size, the atomic and sector "effects enabled" words with their streams,
  `RpMatFXPluginAttach`, `RpMatFXWorldSectorEnableEffects`, `RpMatFXMaterialGetEffects`, every slot getter / setter
  (bump frame / texture / coefficient, environment frame / texture / coefficient / frame-buffer alpha, dual texture /
  blend modes, UV matrices), the passes' default GS words and the dual / environment ALPHA words.
* **RpMorph** (13, plugin 0x105): the atomic state, the geometry's 20-byte interpolation keys (copy, stream read /
  write / size, `RpMorphGeometryCreateInterpolators`), the default key-end callback, `RpMorphPluginAttach`.
* **PDS** (9, plugin 0x131) and the pipeline core it needs: the registry set-up / destroy, the engine close, the
  material / atomic / sector rights callbacks (`RpPDSGetPipe` of the streamed id), `RpPDSPluginAttach`,
  `RxPipelineDestroy` and the node destroy (locked: removed in place, inputs re-indexed; unlocked: the definition's terms).
* **PTank** (11, plugin 0x12F): the atomic extension, the registration, the data allocations by format (separate /
  interleaved, RpPTank's data flags and strides), the data size, the pipeline record's creation, the buffer ring, the
  instance-buffer release, the three PS2All object set-ups (transform, frustum clip flag; the lit one's reinstance
  flags and lights).
* **RpRandom** (6, plugin 0x10C): `RpRandom` (`sub_488F30`), `RpRandomSeed`, the open / close, the registration,
  `RpRandomSeedMT` -- below.
* **RpSpline** (9, plugin 0x102): the basis tables, the open splines' end matrices, the open / close, the control-point
  solve, `RpSplineSetControlPoint`, `RpSplineFindPosition` (the field camera's spline path), the registration.
* **RpUserData** (27, plugin 0x11F): arrays and per-object lists (create / add, copy, destroy, stream read / write /
  size), the array accessors (`RpUserDataArrayGetName` is the 2-instruction body named `name__C9type_info_0`, shared
  with type_info::name), `RpUserDataGetFormatSize`.
* **The world's streams and helpers** (37): the pipeline-id streams of atomics / sectors, the bin-mesh header streams
  of geometries and sectors, the mesh serial, the tri-strip edge / triangle records, the BSP teardown walks, the world
  plugin registrations, the native-data sizes and DMA-chain relocation, a PS2All node's init / callback setter / node
  definition (`sceLibgcc32GetErxEntries` returns it: the symbol name is not its role), `RpLightStreamRead`,
  `RpMaterialStreamRead`, the plugin-0x122 loader the resource manager's thread calls (`sub_464540`, `sub_4643B0`).
* **Rt2d brushes and fonts** (15): `Rt2dBrushCreate`, `Rt2dBrushSetRGBA`, the UV / texture set-ups, the brush stream
  read, the font's high-code map, the font module's open / close, `Rt2dFontSetPath`, `Rt2dFontGetStringWidth` (x the
  height in $f12), the font destroy, `Rt2dFontIsUnicode`.

**RpRandom -- the Tartarus generator's random source** (field4: `sub_488F30` is the floor generator's only random
call). The classic BSD additive generator (TYPE_3): a 31-word table (124 bytes, RwMalloc'd by the plugin open) and
four pointers in the plugin's engine block at `0x960070 + [gp 0x7CE778]`: +0 table, +4 front, +8 rear, +12 end.
`RpRandom`: `*front += *rear`, result `*front >> 1` (31 bits, zero-extended), both pointers step (front wraps to the
table and rear then steps unchecked; else rear wraps) -- x[n] = x[n-31] + x[n-3], front three words ahead of rear.
`RpRandomSeed(s)`: table[0] = s, table[i] = table[i-1] x 1103515245 + 12345, front = table + 3, rear = table, 310 draws
discarded. The open seeds 0x9A319039, kwlnMain reseeds once per boot from the T0 counter: a run's whole sequence
follows from that seed and the number of draws since (what a deterministic co-op Tartarus needs to share). The live
generators of dorm_replay_4900, b_5800 and climb_ref_17000 satisfy the invariants and continue exactly as the host
model does. `RpRandomSeedMT` fills a separate 624-word table (0x95D410: seed | 1, then x 69069 products).

**Not taken / skipped.** (1) The known stand-in conflicts of the prompt and every RW-band address another slice's test
names (stand-ins, recorders, `_callees`), and their callers. (2) The anim ranges, the `_rwDMA*` / VIF / GS hardware
functions (the PTank instance writers / streamers `sub_476140 ..`, `sub_47C240 ..`: hardware registers in their own
bodies) and the 0x4C0000 / 0x4D0000 bands. (3) The PDS pipe constructors (`RpPDSRegisterPipe`, `PDSRegistryAddPipe`,
`RpPDSSkyMatPipeCreate`, `sub_46A8D0`, `sub_46AC30`, `sub_46AFA0`, the engine open `sub_46A600`), the PTank / spr pipe
builders (`rpSpr2dGenCreatePS2AllMatPipe`, `rpSpr3dGenCreatePS2AllMatPipe`, `sub_479030`, `sub_47A3D0`, `sub_47AB70`,
`sub_47B1A0`, `sub_474BB0`, `sub_474C60`) and the default-pipeline builders `sub_49C680 ..`: they need the RxPipeline
lock / add-fragment / unlock core (0x4F2F70, 0x4F3F80 with its cluster / topological-sort helpers 0x4F31C0 ..
0x4F7080, ~30 functions) -- callable only since libc's memset / memcpy reached main during this slice; left for the
next pass with that core (no technical reason beyond the size). (4) The world / clump stream readers `sub_48F580`,
`sub_48FBD0`, `sub_490050` and the 0x490000 clump / atomic bodies behind the known conflicts (`sub_490D40`,
`sub_4916D0`, `sub_491EA0`, `sub_492D10`, `sub_494D50`) and their callers. None of the 170 touches hardware registers,
makes a syscall or talks to the IOP in its own body (`sub_49F500` stores a GIF tag into memory with `sq`).

**Rules worth knowing.** (1) RpMatFX: the slot of an effect is the first of the two whose type (+32) is that effect;
a getter / setter of an effect the material lacks reads / writes address 0 + offset (the original faults there). Flags
-> slot types: 1 (1, 0), 2 (2, 0), 3 (1, 2), 4 (4, 0), 5 (5, 0), 6 (5, 4) -- all 38 live effect records of the three
snapshots agree. The bump coefficient is stored negated. (2) User data: an unnamed array read back keeps whatever its
name word held (the reader skips a 0 length); an int / real array without elements cannot be read (the 0-byte read
fails) and the list reader then continues with a null stream. (3) Bin-mesh: the size counts the header's total index
count (+8), the write each mesh's own -- 6 of the b_5800 geometries carry a total of 0 (their sizes differ from their
written bytes). (4) `RpSplineFindPosition` mirrors negative parameters, wraps closed splines, eases the ends on path 11,
interpolates between neighbouring table entries; the curve passes through the user's control points. (5) The PDS
registry's 20-byte entries hold the id at +8 and the pipeline at +16; the engine's default atomic / sector / material
pipelines (pipe module +60 / +64 / +68) are its pipes 0x1002 / 0x1003 / 0x1001 in every snapshot.

**Types delta.** `tools/ours/types/deltas/render_rw7.json`: RpUserDataArray, RpMeshHeader, RpSpline, RpPTankData,
Rt2dFont and the seed record PdsRegistry (refined). `types_build.py` takes it: found / known RpUserDataArray 4 / 4,
RpMeshHeader 3 / 5, RpSpline 4 / 4, RpPTankData 23 / 23, Rt2dFont 8 / 9, PdsRegistry 3 / 3 (an instance in all six
snapshots); 0 conflicts.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_render_rw7.cpp`, 11 cases, 216,852 assertions on MSVC Release (251 s) and on clang-cl
Release (244 s); on clang-cl also the RW-touching files test_render_rw / rw2 / rw4 / rw5 / rw6 / ptank / game2 / core3 / world,
test_field4_dungeon, test_ui2, test_models, test_anim: 168 cases, 9,838,426 assertions, all green). Every pair compares the whole register file and cycles at every check point, all 32 MiB (dead
stack included), the scratchpad, the bus log, the stand-ins' call logs and heaps. RpRandom: the three snapshots' live
generators (invariants, then 160 draws each equal to the host model, the state after every draw), 12 seeds per
snapshot (0, 1, 0x9A319039, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x80000000, 12345 and random) giving the host's table and the next draws, the
open / close, RpRandomSeedMT's table (480 draws, 36 seeds). Registrations: the six attach functions re-run on a snapshot
with the live entries unlinked register entries with the live entries' sizes and callbacks (15 registry entries:
engine, material, atomic, world-sector, geometry). PDS: 102 registry ids through the three rights callbacks, the live
default pipelines, the registry set-up. RpMatFX: the live effect records, every getter / setter on built materials of
every flags value, the GS / ALPHA words against the 6 x 6 table, the constructors / copies / stream sizes. Streams
through memory streams: 24 random user data lists written, sized and read back equal, their destroy (RwFree calls),
arrays added and lists copied deep; 48 real bin-mesh headers of dorm / b_5800 geometries written, sized and read back
(153 meshes, serial numbers); morph keys written and read back (1 / duration, next pointers),
`RpMorphGeometryCreateInterpolators`. RpSpline: the live and fresh basis tables against the host's B-spline basis, the 7
end matrices equal to the live ones, 24 splines through their 169 control points, the tangent unit, path 11 at the ends,
`RpSplineSetControlPoint`. PTank: 48 allocations against the host's layout, the data size. Fonts / brushes: the high
map, the string width (within the R5900's round-towards-zero), the unicode flag, the brush create / colours / UVs /
texture. Then every body on the three snapshots with built records (5,064 pairs, 3,640 whole) and the random-world
sweep (64 pairs a function). Three planted mutations (RpRandom's output shift, one block's cycles in the atomic rights
callback, the matrix stride of the separate PTank layout) failed 3 of the 9 non-sweep cases (997 assertions).

## Phase 5 slice cri1: the CRI middleware's pure parts -- ADXB headers and ADPCM decoders, the SJ stream joints, SVM, cvFs name helpers (151 functions, 2026-10-23)

**What** (`game/src/cri/cri1_{adxb,sj,svm,cvfs}.cpp`, `game/include/p3fes/game/cri1.h`, `tests/game/test_cri1.cpp`,
`tools/ours/types/deltas/cri1.json`): the parts of the ADX / Sofdec libraries linked into the ELF that only compute or move
memory. Worked from the binary only (the p3fes_handgen bodies, the pseudocode reference, the ELF's data); the CRI SDK is
proprietary and was not opened, fetched or quoted; the ADX block format used by the tests is the public one. Names are
functions.json's (ADR-0009; most are `sub_*`); each function carries a role comment and a bracketed proposal (our own,
from the instructions; not imported). The bodies are the generated ones plus comments and named offsets (329 loads /
stores now name a field of `namespace cri1`: the ADX header, the decoder object, the SJMEM / SJRBF / SJUNI handles and
chunks), so every statement, charge and check point is the generator's.
- **ADXB** (41): the ADX header parsers -- `sub_539A38` (magic, >= 0x8000 bytes, "(c)CRI"), `sub_539AE0` (main header),
  `sub_539BE0` (cutoff), `sub_539C60` (version / flags), `sub_539CD8` (version-4 histories), `sub_539ED8` / `sub_539E10`
  (loop record), `sub_53A138` (AINF) --, the AHX header and sync search (`_get_peer_or_sock_name_3`, `sub_5399B8`), the WAV
  header parser and decoder set-up (`sub_538F18` / `sub_539148`: "fmt " / "data", 16 / 8 / 4-bit kinds), the SPSD / WAV
  tag tests, the prediction coefficients `sub_539858` (sqrtf / cosf), the two ADPCM block decoders -- `sub_53A410` mono and
  `sub_53AD00` stereo, both with the running key (scale XOR key, key = (key * mul + add) & 0x7FFF per block) --, and the 16
  decoder objects at 0x793B80 that run them (`sub_54CB78` .. `sub_54CF88`: create, coefficients, histories, key, entries,
  exec, exec server, state, stop).
- **SJ** (90): SJMEM (a memory block read front to back; 32 handles at 0x7AC7B8), SJRBF (the ring buffer; 256 handles at
  0x7ACCA0), SJUNI (four chunk lists over a node pool; 64 handles at 0x7B0CD8): pool init / finish, create / destroy /
  reset / uuid / error callback, get / put / unget / is-get chunk, counts, each with its locked wrapper; the chunk split
  `sub_563C28`; five stream-record accessors 0x562DE0..0x562E10.
- **SVM** (14): lock / unlock through the callbacks the ADX setup installs (0x99A0A0 / 0x99A0A8; types 1..5, the
  outermost lock's type checked on unlock) and the error-callback helpers (`sub_564AA8` formats with vsprintf).
- **cvFs** (6): `cvFsInit`, the upper-casing `sub_555D10`, `cvfs_getDevName` (the "DEV:file" split), `cvfs_getDefDev`,
  the error helpers `sub_555918` / `sub_5558E8`. The device registration and lookup (`cvFsAddDev`, `cvfs_addDevice`,
  `cvfs_getDevice`, `sub_555D70`, `sub_555F10`, `sub_555E48`, `cvfs_isNeedDevName`) call newlib `strncmp` 0x524670,
  which `test_models.cpp` stands in with a recorder: taken in the first build (pair-tested, audited faithful), then
  trimmed with `strncmp` when the merge check found the recorder (other slices' tests are not edited).

**Findings** (from the instructions, each checked by a test): (1) 0x784948 does not select an implementation of the
stereo decoder but a downmix: non-zero writes (L + R) * 7 / 10, clamped, to both outputs (histories stay per channel);
the retail snapshots hold 0. (2) Both decoders stop before a block whose scale has bit 15 set and then return early
without writing the histories back. (3) The scale is stored minus one: (word & 0x1FFF) + 1 (public descriptions agree).
(4) The decoder object's histories are stored {hist1 L, hist2 L, hist1 R, hist2 R} at +40, and the set / get accessors
take one array of the two hist1 and one of the two hist2. (5) The cvFs device table is 32 x 16 bytes (interface + 12-byte
name; `cvFsInit` clears only the names' first bytes): MFS, CDV, ROFS, VOL, BGM, BTL in every snapshot, default "VOL". (6) An SJRBF put on the data line mirrors the
chunk's part inside the first `extra` bytes into the extra area and the part that ran into the extra area back to the
start; an unget steps the position back only when the chunk was the last one got. In every live handle of the snapshots
free + data + (got0 - put1) + (got1 - put0) equals the buffer size. (7) The coefficients of the disc's 500 Hz / 24 kHz
files are 6687 / -2729 (within 1 of the double-precision formula for every rate tried). (8) The SVM mismatch text names
the unlock function as the binary's own string does.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_cri1.cpp`, 14 cases; no audio committed: the .adx files are read from `extracted/` at
run time): the generic sweep (159 x 24 random worlds); every one of the disc's 601 .adx headers through the parsers
against the public layout (571 version 4, 192 with a loop record); built AHX / AINF / WAV / short / wrong-magic headers
and the sync search against host rules; the coefficients against the formula; one file of each kind (mono v3 voices,
mono v4 battle, stereo 24 / 48 kHz, long headers) decoded through the decoder objects as the library drives them, PCM
compared sample for sample with a host decoder written from the public ADX format, chunk after chunk and at the end
block, also on the downmix path (1,850 frames); random blocks, the running key and odd stereo counts on the decoders
directly; SJRBF (720 operations), SJMEM and SJUNI (560) against host models (chunk sizes, positions modulo the size,
mirroring, unget, merge / split, node pools, conservation); the error paths, the locked wrappers and the SVM lock depth /
type through stand-ins (the lock / unlock / error callbacks as recorders, the real or stood-in vsprintf); the cvFs table
(init on junk-filled tables, upper-casing against the host, nine path splits, the default-device copy, the
error helpers through a recorder); the b_5800 and dorm_replay_4900 snapshots' live SJRBF / SJUNI handles, decoder objects (the last job run
again) and device table. All 151 functions are paired on meaningful inputs.
Counts (main ad99251 merged): MSVC 14.44 Release (gate tree) **14 cases, 113,442 assertions** (126 s); clang-cl 19.1.5
Release (`build\cri1-clang`) **14 cases, 113,442 assertions** (90 s). About 4,800 targeted pairs plus 3,624 on random
worlds (886 stop early, identically in both bodies). No callee was added to the shared `_callees` list. The error-callback
recorder sits at 0x55E978 (not emitted anywhere): the game's own callback 0x197F80 became hand-written with the boot
slice, and a hand-written function cannot be stood in.

**Audit** (`audit_faithful.py --only <the 159 first taken> --seeds 96 --snapshots dorm_replay_4900,b_5800,
climb_ref_17000 --snapshot-seeds 16 --jobs 3`): **faithful 159, differ 0, crash 0, hang 0** (314 s); the 151 kept are
those bodies.

**Types delta** (types_build.py, outputs to scratch): 2,577 known fields / 1,915 found / 11 conflicting (none in these

CvfsDeviceSlot 2 / 2 (in all six snapshots).

## Phase 5 slice scene: the 0x3B0000 band beyond the fonts -- the scene resource manager, mt_scene.c, mt_sceneFunc.c, comuTable.bin and the comu timer steps (109 functions, 2026-10-23)

**What.** `game/src/scene/scene_{res,func,comu,misc}.cpp` (`scene.h`): 109 p3fes_handgen bodies made readable -- a role
comment above every function (and in the header; 67 proposed names in brackets and in `symbols/deltas/scene.sym`), the
globals and record offsets as named constants (`scn::g / comu` for the globals, `scn::res / chr / npc / mdl / eff / fmdl /
blk / hit / pos / cam / snd / scene / path / seq / creq / icondel / task` for the records: 152 constants, each replacing
only the literal it equals, applied per function through a register -> record map by a script); a second script checks
that, comments dropped and constants replaced by their values, every body is token-identical to the generator's output
and the 109 shims unchanged (**109 functions, 0 differ**). What the band holds (K_Assert file strings, task names,
callers; 0x3AE000-0x3B4FC0 are the fonts of font2):
* resrcManager.c (0x3B4FC0-0x3B5620): the resource manager, 22 typed doubly linked lists (create, add with the per-type
  record size from the jump table 0x7BB250, find, count, list head, delete, destroy);
* mt_scene.c (0x3B5620-0x3B8210): the scene record's NPC-set / ENV setters (the loader steps 30 / 40), the field-model
  file test, MT_Scene_GetResListHead, the typed creators (positions 8, type 7, models 2, the character / NPC lights 4 / 5,
  field EPLs 11, Tartarus blocks 12, field hits 13 / 21, markers 14..19, cameras 20), MT_Scene_DeleteRes (per type: tasks,
  models, icon EPLs, blocks, matrices), the transform helpers (pos / rot / scale -> model or EPL), matrix <-> angles;
* mt_sceneFunc.c (0x3B8210-0x3BD280): the show / visible flags, the move / rotate / fade / motion requests the
  "SceneManager Task" executes, the icon EPLs over characters and objects (the "10ban" icon, the "IconEplDestroyDell" task),
  the cubic Bezier, the path point and lengths, the field-hit value under a point, the angle helpers, the SceneManager
  task creator, the icon files icon/ICON1..25.EPL;
* comuFunction.c / comuTimerSequence.c (0x3BD280-0x3C0000): comuTable.bin's loader and accessors, the link-state rules,
  the 56-byte event request, today's links, the dated calls 802 / 803, the comu timer-sequence steps (events 808..811 /
  861 through adminiChangeSeq);
* 0x3C0000's leftovers outside fcl's stood-in list: nmListAllocNode `sub_3C4650`, a facility panel slide `sub_3CA960`,
  the fclBank panel states `sub_3CFB50`; and one callee from the calendar band, `sub_172A50` (links 6..11), so three
  comuFunction.c functions could come along.

**Formats documented in the header (for the editor).** The resource record of every type (the common 256 bytes: id =
type << 10 | index, position, rotation in degrees, scale, flags, the move / rotate / fade request blocks, the list links;
then per type: characters 496 B, models 464, objects / NPCs 544, lights 432, effects 264, 7 272, positions 256, field
models 304, field EPLs 264, Tartarus blocks 368, field hits 336 -- centre, width, depth, turn about y and the derived quad,
the hit value --, markers 272, cameras 288); the scene record 0x95AFC0; the bezier path (u8 count, 3 count + 1 points,
segments sharing end points); comuTable.bin inside event/comuPack.pak (u16 version 1, u8 last section 143, 144 x {offset,
size}; the named tables with their record sizes); the comu timer-sequence step protocol (0 again, -1 done, else the next
step).

**Findings.** (1) MT_SceneFunc_PathPoint rescales the local parameter ((t mod 1/count) * count; IDA's pseudocode drops the
division) and gives the end point for t >= 1; at an exact segment boundary it evaluates the earlier segment's end. (2)
comuDateInRange `sub_3BF270` has two quirks, checked on every day of the year: a range inside one month accepts every day
from its start to the month's end (no end-day test), and a wrapping range starting and ending in the same month rejects
that month's days before the start. (3) The type-7 resource's +256 starts at 35.0 (0x420C0000), not 40. (4) The field hit
is a rectangle (width / depth / turn) whose quad sub_1E6AF0 derives; MT_Scene_ApplyTransform rotates models y-first
(replace), then x and z pre-concatenated. (5) On the live dorm machine the loader rebuilds the comu block byte for byte
from the H_Cdvd cache (the pak's members stay cached).

**Left recompiled.** Stood in with answers by other slices' tests (taking them would change those tests): MT_Scene_Load
0x3B5760, sub_3B5AB0 / sub_3B5A10 (test_battle_core2, test_events, test_shops), MT_Scene_GetRes sub_3B5D10 and the stage
getter sub_3B5D00 (test_events / test_events2 answer with a model), sub_3B5CF0 / sub_3B64C0 / sub_3BD8B0 / sub_3BD9A0 /
sub_3BE8E0 (test_script3's non-zero answers), sub_3B5DF0 / sub_3B55B0 (test_events3's custom stand-ins), sub_3B65D0
(test_field3_units), sub_3BD880 (test_calendar's custom stand-in), the frFontEx trio sub_3B2CB0 / sub_3B2F90 / sub_3B32D0
(font2's list); and what calls them (sub_3BBED0, most of mt_sceneFunc.c's resource-id wrappers through sub_3B5D10, the
big executor sub_3B9610 and the SceneManager task bodies), the fptodp users (sub_3B8540 / sub_3B88C0 / sub_3BBB90 /
sub_3BC220: fptodp is test_events' recorder), the qsort user sub_3BCEB0, sub_3B6030 / sub_3B6270 (sub_19BEB0, boot band),
sub_3BB7A0 / sub_3BCDA0 (sub_198590), sub_3BC940 / sub_3BCBF0 / sub_3BCC80 (callees in the EPL band 0x350000, script4's). In 0x3C0000 only three functions were free: the rest is fcl's (stood in by test_fcl /
test_nm_message / test_social_map) or calls sprites / message windows other tests stand in. Taken although other tests
list them as v0 = 0 recorders (they run for real there now; every affected test file was re-run on the slice tree and
passes: events, events2, events3, calendar, comm_b2, comm_c, field3_kosaka, field3_units, render_game2, script3,
battle_core2, shops, field_lo; and, after the last merge, test_boot_scene's v0 = 0 recorder of sub_3B5D50 -- the whole gate passes): the resource-manager core, the creators, MT_Scene_DeleteRes, the transform / request /
flag setters, the comu accessors. No function of the slice touches hardware registers, makes a syscall or reaches the
IOP: nothing was skipped for a skip reason; refused by the emitter: none.

**How chosen.** The band had 166 recompiled functions, the 0x3C0000 band 60. A leaf-first closure over the pseudocode
reference's callee facts (then re-checked on the generated bodies' `gen::` callees) against main's replaced.txt, the
stand-ins and the functions other tests stand in with answers gave 109; the reach probe of battle3 / fx2 was not needed
because every closed function was taken (the snapshots show the band live on every route: the dorm, battle and Tartarus
scenes hold 58 / 13 / 67 resources).
