## Phase 5 slice tail1: the ELF tail 0x570000-0x5AFFFF is CRI Sofdec -- survey, and 165 functions of it (2026-10-23)

**Survey: what the region is.** 1,517 functions (201,288 bytes) from 0x570030 to 0x5A1CE0; 0x5A2000 onwards is VU1
microcode (data). Every function is CRI's Sofdec movie middleware, identified by the version banners its modules return
(`\nCRI M2V/PS2EE Ver.1.958`, `MPS Ver.1.924`, `MPV Ver.1.958`, `MWSFD/PS2EE Ver.3.50`, `SFD Ver.1.958`, `SFH Ver.1.19`,
`SFX Ver.2.29`, `SUD Ver.0.05`, all built Mar 1 2005) and by its own error strings (`mwPlyCreate`, `mwPlyGetTime`,
`MWSFSFX_SetOutBufSize`, `MWSFSVR_VsyncThrdProc` ...). The libc / SDK names the region carries are **FLIRT false matches**
of tiny code shapes, not those libraries: `sceLibgcc32GetErxEntries_16..23` and `__gthread_get_ee_key_value / _use` are
the modules' 12-byte "return the banner / work address" getters, `__env_lock_N` / `__env_unlock_N` / `nullsub_177` are
empty hooks, `atan2l_N` / `cosl_N` / `coshl_N` / `expl_N` / `powl_11` ... are 20-byte tail-call stubs, `__errno_N`,
`WTLS_get/set_table_N`, `sceInsockSet/GetErrnoMode_N` are 12-byte getters / setters, `sceInsockSetSendTimeout_0` is
`mwPlyGetTime` by its own string, `my_malloc_N`, `r_lock_def_*`, `R_LOCK_DEF_*`, the STL `tie__` / `rdbuf__` names are
the same kind of shapes (80 such names in all). **There is no network stack (insock), no ERX relocatable-module loader and
no second libc / libm here.** Modules by banner (boundaries approximate: a banner sits at the start of its module's main
object, helpers can sit before it):

| module (banner / evidence) | range | functions | bytes | reached on the routes | pure closure | taken |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| M2V, the MPEG video decoder on the IPU (continues from the cri1 band) | 0x570000-0x577A28 | 60 | 30,436 | 28 | 56 | 2 |
| MPS, the program-stream demultiplexer | 0x577A28-0x578D98 | 25 | 4,928 | 15 | 23 | 16 |
| MPV, the MPEG video layer (error codes 0xFF03xxxx) | 0x578D98-0x57C4E8 | 94 | 13,956 | 54 | 64 | 18 |
| MWSFD, the movie player (mwPly*, the MWSFSVR threads) | 0x57C4E8-0x586300 | 416 | 40,016 | 146 | 189 | 14 |
| SFD, the stream core, with its stream objects (vtables 0x7C9D78.., "SJ" in MWSFD's errors) | 0x586300-0x59CFA0 | 743 | 93,052 | 426 | 523 | 39 |
| SFH, the stream-header parser | 0x59CFA0-0x59E7A8 | 60 | 6,012 | 50 | 60 | 60 |
| SFX, frame conversion / composition (Z, alpha) | 0x59E7A8-0x5A1158 | 98 | 10,292 | 21 | 81 | 6 |
| SUD, utilities (the "<SUDPS_>" tag, the time base, the timer) | 0x5A1158-0x5A1D00 | 21 | 2,596 | 10 | 14 | 10 |
| total | | 1,517 | 201,288 | 750 | 1,010 | 165 |

**Reachability.** Static: game code enters the region at eight places -- `kwlnInitMain` 0x198010 and `sub_108740` (the
movie module's init) call `sub_57F768` [mwPlyInitSfdFx-like init: "iprm is NULL", "can't init GSC"]; `H_Cdvd_StartSfd`
0x1023F0 starts a movie (`sub_580378` / `sub_584290`, "fname is NULL"); `sub_10A860` / `sub_10BB00` (the game's movie
player task) call the mwPly create / destroy / get-frame / header-info entries; `kwlnRootUpdateShowRasterTask` calls
`sub_5810F0` (a two-instruction wrapper into the CRI band); the cri1 band's `sub_56F888..sub_56FE40` call M2V and MPV;
110 functions are reached only through function-pointer tables (SJ / SFD vtables at 0x7C9D78-0x7CA544) and 65 through
`lui/addiu` addresses (callbacks such as `sub_57F3E0`, the header getters SFD calls through `sub_58BB10`); 288 have no
caller and no reference at all (dead library code). The static closure from those roots holds 1,028 functions.
Dynamic (measured as battle3 / battle4 did: a temporary first-call probe in every generated function of
0x570000-0x5B0000 -- scratch `instrument.py`, never committed; the next gate build re-emitted `recomp/generated` -- in a
copied instrumented `p3fes.exe`, `--vu1 aot --gs-backend d3d11 --gs-exact`): **750 of the 1,517 run on the dorm,
battle, climb (to vblank 39,820), fusion and shop routes alike** (749 on fusion / shop, the same set otherwise): the boot
plays a Sofdec movie on every route, so the replay gates run this middleware. The m1 route (to sky:11, boot only) reaches
113 (the init path).

**Duplicates.** Byte-identical (raw) bodies elsewhere in the ELF: 116 functions, 92 of them with an already-replaced
original -- almost all 8-byte shapes (`jr $ra` + `nop` = nullsub_1 0x1007F0 and ~90 more replaced empty functions;
`return 0` = sub_48A190; `return a0` = sub_489950; `return 1` = sub_48ABF0; `return *(a0 + 4)` = sub_4C2120). Larger
twins are inside CRI: sub_578ED8 = sub_577C30 = sub_56F9C8 (the error-record call), sub_5810F0 = sub_541040, sub_585658 =
sub_5617F0, sub_5A1778 = sub_55E208, sub_57F5F8 = sub_5335A0. The "numbered copies" of the libc slice's notes are the
same wrappers repeated per module, not copies of libc (their 20-byte shape only masks equal to `acos` / `log10` /
`pow`'s, with different targets).

**What.** 165 functions (14,844 bytes; 124 of them on the measured routes), game/src/lib/tail1_{mps,mwsfd,sfd,sfh,sud}.cpp,
game/include/p3fes/game/tail1.h, tests/game/test_tail1.cpp, tools/ours/types/deltas/tail1.json. Chosen as whole
families whose callees are all replaced or in the slice (libc leaves on main: memset, memcmp, strstr, strncpy, atoi,
__divdi3), reached first:
- SFH, the Sofdec stream-header parser, whole (60): the 32-view pool (init / finish / take / release), the parse
  ("SofdecStream" padded to 24 bytes at +32 of a header sector of >= 2,048 bytes; state 2 / -1), the version (the larger
  of the header's bytes +56 / +57 and the "Ver.x.yy" of the creator text +96), the readability gate (version 1.07 or
  >= 1.10), the 8.3 file name / date / text fields, the general (+128) and system (+176) blocks with their version
  gates (>= 1.10, >= 2.25), the 26-entry stream table (+384, 64 bytes each), the audio and video entry getters (the
  picture size packed as MPEG's sequence header packs it, the frame rate through the ISO/IEC 13818-2 frame_rate_code
  table, the flags), the stream-id classes of ISO/IEC 13818-1, the SFX handle pool beside it;
- SFD (39): the header-info builder `sub_58B5C8` with its helpers (the record at handle +120: version, first stream id
  per class, the audio and video blocks), the header-sector test, the error record (raise with "first error sticks",
  set / get callback, the handle check), the parameter tables (handle +2572 / +2972, the global defaults 0x7B4570, the
  filter on parameters 5 / 6 and stream records 2 / 3, all eight open handles);
- MWSFD (14): the header-sector callback `sub_57F3E0` and the player's 8-entry header ring (+180..+351), its reset and
  readers, `mwPlyGetHdrInf`'s header probe, the callback installation (SFD parameters 75 / 76);
- MPS / MPV (36): the MPS handle pool (find free, destroy, finish), both modules' error records and handle checks, the
  MPEG start-code classifier and the forward / backward scanners, the MPEG-1 / MPEG-2 decision (`sub_579770`), the
  picture-level search, the sequence-header figures (vbv size in bytes, bit_rate_value with the 0x3FFFF marker);
- SUD (10): the "<SUDPS_>" tag finder, its two-digit number and character fields, the 64-bit time base;
- the FLIRT-misnamed getters / hooks among them (`sceLibgcc32GetErxEntries_17 / 20 / 21 / 23`, `__gthread_get_ee_key_*`,
  `__env_unlock_3 / _4`) and 9 byte-identical duplicates: five empty hooks (= nullsub_1 0x1007F0, replaced by font2),
  sub_579078 (`return -1` = the close / ioctl / lseek stubs 0x503848..), sub_577C30 and sub_578ED8 (= sub_56F9C8, the
  error-record call), sub_57F5F8 (= sub_5335A0).

**How.** p3fes_handgen bodies (165 generated, 3 refused for mid-body entries: sub_577BB8, sub_578D60, sub_58B398), split
by module into five files; a scripted readability pass (a role per function with a proposed name in brackets, written
from the instructions and the pseudocode reference; 127 named constants in `tail1::` -- err / mps / sc / mpv / sfd /
sfdinfo / sfh / sid / mwsfd / sud -- used 164 times in place of the numbers they equal; state comments in the
forward start-code scanner); a normaliser (comments stripped, every `tail1::` name swapped for its value, hex and
decimal compared by value) proves **all 165 bodies token-equal to the generated ones**. Types: `deltas/tail1.json` adds
SfhView 4 / 4 found, SfdHeaderInfo 13 / 10, SfdHandle 10 / 6, CriErrRec 3 / 3, MpsHandle 4 / 2, MpvHandle 8 / 7,
MwsfdPlayerHdrRing 6 / 4; whole program 2,609 known / 1,936 found / 11 conflicts -> 2,657 / 1,972 / 11 (no new conflict).

**Findings** (each checked by the tests). (1) The disc's 41 movies (extracted/DATA/SFD) all carry their Sofdec header in
sector 2 (offset 4,096), format 2.26, written by "Sofdec CRAFT/GUI Ver.1.74"; the header's +64 / +76 texts are the
movie's 8.3 file name and its date "yyyymmddhhmm"; each stream entry starts with its elementary stream's file name
(".SFV" / ".M2V" video, ".SFA" audio, "<SFM_P2>.TMP" for 0xBF); audio is 2 channels at 48,000 Hz (entry +27 / +28),
video 640 x 448 or 640 x 368 at frame_rate_code 4 (29.97). (2) 38 movies are MPEG-1 video (user data follows the
sequence header) and 3 MPEG-2 (P3CTOP, P3FCT003, STAFF_ROLL_F: a sequence_extension follows, and their video entry is
named ".m2v"); the stream entry's byte +32, which the audio / video getters require to be 1, is 1 for both kinds (not an
MPEG-2 marker). (3) `sub_5A12F8` [sudTagNumber] copies the two digits to the stack without a terminator: atoi reads on
into whatever the stack holds after them. (4) SFH's init counts only when the count is <= 0 (a second init is a no-op;
a finish below 0 is undone by the next init). (5) SFD's error record keeps the first error code (later raises still call
the callback); MPS / MPV overwrite it. (6) `sub_5A1CE0` returns 0x7B0000 in $v0 (the lui of the store address).

**Kept recompiled, with the reason.** In the chosen families: the mid-body entries above and what needs them
(sub_577AB0 / sub_577A38 [MPS init], sub_577E68 / sub_577DD8 [MPS create] via loc_577BD0, sub_58B2D0 / sub_58B168
[header sector intake], sub_58B4A8 via loc_58B3D8); the SUD timer readers sub_5A1868 / sub_5A19C0 / sub_5A1A30 (they
read and program the EE timer through the pointers 0x7CAC20 / 0x7CAC30: hardware registers); the strncmp callers
sub_5A1340 / sub_5A1380 / sub_5A13C0 / sub_5A1420 / sub_5A14B0 (strncmp is stood in by test_models, not replaced) and the
sprintf caller sub_5A1188 (left with its tag writer); sub_579080 / sub_579450 (the MPV header decoders and stream
readers they call are not taken), sub_578F10 / sub_5796D0 (they call sub_561970 in the CRI band), sub_57F600 /
sub_57F670 / sub_57F6F8 / sub_57F750 (MWSFD's handle check sub_581798 and error path sub_585590 reach the CRI band),
SFD's init / finish sub_58BC30 / sub_58BC98 / sub_58BD68; not pulled in: sub_599408 / sub_599368 (reached, pure; no
selected caller), sub_578268 / sub_578378 / sub_578820 / sub_5A1518 (unreached, large). Outside the families, the
region's IPU / DMA / semaphore / thread paths (M2V, the MWSFSVR server threads), everything reaching the CRI band
0x531998- (cri1's area) and the SFX frame converters remain for a later pass: 1,010 functions form a pure closure in
the region (no syscall / COP0 / hardware in their own bodies, every callee replaced or in the set), 498 of them reached.

**Tests** (tests/game/test_tail1.cpp, 7 cases): the generic sweep (32 random worlds per function, 5,280 pairs, 1,860
stopped identically); SFH on the 41 movie headers -- every getter against the header bytes, the picture size and frame
rate against MPEG's packing and table, the stream table, the texts, the version gates on edited copies, the view states,
short / foreign headers, the decimal reader, the frame-rate table and all 256 stream ids (2,564 pairs); the SFH pool and
SFD's header-info record from every header, the first-stream finder, the handle readers (610 pairs); the start-code
classifier on every code 0xF0..0x20F against ISO/IEC 13818-2 table 6-1, the forward scanner on random buffers against a
host model of its state machine, the backward scanner's hits checked, and every movie's MPEG kind against its
".m2v" / ".sfv" name and the swapped lookalike (630 pairs); the error records with a real callback (sub_59D1B0 clears
its argument), the MPS / MPV / SFD handle pools and checks, SFD's parameter tables and filter, the two error-record
twins (55 pairs); MWSFD's header ring fed with ten sectors (31 pairs); SUD's time base (64-bit division), tag finder

SpriteSheet 2 / 1.

**Findings.** (1) The formation pick counts an enemy as small / medium / large by scale * radius (+144) and scale *
height (+140) -- and some size pairs count as nothing (a radius over 200 with a height over 125): such an enemy fits
every formation. (2) The skill power-up / change of the result screen draws from the libc `rand` (sub_488F30), not
from the battle's datCalcRand stream. (3) A party member's voice line for a situation (sub_2E1500) swaps the rows of
situations 5 / 6 and rotates 7 / 8 / 9 (+6, +5, +9, +7, +8 from the member's base). (4) btlBossReactMotion: on
encounter 424 the boss 269's reaction to skill 308 turns from motion 7 to 21 once gBtl +2900 is set; the enemies
149..156 (outside the boss encounters) react with motion 4 / 7 / 23 / 24 by the column of their 8-byte row in
*0x7CE4A4 and 7 for any other skill. (5) The battle music kinds of gEncountTbl +22: 2..6 -> tracks 27..31, 7 / 8 ->
113 / 114, anything else 2 (106 when sub_17D800 says so).

## Phase 5 slice cri2: the CRI middleware, second pass -- ADXT, ADXSJD, the cvFs request layer, libmpeg's pure parts (186 functions, 2026-10-23)

**What** (`game/src/cri/cri2_{adxt,adxsjd,cvfs,mpeg}.cpp`, `game/include/p3fes/game/cri2.h`, `tests/game/test_cri2.cpp`,
`tools/ours/types/deltas/cri2.json`), under the relaxed callee rule (a body may call still-recompiled functions through
their `gen::` entry points; only a function whose own body touches hardware, makes a syscall, talks to the IOP or calls
ADXF / ROFS / sceCd directly stays recompiled). Built on cri1's records and bodies (main `f4c5ef3`; the branch was
first developed on a cherry-pick of it, then rebased onto main 1c8182c). Worked from the binary and public format descriptions only (ADX; ISO/IEC 13818-2 video
syntax; the MPEG program stream); no CRI or Sony SDK material was opened, fetched or quoted. Names are functions.json's
(ADR-0009); each function carries a role comment and a bracketed proposal (our own, from the instructions and the
binary's own error texts such as "cvFsDelDev #1:illegal device name"; not imported).
- **ADXT** (66, 0x547BC0-0x54CA08 + the SVM lock wrappers 0x539818 / 0x539830): the player handle (16 x 200 bytes at
  0x787570, `cri2::adxt`): create (`sub_547C18`: the work area laid out as two 16,576-byte PCM buffers at the 64-byte
  aligned start, the input ring in whole sectors after them, a 36-byte extra area and the name buffer; the ring joint,
  the streamer, the output joints, the decoder, the output and the list streamer), destroy (`sub_548078`), the starts
  (`sub_54B230` named file range, `sub_54B0D8` file N of a partition through ADXF's lookup, `sub_54B520` entry N of a
  memory index (big-endian count and offsets) over an SJMEM joint, `sub_548520` a caller's joint), stop
  (`sub_5486A8` / `sub_5485D8`), **the state machine** (`sub_54CA08`: 1 opening `sub_54BCD8`, 2 buffering `sub_54C100`,
  3 playing `sub_54C288`, 4 decode end `sub_54C370`, 5 play end `sub_54C578`, then the end-of-input check `sub_54C940`
  and the error check `sub_54C8C0`; 6 = error), the server `sub_549EC8`, the loop / end-of-stream traps, and the
  accessors (status, time, samples, rate, volume, pan, loop flag, pause, server frequency, error code, PCM waiting).
- **ADXSJD** (38, 0x541D48-0x5433A8): the sound-joint decoder handle (16 x 168 bytes at 0x78FF98, `cri2::adxsjd`): pool,
  create / destroy, start / stop, the header stage `sub_542130` (skips zero padding, hands the header to ADXB, keeps the
  header length), the decode stage (`sub_542558` input side: the trap, an AHX resync, the decode end at the total;
  `sub_5428C0` output side: the consumed input put back, the PCM chunks forward, the PCM filter callback; the output-info
  callback `sub_542438` ADXB calls), and the 22 accessors and setters the player uses.
- **cvFs** (51, 0x555B10-0x557A28): device registration (`cvFsAddDev` / `cvfs_addDevice`, the upper-cased name in the
  first free of the 32 slots), removal, lookup (`cvfs_getDevice`), the default device, the resolve step
  (`cvfs_variousProc`: the named device or the default one, "DEV:" prefixed for a device that asks for it), the 40 file
  handles, every request through the device's 26-entry interface table (`cri2::cvfs::kIf*`): open / close / seek / tell /
  read / write / stop / status / sector length / transfer count / byte rate, the name requests (file size two ways,
  change / make / remove directory, delete, exists, number of files, directory info, free size) and the option requests
  (OptFn1 codes 1-6 for volumes, 100 "needs its name", 200-205 the 64-bit pairs, 299, 300). These are the functions
  cri1 trimmed with strncmp (test_models stands strncmp in): under the relaxed rule only strncmp itself stays
  recompiled, and test_cri2 stands it in with its real semantics.

**Readability** (reproducible: scratch `ready.py` + `spec.py` rewrite the generator's output): a role comment with the
proposal per function (the same text in `cri2.h`), a file comment per unit (`cri2_adxt.cpp` documents the state machine),
and **482 named offsets** where one register holds one record for the whole body (checked by the script: one
assignment, or an untouched `$a0` in a leaf) or an explicit access list (the cvFs interface entries); each constant
equals the literal it replaces, so every statement, charge and check point is the generator's; the dispatcher
`sub_54CA08`'s branches are labelled with their states. A check script (scratch `check_same.py`) confirms that the four
files, comments dropped and the named offsets replaced by their values, equal the generator's output: 11,986 lines,
0 differ.

**Findings** (each checked by a test, on both bodies):
1. `sub_557908` (the 64-bit free size) looks the device up in the caller's stack buffer **before** `cvfs_getDevName`
   fills it: it uses whatever the frame held (a stale name); kept as is.
2. The cvFs name requests report "#3:device not found" and then still read the interface entry from a null pointer
   (addresses 8, 0x3C, 0x50 ... -- kernel RAM on the PS2); `sub_556BE8` (exists) has no null-name check at all.
3. `cvfs_getDevice` compares with the length of the name asked for: a prefix finds a device ("T" -> "TST"), and
   `sub_5568C0` (free size) calls every matching device, not the first.
4. `sub_54B520` (start a memory index entry) stops the player before it checks the entry: an entry past the count
   stops whatever played and releases a memory source's joint, then starts nothing.
5. The header stage takes the header only after an even number of zero bytes; an odd count is "E04102501 The data
   alignment is illegal." and decoder state 4. A chunk below 16 bytes or a non-header leaves state 1 and the data in
   place.
6. The ADXT server runs the output server twice per call while the current server frequency is below 51 (29 / 30 in
   every snapshot); the state machine never goes back (3 -> 4 -> 5) and state 5 does nothing.
7. The ADXT opening state sets the samples per call to 3 x rate / server frequency (halved without a loop), rounded up
   to a multiple of two blocks; the buffering state starts the output once min(2 x that, 0x4000) samples are queued.

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_cri2.cpp`, 17 cases; no media committed -- .adx and .sfd files are read from
`extracted/` at run time): the generic sweep (186 x 24 random worlds); cvFs through a test device (registration, the
prefix rule, removal, the default device, 12 handle requests with their error paths, 7 name requests with the missing
entry, the volume / option requests with their request blocks and codes, the 64-bit pairs, the server, close) and the

joints out: the playing players reach the play end), a whole player life on a fresh machine around a real .adx file
(create, the four starts, the header from a memory index, the accessors, the traps, stop, destroy; every lock wrapper
against its body: same memory, same calls); MPEG: GOP / picture headers on 7 of the disc's .sfd video streams (a

**Findings.** (1) `H_Cdvd_RtFsPak_FOpen` refuses the name pointer 1 (a sentinel), not a mode. (2) The pak device's seek
returns its 64-bit position through a 128-bit result ($a0) built in a stack quadword; whence 2 adds min(offset, size)
to the position (it never clamps the sum), whence 3 gives size - 1 when size + offset does not wrap. (3) The CRI thunks
0x54D000-0x54D400 that the sound helpers call are ADXT entry points (FLIRT named some atan2l_4 / cosl_4 / setenv /
pvalloc). (4) comuFunction.c's accept takes the cost from the money before it knows whether the entry was already
accepted, but stores the money only for a new entry.

blocks, the record offsets named (`rw8::` beside `rw4::`..`rw7::`: rxpipeline / rxpnode / rxdef / rxclref / rxoutspec,
pipemodule, rxheap / heapblock, pdsentry / pdsmatdef / pdsobjdef, ptankpipes) and the RW globals labelled; the scratch
tool only adds comments and replaces literal load / store offsets by those names for the base registers a per-function
spec names, and checks that the code token stream with the names resolved equals the generated body's (157,309 tokens,
equal). Groups:
* **The RxPipeline core** (48, 0x4F22B0-0x4F72F0): RxPipelineCreate (`sub_4F2F70`, the 52-byte pipeline free list),
  RxPipelineLock (`sub_4F4640`), RxLockedPipeAddFragment (`sub_4F4950`, a NULL-terminated list of definitions from $a2,
  output 0 of each node to the next), RxLockedPipeAddPath (`sub_4F4C30`), RxPipelineFindNodeByName (`sub_4F4830`),
  RxLockedPipeUnlock (`sub_4F3F80`) and its passes -- the node record set-up, the super block's sizing / relocation /
  copy, the distinct-cluster count, the topological sort (in-degrees, then a depth-first placement that swaps nodes into
  order and renumbers every output), the cluster requirement / propagation / slot passes and their record sort (radix +
  insertion), a top-down scratch allocator --; the pipeline and Im3D modules' open / close, the default render-state
  vector, the RxHeap (create, alloc with split and grow -- 'Heap resized from %d to %d bytes' --, free with merging,
  destroy), a packet's cluster release, RwIm3DRenderLine (`sub_4F22B0`).
* **The pipe constructors** (24): the PDS registry's engine open (every registered pipe built), RpPDSRegisterPipe /
  PDSRegistryAddPipe, RpPDSSkyMatPipeCreate (material definitions), `sub_46AFA0` / `sub_46A8D0` (object definitions and
  their material pipe); PTank's engine open / close and its six pipes (`rpSpr2dGenCreatePS2AllMatPipe`,
  `rpSpr3dGenCreatePS2AllMatPipe` with their object pipes, the tank pipe, the instancing pipe); the world module's open /
  close with the default pipelines, the Im3D pipes (`sub_49C810` FastIm3DTransform, the render pipes taken from the
  registry); the PS2AllMat node's initialisation (`PS2AllMatPipelineNodeInit`, the cluster layout `sub_4A30D0`).
* **World leftovers** (6): RpUserData's registrations on nine object types (`sub_48F030`), plugin 0x11D's registration and
  stream write, the atomic / plane sector stream readers (`sub_48F580`, `sub_48FBD0`), a float compare.
* **Rt2d** (28): the font lookup by name, text objects (string, font, stream read), object init / colour multiplier, the
  object-list walks; the path fill's triangulation (ear clipping); Rt2dAnim's keyframe lists (reset, step, go to, set
  time, apply, stream read) and the maestro (scene object, update, buttons, message handler).
* **Image files** (9): the BMP reader / writer (headers, palette, rows by depth), the Sun raster writer's open.
* **The mipmap K / L pass** (7): per texture of the current dictionary, the texel density over a world's sectors, the
  raster's K value (`RpSkyTextureSetMipmapK`).
* **RtQuat** (8): RtQuatConvertFromMatrix (three major-axis cases), RtQuatRotate, RtQuatTransformVectors,
  RtQuatSetupSlerpCache.
* **The palette quantiser** (20, 0x4D1900-0x4D41E0): a 16-way colour tree (one bit of each channel per level, a 92-byte
  node free list), the pixel statistics with luminance weights, the box sums / best split / assignment, the palette and
  index conversion, an image's alpha class (opaque / cut-out / translucent).

**The pipeline rules** (render_rw8.h; all checked on the snapshots). (1) A lock / unlock round trip of every live
pipeline (dorm, b_5800, climb: the PDS registry's 33, PTank's six, the Im3D transform -- 40 each, all one-node) keeps
every node, output, initialisation data, input-slot map, the cluster-slot count and the entry point; the unlock runs
each node's initialisation again, so the private data returns to the definition's defaults (PS2AllMat: no callbacks,
VIF offset 0x114, the VU1 code array 0x77F130 x 32; PS2All: no callback, no material pipe) -- every constructor sets its
callbacks after its unlock. The lock marks the pipeline locked and clears each node's slot-cluster word; a second lock is
a no-op; unlocking an unlocked or null pipeline fails and changes nothing. (2) The constructors rebuild the live
pipelines node for node, private data included (the PS2All node's +36 points into the pipeline's own super block); the
registry stores the entry id as plugin data (RpPDSSkyMatPipeCreate leaves the definition's +4, which differs for
0x1001..0x1003 and 0x11001 / 0x11002). (3) The unlock sorts the nodes topologically (each output to a later node), makes
node 0 the entry point, gives each distinct cluster one slot and counts each definition's use (+60). (4) RxLockedPipeAddPath
refuses an unlocked pipeline, a connected output and a pointer that is not a node of the pipeline; the fragment refuses
more nodes than the module's limit (64).

**Not taken / skipped.** The prompt's known stand-in conflicts and every RW-band address another slice's test names (122
excluded, none of them taken), the anim ranges (0x464760-0x466F00, 0x489020-0x48AC10, 0x4B65A0-0x4B97F0, 0x4F7300-0x4F8E10),
the running slices' and script4's rows (none in this list), the `_rwDMA*` / VIF / GS functions and the PTank streamers
(hardware registers in their own bodies: `sub_473FB0`, `sub_474820`, `sub_474D30`, `sub_476140 ..`, `sub_47A510`,
`sub_47A710`, `sub_47C240 ..`), the sky driver's start-up (`RwEngineStart`, `RwEngineOpen`, `sub_4CA850`, `SkyUseMode`,
`skyCustomModeIsOk`, the frame / depth buffer rasters: the device start-up, outside this pass) and the functions named after
libmpeg (`_dispRefImage*`, `_getRef0`, `_dualPrimeVector`, `_rix_*` / `_ri0_*`: not RenderWare). Left for a later pass for size: the raster / texture conversion band 0x4CC5C0-0x4D0AC0 (the callers of the
quantiser), `sub_4734D0` / `sub_474260` / `sub_474F20` (PTank instancing beside the streamers), the remaining
functions of 0x49A290-0x49F040. None of the 150 touches hardware registers, makes a syscall or talks to the IOP in its own body.

**Types delta.** `tools/ours/types/deltas/render_rw8.json`: RxPipeline, RxPipelineNode, RxNodeDefinition, RxHeap,
PdsRegistryEntry, PdsObjPipeDef (the material definition is the seed record RpPDSMatPipeDef already). `types_build.py`

## Phase 5 slice unblock: recorder checks in merged pair tests rewritten as guest-memory checks, 104 freed functions replaced (2026-10-23)

**Why.** Many merged pair tests stand a callee in with a recorder (a stand-in that logs the call and returns a fixed
value). A replaced (hand-written) callee cannot be stood in: it always runs, so a check on the recorder's log reads 0,
and a check that relied on the recorder's canned result or on a missing-function stop changes. The user approved
(2026-10-23) rewriting such checks as checks of the callee's effect in guest memory, under safeguards: every test keeps
its case count and gets no weaker, the edited tests pass on main first on both compilers, one mutation per edited test.
Pattern: 51b80f2 (test_field3_camera).

**How the set was found (measured, not guessed).** Every function start named by a test file (main's and the then
unmerged script4 / render_rw7 / cri1 tests), not replaced, not claimed by a running slice (their worktrees' rows and new
sources; their bands excluded: band20 0x200000-0x23FFFF, field7 0x1A0000-0x1AFFFF, scene 0x3B5000-0x3BFFFF, the CRI tail
0x531000-), not a stand-in hook / heap / printf / H_Cdvd / kernel / IOP / sound-driver entry, without a hardware access
or syscall in its own body: 414 candidates. All 414 were generated with p3fes_handgen and replaced in a scratch build and
the whole suite run: 31 test files failed. Each failure was traced to its callee (a recorder count, a canned result, a
stop at a not-emitted callee used as the observation, an address the test uses as a "function that is not emitted", a
callee chain into CRI / RW / the texture builder). Then, on main 1c8182c and again on d86c959: (1) only functions of at
most 800 bytes (so every one gets its comments); (2) a callee closure -- a function stays only if every direct callee runs
in the test build (replaced in main, in the set, emitted, or served by the standard stand-ins), otherwise a test that used
to record it would now stop deeper and lose coverage (this removed 54, e.g. the shop step adders that call the
not-emitted sub_3E0C20, the itfMesMng wrappers, sub_3C7E20 -> sub_3C7E50); (3) every test file that names a function of
the set run on main and on the slice build and their messages diffed -- a function that made any real-data run stop
earlier was dropped (the Rt2d / maestro group of test_render_game2's MAESTRO test, the RW helpers test_render_rw4 / rw5
stand in on their snapshots, the callees battle_core2 / battle3 / battle5 record). 104 remain.

**Test files edited (7)** -- `cases / assertions`, MSVC Release and clang-cl Release (equal on both): "before" = main with
the original file; "after (main)" = main with the edited file and the four converted callees (0x104D10, 0x1158B0,
0x434F70, 0x52EDA0) emitted as recompiled bodies, no new replacement (the validation build); "after (final)" = the
slice's build:

random start ages below the life +76; a life of 0 emits nothing. (4) The developer text screen of kind 9's draw is
written whenever the word 0x7CCA3C is 0. (5) Kind 5 drives the battle's colour scale gBtl +548 (sub_29EA50) into
K_SceneDraw_SetColorScale; kind 12 is h_fade.c's screen fade inside the effect system. (6) The compendium animator's
coming-in templates stagger elements by 5-frame steps; going out every element starts at once.

4 / 4, BtlVoiceBankPktData 2 / 2.

**Findings.** (1) FRBAD (condition 12) counts dead units only when its parameter itself asks for the dead status
0x80000. (2) ENBAD_ALL (14) is true when no living enemy lacks the status -- also with no enemy at all. (3) The
weighted target pick ranks candidates by missing HP percent + an ailment bonus (64 / 32 / 2: +20, 16 / 4: +30, 8:
+50) and draws by rank weights (0x696FB0), so the most hurt / most afflicted unit is likeliest, not certain. (4) The
party voice line packet waits for the voice bank (gBtl +2806 bit 0); without it every voice line packet ends at
once. (5) A unit's cell position: x = 25 * cell x - 1750, z = 25 * cell z - 1750 + 200 + radius * scale.

## Phase 5 slice libs2: the library band 0x530000-0x56FFFF -- census, and CRI ACSS, the sound layer the BGM manager drives (188 functions, 2026-10-25)

**What** (`game/src/cri/libs2_acss_{fader,backend,sound,server,api}.cpp`, `game/include/p3fes/game/libs2.h`,
`tests/game/test_libs2.cpp`, `tools/ours/types/deltas/libs2.json`), under the relaxed callee rule. ACSS is the layer the
game's BGM manager (0x108740 init, 0x109180 / 0x108BC0 / 0x1099D0 / 0x10A100 the per-scene calls) and H_Cdvd_StartADXTFile
drive: sound objects with one or two players, volume fades with callbacks, cross-fades, AIX track volumes and a server-wide
ducking object that lowers the music while a voice plays. The binary's own error texts name its parts ("E2003052903
ACSSND_SetOutVol : Not initialized.", "ACSFDR_Create", "ACSVHL_Init", "ACSSVR_CreatSnd", "ACSSBADX_CreateHndl", ...): those
names are the bracketed proposals where a function carries one (35 functions), our own elsewhere (ADR-0009; not imported).
Worked from the binary only; no CRI SDK material.
- **Fader ACSFDR** (24 with ACSS's SVM lock thunks and the error reporter, 0x531998-0x532118): a volume in dB x 10 (0 full,
  -960 silent) driven per frame through a level 0..3238200 (curve 0: 3238200 x 10^(vol / 200); curve 1 the logarithmic
  alternative), delay / fade / hold, a start and an end callback.
- **Back ends** (38, 0x532118-0x532788): ACSSBADX over an ADXT player and ACSSBAIX over an AIXP handle, each a 16-entry
  method table in the ELF (0x7C0520 / 0x7C0630: create, destroy, the four starts, stop, pause, pause state, status,
  volume, track volume, loop flag, handle).
- **Sound ACSSND** (53, 0x532788-0x5349F8, 208 bytes): init from a 40-byte configuration and a work area (one player, or
  two for cross-fades; per player a back end with its input / PCM buffers and a fader; the AHX buffers, the name buffer,
  the AIX track volumes), the four start requests (stored, then sent through the method table), stop / pause / volume
  with fades, cancel-fading, the per-frame update and the fade bookkeeping (each player's next action when its fader
  goes idle), the accessors.
- **Server ACSSVR and ducking ACSVHL** (29, 0x5349F8-0x535688): the server (176 bytes at the address 0x793F44 holds; 16
  sound slots; counted init / finish; the SVM server entry 'adxcs_exec_svr'), the per-frame server, and the ducking
  object (96 bytes: enable, state, lowering / restoring frames, depth, its own fader).
- **Public entry points** (44, 0x54D030-0x54D528): thunks into the above (FLIRT leftovers such as setenv / valloc /
  cosl_4 are not what they are); the create / destroy / ducking ones read the server pointer 0x793F44.

(* driver layers: the own body is plain C but the band is the device / thread / IOP layer -- ADXF and ADXSTM read through
cvFs, SRD / dvCi through sceCd, DTX / PS2RNA / SJX through SIF RPC, ADXM creates and wakes threads, ROFS reads sectors
through dcf / sceCd; only own-body hardware, syscalls and direct ADXF / ROFS / sceCd / SIF calls were counted in the
"directly" column. Hardware in the own body: 2 functions -- the ADXM syscall user and sub_549C58's 0xBF80xxxx reads.
p3fes_handgen refuses 5 (mid-body entries): sub_53EF40, sub_54E7D8, sub_554138, sub_56DE28, sub_56F8F8.)

**How chosen.** The reached pure functions outside the driver layers are ACSS (80 of 138) and its public entry points (18
of 44); the next largest are SVM (20), ADXB's stream decoder (14, the rest stood in by test_cri2), the RSU descrambler (10)
and the Sofdec glue (13). ACSS was taken whole -- the 98 reached functions plus the 90 unreached ones of the same library
(accessors, AIX methods, the second player's paths), every one of them testable on the snapshots' live objects -- so the
library is complete in one slice; the three public thunks other tests stand in (0x54D100 / 0x54D148 / 0x54D220:
test_sweep1_sound, test_font2) stay recompiled. p3fes_handgen: 188 generated, 0 refused; 24 of the 188 call
27 still-recompiled functions through their `gen::` entry points (AIXP 15, ADXT's start-from-memory / volume / create
variant / AHX attach and detach 5, ADXT init / finish, SVM's server registration and test-and-set 3, the ADX error
reporter, libm pow).

**Readability** (reproducible: scratch `split.py` / `apply.py` / `spec.py` / `records.py` rewrite the generator's output):
five units by library part, a role comment with the proposal on every function (the same text in `libs2.h`), the seven
records of `namespace libs2` (fader 68, ADX back end 12, AIX back end 16, player record 12, sound 208, server 176,
ducking object 96 bytes; field comments from the instructions and the snapshots) as **370 named offsets** where one
register holds one record for the whole body (the argument register in a leaf that never writes it, or an s-register
whose only write is the copy of it before any call); `check_same.py` confirms the five units, comments dropped and the
constants replaced by their values, equal the generator's split output: **7,360 statements, 0 differ**.

**Findings** (each checked by a test on both bodies):
1. The fader's start (`sub_531B00`: fader, target, frames, delay, hold) computes the step from the *current* volume, so a
   fade started mid-fade continues from where it is; frames > 0 always passes through state 1 (the delay, even 0) and
   calls the start callback when the fade begins; frames <= 0 jumps to the target.
2. Curve 1 of the fader maps volume to level as 3238200 log10(-vol) / log10(960) -- louder as the volume falls; every
   live fader of the snapshots uses curve 0.
3. ADXT's status 0..7 maps through the table 0x7C0610 to 0 stop, 1 preparing (ADXT 1, 2), 2 playing (3 playing and 4
   decode end), 3 play end (5), 4 error (6, and 7 by the range check).
4. The work size (`valloc` 0x54D080) for an ADX configuration: per player an input buffer of channels x (rate / 1000) x
   25000 / 44 x (+0 + 1) bytes rounded to the *nearest* 2 KiB (not up), + 36, times +16, + 16576 x channels + 76, + 12,288
   with AHX, + 68 for the fader; doubled for two players; + 464. The game's BGM configuration (2 channels, 48 kHz) needs
   252,932 bytes and the voice one (1 channel, 24 kHz) less; a sound created in exactly that work succeeds, a 4 KiB one
   unwinds ("Specified work area size is too small") and frees its slot.
5. The game's settings (dorm snapshot): fade-out 30 frames, fade-in 1, volume change 15, cross offset 55, hold 10; ducking
   enabled, lowering 15 frames, restoring 180, depth 60 (6 dB; the reset value is 120). On battle_ref_6150 the ducking
   object is restoring; with no voice playing it reaches 0 dB and idle in 151 frames, its volume never falling.
6. The ADX back end answers the track-volume methods for track 0 only; the AIX back end's track-volume getter always
   returns 0 (the sound keeps the AIX track volumes itself, +192).

**Pair tests** (`tests/game/test_libs2.cpp`, 7 cases; stand-ins: AIXP, ADXT's own drivers -- PS2RNA, ADXSTM, ADXB, the list
streamer, the amplifier hooks --, the SVM callbacks, the ADX error reporters (texts kept), libm pow (the host's pow on the
soft-float registers), all recorders without scratch clobbering so the hgp runner compares the calls through the callees'

tables, the ADX status map through the live ADXT player, the back-end resets and accessor rules; the sound's start

Every function is paired on meaningful inputs.

## Phase 5 slice scene2: the leftovers of 0x3B0000-0x3CFFFF -- the SceneManager task, nmListSort, the message-window helpers and MsgAssist, psStatus, psModel, the fclBank bust-ups (46 functions, 2026-10-25)

**What.** `game/src/scene/scene2_{func,msg,fcl}.cpp` (`scene2.h`): 46 p3fes_handgen bodies (32,764 bytes) made readable -- a
role comment above every function (in the header too; 36 proposed names in brackets and in `symbols/deltas/scene2.sym`),
block-role comments at the branch points of the big bodies (40), the globals and record offsets as named constants
(`scene2::res / cam / eff / g / msgw / assist / req / sprslot / nml / nmnode / sprh / ps / psm / psfade / tween4 / mdlx /
bank / bankw / bankreq`, plus `scn::` from scene.h: 930 substitutions, each replacing only the literal it equals, applied
per function through a register -> record map by a script); a second script checks that, comments dropped and constants
replaced by their values, every body is token-identical to the generator's output (**46 functions, 0 differ**). By file:
* func (16): mt_sceneFunc.c's SceneManager -- the per-resource update `sub_3B9610` (5,208 B: every move / rotation / scale /
  alpha / fov-tween / queued-motion / footstep request), its task update `sub_3BCCB0` / destroy `sub_3BCD80` / draw
  `sub_3BD010`, the camera shake `sub_3BC940`, the scene camera (eye `sub_3BB620`, placement `sub_3BB7A0`), the
  depth-sorted effect draw `sub_3BCEB0` with its qsort comparator `sub_3BCDA0`, the path move request `sub_3B88C0`, the
  path point / heading at a distance `sub_3BC220`, the easing curve `sub_3BBED0`, the direction-angle helpers `sub_3B8540`
  / `sub_3BBB90`, the NPC icon wrapper `sub_3BB060`, a COMM handler `sub_3BD230`;
* msg (13): nmListSort `sub_3C4FC0`, the message-window slot helpers (open / release / show / update / clear, the
  current-slot step `sub_3C7990`, the handle table `sub_3C7DD0`), fclMisc.c's "MsgAssist" task and its sprite / request
  / icon helpers;
* fcl (17): fclMisc.c's "psStatus" screen (loader `sub_3C9FE0`, update / destroy, the sheet sprite `sub_3CA780`, the
  tabs and six layout callbacks), the persona-model preview (`sub_3CE2A0` / draw `sub_3CEA50`, the "psModel_dummy" task
  creator and update), fclBankManager.c's panel take `sub_3CF6C0` and update `fclBank_UpdateTask`.

**Records documented in the header (for the editor's Scene view / Inspector).** The scene resource record, extending
scene.h's `scn::res` (nothing renamed there): +80 the move kind (0 at a speed, 1 timed, 2 along the path), +81 the move
easing, +84 the path block (304 B: u8 count + 25 points), +92 / +96 the move time and frames (s32; f32 distance / length
for kind 2), +125 the rotation easing, +136 / +148 / +160 / +164 the scale tween, +168..+176 the footsteps (mode, index,
sound bank, timer, interval, delay), +196..+208 the float tween, +244 the pending steps, and the flag bits 0x20 / 0x40 /
0x400 / 0x2000 / 0x4000 / 0x8000; type 7 is the scene camera (+256 fov, +260 eye distance, +264 active, +268 the target
id); type 6's +256 draw pass; the camera shake globals (0x7CE658..0x7CE664, 0x7CD560 / 0x7CD564; scene.h's "reference
point" 0x95AFF0 / 0x95AFF4 is the shake offset); the 14-byte message-window slot; the MsgAssist work and requests; the
psStatus and psModel works; the fclBank panels.

**Findings.** (1) The type-7 fov tween (flag 0x400) interpolates with the move time +92 as its time base while its own
counter +208 only decides when it ends (pinned by a test: from 30 to 60 over 10 frames with +92 = 5 gives 45 on the
first frame). (2) The message-window open `sub_3C91B0` writes handle -1 before testing for an existing handle, so a
non-NULL slot always gets a new handle (an old one is dropped without itfMesMngDestroyHandle) and the "already open"
branch is dead. (3) The per-resource update steps once per frame only while flag bit 3 is clear (0 steps when set),
unless flag 0x20 hands it +244 steps for one frame; the speed move does not recompute the distance inside its step loop.
(4) The rotation's first frame only arms the time (+132 = the steps), nothing turns. (5) fclBankManager.c's "banks" are
the facility screens' three bust-up portrait slots: a panel's word is character << 16 | pose << 8 | expression and it is
handed to H_ChrDsp_Request (sub_106860; on the dorm machine it prints "!!! READ DISP2 1" and asks for bustup/*.bin);
END / KILL release it (H_ChrDsp_Release). (6) The path length the request prints for a straight 30-unit segment is
29.999989 (20 float chords); the unturned view direction of the camera eye (sub_3BB450) is +z.

## Phase 5: rendering -- RenderWare, ninth pass: the clump / atomic / geometry core and their streams, Rt2d scenes and the maestro, the image module and texture readers, the sky driver's formats and texture cache (render_rw9, 165 functions, 2026-10-25)

**What.** 165 functions (69,108 bytes) of the RW band in `game/src/render/render_rw9.cpp` /
`game/include/p3fes/game/render_rw9.h`, started from `p3fes_handgen` (0 refused) and made readable the way render_rw4..8
were: each function's role (proposed names in brackets, `symbols/deltas/render_rw9.sym`, 158 rows), and the record
offsets named (`rw9::atomic / geometry / matlist / image / raster`, beside `rw4::`..`rw8::`) where one base register holds
one record for the whole body; the scratch tool only adds comments and replaces literal load / store offsets by those
names for the base registers a per-function spec names, and checks that the code token stream with the names resolved
equals the generated body's (169,449 tokens, equal). Groups:
* **The clump / atomic / geometry core** (35): RpAtomicCreate (`sub_491880`), RpAtomicSetGeometry (`sub_4919B0`),
  RpAtomicClone (`sub_491B40`), RpClumpClone (`sub_491CC0`) and its per-atomic callback, RpGeometryCreate (`sub_493710`),
  RpGeometryDestroy (`sub_493B60`) and the free behind it, the clump / atomic / geometry-list / geometry stream readers
  (`sub_4920A0`, `sub_490DC0`, `sub_490980`, `sub_493CB0`), the material list's free and stream read, RpWorldStreamRead
  (`sub_490050`), RpWorldCreate / RpWorldDestroy, the clump-copy callback, the native-data plugin's list free and
  destructor; RpMatFX's material stream read, RpMatFXMaterialSetEffects and the dual-texture setters; PTank's atomic
  create / destroy, the GS packet field, instance layout, packet flush, the per-atomic set-up and the 2D / 3D sprite geometries.
* **Rt2d** (48): Rt2dOpen / Rt2dClose; the path layer (create, sList form, moveto, the module open, the stream readers);
  the shapes (the fill geometry, the shared representations' stream read / build / geometry / release, the shape's read
  and destroy); the scene (stream read, unlock, destroy, the per-type dispatch); the maestro (create / init / destroy,
  the animation / button / label / message lists and their readers, the keyframe interpolation and the props' commit,
  the per-animation update and rewind) -- the battle route runs them.
* **Engine helpers** (33): the dictionary schema init / destruct, RwFsInit and the RtFS file-record open / file system
  lookup / exists test, the memory module open / close with the newlib defaults (`j_malloc` / `j_realloc` / `j_calloc`),
  the default vector transforms and their set-up, the module 1042 open / close, the string helpers (upper / lower case,
  strchr / strrchr, the string chunk size and read), the absolute-path test, RwCameraRegisterPluginStream, the engine's
  core module registration, the frame root set-up.
* **The image module and the texture readers** (21): the module open, RwImageSetPath and the search-path walk, the format
  registry, RwImageRead / RwImageReadMaskedImage, RwImageSetGamma / RwImageGammaCorrect, the pixel copy, the 32-bit
  resample, the palettisers, the default texture readers, the raster mip-level fill, the named-texture search,
  RwTexDictionarySetCurrent.
* **The sky driver** (28): RpSkySelectDeepZBuffer, the option setters, the texture K / L stream read, the raster format
  rules, the texture mip-chain GS layout (`sub_4D9BC0`, 5,696 bytes), the sub-raster set-up, the mip-level count, the
  raster / texture native stream readers, SkySystem (the device-control entry) and its frame / scratch raster helpers, the
  standard-function table, the plugin attach, the raster format from an image, the palette upload in the GS CLUT layout,
  the palettised image copy, the upload-packet preparation, the texture cache's placement (`sub_4F02E0`, the most called:
  156,767 calls on the six routes) and reset.

recomp/generated of the gate tree, never committed; the next emission removed it), run on dorm, m1, battle, fusion and

**Findings.** (1) The hdd device's seek copies the position quadword to its result like the pak device (sweep1 finding 2);
an unknown whence sets the position to -1 without a seek. (2) `sub_10BF70` / `H_ResrcMan_MaybeResumeThread` enable
interrupts first (EIntr) and disable them again only when they were disabled -- the opposite bracket of the DIntr / EIntr
pairs elsewhere. (3) The resource-manager worker chains straight to the next request only when it is new and needs no
file; otherwise the per-frame pump issues its H_Cdvd load first. (4) H_Memcard_Check leaves the ok flag untouched for a
failed command other than 5 / 6 (only 5 / 6 clear it). (5) The light set-ups write through the kind-4 / kind-5 record
pointers without a null check on the stores (each pointer is 0 when the record is missing).

## Phase 5 slice libs4: the CRI middleware, third pass -- SVM's server table, ROFS's pure parts, the RSU CVM descrambler, the glue next to Sofdec (184 functions, 2026-10-28)

**What** (`game/src/cri/libs4_{svm,rofs,rsu,sofdec}.cpp`, `game/include/p3fes/game/libs4.h`, `tests/game/test_libs4.cpp`,
`tools/ours/types/deltas/libs4.json`; 184 functions, 24,140 bytes), under the relaxed callee rule. The CRI library's own
calls into ADXF / ROFS were allowed for this slice (packet `--allow adxf,rofs`). p3fes_handgen bodies made readable
without changing a statement: a role comment and a bracketed proposal per function (the binary's own texts where they name
it -- SVM's error texts, ROFS's "../../rofs_hn.c" texts, the version texts --, ours elsewhere; ADR-0009, not imported), the
globals and record offsets in `namespace libs4`. Worked from the binary only; no CRI SDK material.
- **SVM** (36, 0x564878-0x5656F0): the lock-type getter, the error helpers, the version text, the server table (8 server
  types x 6 slots of {function, object, name} at 0x999E20: register, unregister, set, execute one, execute a type), the
  per-type execution counters and flags, init / finish, the callback setters and the test-and-set.
- **ROFS** (65, 0x5658A8-0x56CA78 and 0x56DD50-0x56DDF8): the file handle (fill, create, reopen, seek, tell, status,
  transfer counts), the volume record, the error reporter and last error, the work-area flags, the ISO 9660 record copiers
  (driven by the 40-word field table at 0x7B2710), the CVM header parsers (CVMH, CVMF, ZONE), the PFS lock / wait helpers,
  ROCI's interface getters.
- **RSU** (36, 0x56CDF0-0x56DCE8): the CVM descrambler -- the three prime hashes, the fixed keys (from a CVM header or a
  password), the per-sector round keys, the permutation rounds, the decipher entry points.
- **Glue next to Sofdec** (47, 0x56DEC0-0x56FEC0): CFT's work pointer and its 8-bit to 32-bit converter, the newlib lock
  stubs, the 64-bit multiply compare, the callback thunks of 0x7B292C-0x7B2978, the reader methods of 0x56F888-0x56FEC0.
- Types: seven records in `deltas/libs4.json` -- RofsHandle (60 bytes), RofsVolume (52), RofsDirHandle (72), CvmInfo
  (1904), CvmZoneInfo (44), RofsWork, SfdReader.

**How chosen.** The `libs4` packet (main 35040ad): reach from the saved first-call probes (81 files), then caller count;
callees from the handgen bodies. 0 exclusions. The slice was paused with every body written; this pass merged main
b97a80e (no row of the slice is on main, none dropped) and wrote the docs.

**Tests** (`tests/game/test_libs4.cpp`, 8 cases; MSVC and clang-cl each 8 / 8 cases, 76,759 / 76,759 assertions): every
body against its `__recomp` on random worlds (4,416 pairs, 1,088 stopped early identically) and on the snapshots' live SVM
table, ROFS work area and handles (`dorm_replay_4900`, `b_5800`, `climb_ref_17000`); directed worlds for SVM, the ROFS
handles / seek rules / error text / work flags, the disc's CVM headers (BGM / BTL / DATA.CVM: CVMH + ZONE parsed and
checked against the bytes, a CVMF header, bad magics refused), the ISO 9660 volume descriptor and root record, RSU
(decipher twice = identity), the Sofdec glue -- 3,165 pairs over the 184 functions in all on the snapshot and directed
worlds. The CRI drivers are recorders and the callback targets stand-ins inside the test only. Skips cleanly without game
data.

**Findings** (each checked by a test on both bodies).
1. The boot movie: on the dorm route MWSFD plays its one movie from vblank ~840 to ~890 (then the replay input skips
   it); at vblank 860 player #0 (0x7B2FBC) is playing (status 2) with SFD handle 0x018C3EA0 -- the slice's snapshot
   `extracted/_ours/libs5_movie_860` (gitignored, made with the gate tree's `p3fes.exe`, dorm route `--snapshot-at
   vblank:860`). The dorm snapshot at 4900 has MWSFD initialised and no player.
2. mwPlyGetStat follows SFD's status only while the player is playing: SFD 4 and 6 give 2 (playing), a negative SFD
   status (after an error) 4, every other value 1 (preparing); other player states are returned as stored; a bad
   handle records last error -12 (MWSFD work +104) and gives 0.
3. The file-name copy (mwPlyStartFname's helper) truncates a name longer than the buffer with strncpy and leaves it
   unterminated (after reporting "E211121: filename is longer.").
4. SFX's work must be at least 6,175 bytes and MWSFD asks for exactly that (sub_5827F0); the layout rounds the work up
   to 32 bytes before carving three 1 KiB areas.
5. The SFD statistics record starts with minimum INT64_MAX but maximum 0, so a run of negative samples keeps the
   maximum at 0.
6. sub_599E48 divides by a figure of sub_599D70 and keeps the compiler's divide-by-zero trap (`break 7`); the body
   carries it as generated.

  mwPlyGetHdrInf, the handle-checked getters, init (the CRI layers, SFD, the server threads), the SFD error handler.

**How chosen.** The census above, then the continue packet `lead/packets/libs3` (main 35040ad2: 252 rows done,
0 remaining, 0 excluded, no row dropped by `sync`; the CRI library's own ADXF / ROFS calls allowed).

**How.** p3fes_handgen bodies (271 of the 275 candidates generate; the final list of 252 with 0 refused), split by
library into eight files, then a scripted readability pass (`annot.py`, the role data in `annot_data.py` /
`annot_cri_*.py` / `annot_subs.py`): a role per function written from the instructions and the pseudocode reference,
a [proposed name] for every sub_ and FLIRT false match (mwPly* names only where CRI's own error strings name the
function -- mwPlyCreate, mwPlyGetHdrInf, mwPlyGetFrmSync, mwPlyGetFrm --, descriptive mwsfd* / mpv* / mps* / m2v*
names otherwise), block comments where a constant decides the path (qsort's swap type and thresholds, _malloc_r's
request rounding), and 217 uses of named offsets (`libs3::reent / glue / file / m2v / mps / mpv / mwsfd`,
`libc::reent / file / bigint`, `tail1::mps / mpv / mwsfd`). A normaliser (comments stripped, every named constant
swapped for its value, hex and decimal compared by value) proves **all 252 bodies token-equal to the generated ones**.

**Findings** (checked by the tests). (1) `_getpid_r`, `_execve_r` and `_fork_r` are FLIRT
false matches: their bodies are newlib's vectored write (__sfvwrite: unbuffered, line-buffered with memchr, fully
buffered with the string-FILE case), _lseek_r (the errno word 0x9ACC20) and __smakebuf (fstat through `_kill_r`, the
1,024-byte block, flags 0x80 / 0x400 / 0x800). (2) scanf's `%c` reads through fread (0x51FAA0), not the buffer; fread
is not emitted in the test build, so `%c` pairs stop there identically and the meaningful cases avoid it. (3)
_multadd multiplies in 16-bit halves: exact for m, a < 2^16 (dtoa's 10 and 5^k), wrong beyond -- the tests keep to the
contract. (4) _pow5mult keeps its 5^(4 * 2^k) chain in the _reent (+72) across calls; a test that recycles Bigint blocks
must clear it (a stale chain sent strtod into a runaway loop until the tests cleared it). (5) strtod returns the host's
correctly rounded double for every normal input of the test (173 of 173, 19-digit mantissas, exponents -40..40), the
truncating soft-float library notwithstanding (the Bigint correction loop); strtodf is within one ulp (dptofp
truncates). (6) __ieee754_pow is within one ulp of the host on 313 cases. (7) qsort swaps 64-bit doublewords
(alignment and size multiples of 8; a single doubleword for size 8) -- long is 64-bit in this build. (8) _malloc_r's
chunk size is (size + 19) & ~15, at least 16; on the b_5800 snapshot's live arena all nine test sizes, and their
reallocations, run to the end. (9) MPS's PES reader takes the packet length as 16 bits only when the handle's mode word (+16) is 2,
which sub_577E68 sets; with it the bytes the demultiplexer reports used equal a host walk of ISO/IEC 11172-1 for the
first 12 packs of each of the 41 movies (492 packs; 82 with a system header; padding 0xBE and private_stream_2 0xBF
end after the length). (10) M2V's MPEG-2 probe agrees with a host check of the sequence_extension on all 41
movies (3 MPEG-2, the count tail1 found by name); MPV's header decoder, run over a memory stream joint on the other 38 movies' video,
stores the sequence header's horizontal / vertical size at +464 / +468. (11) MPV's 7,136-byte shared area starts one
1,056-byte record past the n handles (0x99B30C holds base + n * 1,056, 0x99B310 base + (n + 1) * 1,056).
(12) sub_57C270 (the "already a pack" test of the descrambler) reads its second argument; the descrambler sub_57C188
is an involution (applied twice the block comes back).

**Tests** (tests/game/test_libs3.cpp, 12 cases): the generic sweep (32 random worlds per function, 8,064 pairs, 4,592 stopped
identically -- mostly at callees this test build does not emit); sscanf / _sscanf_r on 19 formats against the host's
sscanf (bases, widths, scansets, %n, %*, floats through strtod) and 40 random three-base round trips (78 pairs);
sprintf_r / vsprintf_r on 10 formats x 6 argument sets against snprintf (120 pairs); ungetc / __srefill on string
FILEs, _fwalk over a two-block glue list with strlen as the callback, lflush's flag test (16 pairs); strtod / strtodf
/ _strtod_r on 179 inputs (234 pairs); _i2b, _multiply, _lshift, __mdiff, _multadd, _pow5mult, _s2b, _d2b against host
bignums (290 pairs); qsort with strcmp on 72 arrays of the three swap types (72 pairs); __ieee754_pow on 313 cases and
__ieee754_rem_pio2 on 120 (433 pairs); _malloc_r / _realloc_r on the b_5800 arena (27 pairs); MPS start-code classes
of all 256 codes, the byte search against a host search, the demultiplexer on 492 real packs (562 pairs); the MPEG-2
probe and the MPV header decoder on the 41 movies' video (79 pairs); CRI muldiv / rounded muldiv against host 64-bit
arithmetic, the clip table, the M2V / MPV pools, MWSFD's work allocator on user work and on malloc callbacks, the
code mappers against their rules, the key table and the descrambler, the MPS getters (287 pairs). Fixed fields
throughout use the real records (sscanf's FILE, the _reent at _impure_ptr, the handles' init values). MSVC 14.44 Release (`build\libs3-gate`, on main b97a80e
merged): 12 cases / 109,471 assertions, all passed; clang-cl (`slice.ps1 clang`, same merge): 12 cases / 109,471 assertions,
